Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

96. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo [T 3.0046] – sahetukā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

96. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of root condition—the rooted roots are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – sahetukā hetū cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of root condition—the rooted roots are a condition for mind-originated matter by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (2)

Sahetuko [M 3.0039][V 3.0047] dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – sahetukā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon and for a rootless phenomenon by way of root condition—the rooted roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (3)

97. Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

97. A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of root condition—delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of root condition—delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon and for a rootless phenomenon by way of root condition—delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

98. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ paccavekkhati. Ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti. Pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe…pe… sahetuke [T 3.0047] khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; cetopariyañāṇena sahetukacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānanti. Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… sahetukā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; sahetuke khandhe ārabbha sahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

98. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of object condition—having given a gift, observed the precepts… and so on… having performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects upon it; one reflects upon past good deeds; having emerged from jhāna, one reflects upon the jhāna. Noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect upon the path; they reflect upon the fruit. They reflect on abandoned defilements… and so on… on suppressed defilements… and so on… on past… and so on… When one regards the rooted aggregates as impermanent… and so on… grief arises. When wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rooted resultant consciousness arises taking that as its object. With the knowledge of others’ minds, they know the mind of one endowed with a rooted mind. The base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness… and so on… the base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… and so on… rooted aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of others’ minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, and the knowledge of the future, by way of object condition. Taking rooted aggregates as object, rooted aggregates arise. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – sahetuke khandhe aniccato [V 3.0048] …pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, kusalākusale niruddhe ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, sahetuke khandhe ārabbha ahetukā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (2)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of object condition—when one regards the rooted aggregates as impermanent… and so on… grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rootless resultant consciousness arises taking that as its object; taking the rooted aggregates as object, rootless aggregates and delusion arise. (2)

Sahetuko [M 3.0040] dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – sahetuke khandhe ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (3)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon and a rootless phenomenon by way of object condition—taking the rooted aggregates as object, aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, arise. (3)

99. Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nibbānaṃ āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… ahetuke khandhe ca mohañca aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… ahetuke khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha ahetukā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti[T 3.0048]. (1)

99. A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of object condition—Nibbāna is a condition for adverting by way of object condition; the eye… and so on… the physical basis… when one regards the rootless aggregates and delusion as impermanent… and so on… grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rootless resultant consciousness arises taking that as its object; the form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… and so on… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness… and so on… taking the rootless aggregates and delusion as object, rootless aggregates and delusion arise. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ariyā ahetuke pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ…pe… ahetuke khandhe ca mohañca aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, cetopariyañāṇena ahetukacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānanti; ahetukā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ahetuke khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha sahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of object condition—noble ones reflect on Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, purification, path, and fruit by way of object condition. Noble ones reflect on abandoned rootless defilements, on suppressed defilements… and so on… on past… and so on… the eye… and so on… the physical basis… and so on… when one regards the rootless aggregates and delusion as impermanent… and so on… grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rooted resultant consciousness arises by taking that as its object; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds, with the knowledge of others’ minds they know the mind of one endowed with a rootless mind; the rootless aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of others’ minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of the future, by way of object condition; taking the rootless aggregates and delusion as object, rooted aggregates arise. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cakkhuṃ ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti; sotaṃ [V 3.0049] …pe… vatthuṃ… ahetuke khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (3)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon and a rootless phenomenon by way of object condition—taking the eye as object, aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, arise; taking the ear… and so on… the physical basis… taking the rootless aggregates and delusion as object, aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, arise. (3)

100. Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha sahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

100. A rooted phenomenon and a rootless phenomenon are a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of object condition—taking the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, as object, rooted aggregates arise. (1)

Sahetuko [M 3.0041] ca ahetuko ca dhammā ahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha ahetukā khandhā [T 3.0049] ca moho ca uppajjanti. (2)

A rooted phenomenon and a rootless phenomenon are a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of object condition—taking the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, as object, rootless aggregates and delusion arise. (2)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (3)

A rooted phenomenon and a rootless phenomenon are a condition for a rooted phenomenon and a rootless phenomenon by way of object condition—taking the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, as object, aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, arise. (3)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

101. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… phalaṃ…pe… sahetuke khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – sahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

101. A rooted state is a condition for a rooted state by way of dominance condition—object-dominance, conascence-dominance. Object-dominance: Having given a gift, kept the precepts,… having performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews that, regarding it as weighty; having arisen from the jhānas,… noble ones having arisen from the paths, one reviews the path, regarding it as weighty… the fruit… one relishes and welcomes the rooted aggregates, regarding them as weighty; making that weighty, lust arises, wrong view arises. Conascence-dominance: A rooted dominant state is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – sahetukādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rooted state is a condition for a rootless state by way of dominance condition. Conascence-dominance: A rooted dominant state is a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dominance condition. (2)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati [V 3.0050] – sahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rooted state is a condition for a rooted state and a rootless state by way of dominance condition. Conascence-dominance: A rooted dominant state is a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of dominance condition. (3)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… ahetuke khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ [T 3.0050] garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1)

A rootless state is a condition for a rooted state by way of dominance condition. Object-dominance: The noble ones review Nibbāna, regarding it as weighty; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, purification, path, and fruition by way of dominance condition; the eye… the base… one relishes and welcomes the rootless aggregates, regarding them as weighty; making that weighty, lust arises, wrong view arises. (1)

Anantarapaccayo

Proximity Condition

102. Sahetuko [M 3.0042] dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā sahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa… maggo phalassa… phalaṃ phalassa… anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

102. A rooted state is a condition for a rooted state by way of proximity condition—preceding rooted aggregates are a condition for succeeding rooted aggregates by way of proximity condition; conformity for change-of-lineage… conformity for purification… change-of-lineage for the path… purification for the path… the path for the fruit… the fruit for the fruit… conformity for fruition-attainment… for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither perception nor non-perception is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of proximity condition. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā pacchimassa pacchimassa vicikicchāsahagatassa uddhaccasahagatassa mohassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; sahetukaṃ cuticittaṃ ahetukassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; sahetukaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāya anantarapaccayena paccayo; sahetukaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ ahetukassa bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; sahetukā khandhā ahetukassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rooted state is a condition for a rootless state by way of proximity condition—preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness are a condition for succeeding delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness by way of proximity condition; a rooted death consciousness is a condition for a rootless rebirth consciousness by way of proximity condition; a rooted life-continuum is a condition for adverting by way of proximity condition; a rooted life-continuum is a condition for a rootless life-continuum by way of proximity condition; rooted aggregates are a condition for rootless emergence by way of proximity condition. (2)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rooted state is a condition for a rooted state and a rootless state by way of proximity condition—preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness are a condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness and for delusion by way of proximity condition. (3)

103. Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo [V 3.0051] vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho pacchimassa [T 3.0051] pacchimassa vicikicchāsahagatassa uddhaccasahagatassa mohassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; purimā purimā ahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ ahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

103. A rootless state is a condition for a rootless state by way of immediate condition—preceding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied delusion is a condition for succeeding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied delusion by way of immediate condition; preceding rootless aggregates are conditions for succeeding rootless aggregates by way of immediate condition; adverting is a condition for the five consciousnesses by way of immediate condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo[M 3.0043]; ahetukaṃ cuticittaṃ sahetukassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; ahetukaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ sahetukassa bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; ahetukā khandhā sahetukassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless state is a condition for a rooted state by way of immediate condition—preceding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied delusion is a condition for succeeding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates by way of immediate condition; a rootless death consciousness is a condition for a rooted rebirth consciousness by way of immediate condition; a rootless life-continuum is a condition for a rooted life-continuum by way of immediate condition; adverting is a condition for rooted aggregates by way of immediate condition; rootless aggregates are conditions for rooted emergence by way of immediate condition. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rootless state is a condition for a rooted state and a rootless state by way of immediate condition—preceding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied delusion is a condition for succeeding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates and for delusion by way of immediate condition; adverting is a condition for doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates and for delusion by way of immediate condition. (3)

104. Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena [T 3.0052] paccayo. (1)

104. Both rooted and rootless states are conditions for a rooted state by way of immediate condition—preceding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates and delusion are conditions for succeeding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates by way of immediate condition. (1)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā ahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca pacchimassa pacchimassa vicikicchāsahagatassa uddhaccasahagatassa mohassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca ahetukassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Both rooted and rootless states are conditions for a rootless state by way of immediate condition—preceding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates and delusion are conditions for succeeding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied delusion by way of immediate condition; doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates and delusion are conditions for rootless emergence by way of immediate condition. (2)

Sahetuko [V 3.0052] ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Both rooted and rootless states are conditions for both rooted and rootless states by way of immediate condition—preceding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates and delusion are conditions for succeeding doubt-accompanied and agitation-accompanied aggregates and for delusion by way of immediate condition. (3)

Sahajātapaccayādi

Co-nascence Condition, etc.

105. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccavāre sahajātasadisaṃ, iha ghaṭanā natthi)… aññamaññapaccayena [M 3.0044] paccayo (paṭiccavārasadisaṃ)… nissayapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccavāre nissayapaccayasadisaṃ, iha ghaṭanā natthi).

105. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of the co-nascence condition (similar to co-nascence in the Conditional Relations; here there is no occurrence); by way of the mutuality condition (similar to the Conditional Relations); by way of the dependence condition (similar to the dependence condition in the Conditional Relations; here there is no occurrence).

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

106. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – sahetukā khandhā sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

106. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: Rooted aggregates are a condition for rooted aggregates by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – sahetukā khandhā ahetukānaṃ [T 3.0053] khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: Rooted aggregates are a condition for rootless aggregates and for delusion by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – sahetukā khandhā vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for both a rooted and a rootless phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: Rooted aggregates are a condition for the aggregates associated with doubt and agitation, and for delusion, by way of the decisive support condition. (3)

107. Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo; kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utu… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena [V 3.0053] paccayo; moho kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo; kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utu… bhojanaṃ, senāsanaṃ, moho ca kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

107. A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: Bodily pleasure is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and delusion by way of the decisive support condition; bodily pain, climate, food, lodging are conditions for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and delusion by way of the decisive support condition; delusion is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and delusion by way of the decisive support condition; bodily pleasure, bodily pain, climate, food, lodging, and delusion are conditions for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and delusion by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ… mohaṃ upanissāya [M 3.0045] dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… moho ca saddhāya…pe… paññāya rāgassa…pe… patthanāya maggassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: Relying on bodily pleasure, one gives alms, etc., or splits the Sangha; relying on bodily pain, climate, food, lodging, or delusion, one gives alms, etc., or splits the Sangha; bodily pleasure, etc., and delusion are a condition for faith, etc., for wisdom, for lust, etc., for aspiration, for the path, and for fruition attainment by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa [T 3.0054] ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ moho ca vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for both a rooted and a rootless phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: Bodily pleasure and delusion are a condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt, for the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and for delusion, by way of the decisive support condition. (3)

108. Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

108. Both rooted and rootless phenomena are a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: The aggregates accompanied by doubt, the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for rooted aggregates by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā ahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca ahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Both rooted and rootless phenomena are a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition: contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: The aggregates accompanied by doubt, the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for rootless aggregates and for delusion by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – vicikicchāsahagatā [V 3.0054] uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Both rooted and rootless phenomena are a condition for both rooted and rootless phenomena by way of the decisive support condition: contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support: The aggregates accompanied by doubt, the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt, for the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and for delusion, by way of the decisive support condition. (3)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

109. Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, kusalākusale niruddhe ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa [T 3.0055] …pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo[M 3.0046]. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… purejātaṃ vatthu ahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

109. A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of the pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: The eye…pe…the base as impermanent…pe…sorrow arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rootless resultant arises with that as its object; the visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe…the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of the pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: The eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe…the body base is a condition for body-consciousness…the pre-nascent base is a condition for the rootless aggregates and for delusion by way of the pre-nascence condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of the pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: The eye…pe…the base as impermanent…pe…sorrow arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rooted resultant arises with that as its object; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear element one hears sounds. Base pre-nascence: The base is a condition for the rooted aggregates by way of the pre-nascence condition. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for both rooted and rootless phenomena by way of the pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: The eye…pe…taking the base as object, the aggregates accompanied by doubt, the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion arise. Base pre-nascence: The base is a condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt, for the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and for delusion, by way of the pre-nascence condition. (3)

Pacchājātapaccayādi

Post-nascence Condition, etc.

110. Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā sahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

110. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of the post-nascence condition. The post-nascent rooted aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of the post-nascence condition. (1)

Ahetuko [V 3.0055] dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā ahetukā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of the post-nascence condition. The post-nascent rootless aggregates and delusion are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of the post-nascence condition. (1)

Sahetuko [T 3.0056] ca ahetuko ca dhammā ahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

Both rooted and rootless phenomena are a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of the post-nascence condition—the post-nascent aggregates accompanied by doubt, the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of the post-nascence condition. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo (anantarasadisaṃ. Āvajjanampi bhavaṅgampi natthi, āsevanapaccaye vajjetabbā navapi ).

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of the repetition condition (similar to the contiguity condition. Neither adverting nor life-continuum is present; nine are to be excluded in the repetition condition).

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

111. Sahetuko [M 3.0047] dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – sahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – sahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

111. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of the kamma condition—simultaneously arisen and occurring at different moments. Simultaneously arisen: Rooted volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. Occurring at different moments: Rooted volition is a condition for the resultant rooted aggregates by way of the kamma condition. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – sahetukā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – sahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ ahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of kamma condition—co-nascent and at different moments. Co-nascent: rooted volition is a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, etc. At different moments: rooted volition is a condition for the rootless resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of kamma condition. (2)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – sahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – sahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena [T 3.0057] paccayo. (3)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon and for a rootless phenomenon by way of kamma condition—co-nascent and at different moments. Co-nascent: rooted volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. At different moments: rooted volition is a condition for the rooted resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of kamma condition. (3)

Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – ahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ [V 3.0056] khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of kamma condition—rootless volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, etc. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Resultant Condition

112. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko sahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

112. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of resultant condition—one rooted resultant aggregate is a condition for three aggregates... etc.; two aggregates... etc.; at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipākā sahetukā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of resultant condition—the rooted resultant aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of resultant condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc. (2)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko sahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon and for a rootless phenomenon by way of resultant condition—one rooted resultant aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality... etc.; two aggregates... etc.; at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc. (3)

Ahetuko [M 3.0048] dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko ahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa vipākapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of resultant condition—one rootless resultant aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality... etc.; two aggregates... etc.; at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc.; the aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of resultant condition. (1)

Āhārapaccayo

Nutriment Condition

113. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

113. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of nutriment condition... three.

Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – ahetukā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of nutriment condition—rootless nutriments are a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality... etc.; at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc.; edible food is a condition for this body by way of nutriment condition. (1)

Indriyapaccayādi

Faculty Condition, etc.

114. Sahetuko [T 3.0058][V 3.0057] dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

114. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of faculty condition... three.

Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – ahetukā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa indriyapaccayena paccayo; rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of faculty condition—rootless faculties are a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality... etc.; at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc.; the eye-faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness... etc.; the body-faculty is a condition for body-consciousness by way of faculty condition; the material life-faculty is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of faculty condition. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of jhāna condition... three.

Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo – ahetukāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of jhāna condition—the rootless jhāna factors are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality... etc.; at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa maggapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of path condition... three.

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccavāre sampayuttasadisā cha pañhā).

A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of association condition. (In the Dependent section, there are six questions similar to association.)

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

115. Sahetuko [M 3.0049] dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – sahetukā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe sahetukā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – sahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena [T 3.0059] paccayo. (1)

115. A rooted phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent and post-nascent. Co-nascent: the rooted aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, the rooted aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: the rooted aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – ahetukā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe ahetukā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena [V 3.0058] paccayo; vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu ahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – ahetukā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent, pre-nascent, and post-nascent. Co-nascent: the rootless aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, the rootless aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of dissociation condition; the aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of dissociation condition; the physical base is a condition for the aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness... etc.; the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness... the physical base is a condition for the rootless aggregates and for delusion by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: the rootless aggregates and delusion are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for a rooted phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent and pre-nascent. Co-nascent: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition for the rooted aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: the physical base is a condition for the rooted aggregates by way of dissociation condition. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rootless phenomenon is a condition for rooted and rootless phenomena by way of dissociation-condition. By way of pre-nascence—the physical base is a condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and for delusion, by way of dissociation-condition. (3)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā ahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho [T 3.0060] ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

Rooted and rootless phenomena are a condition for a rootless phenomenon by way of dissociation-condition—by way of co-nascence and post-nascence. By way of co-nascence—the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation-condition. By way of post-nascence—the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation-condition. (1)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

116. Sahetuko [M 3.0050] dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

116. A rooted state is a condition for a rooted state by presence condition—one rooted aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates…etc.… two aggregates…etc.… at the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (1)

Sahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – sahetukā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā mohassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – sahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rooted state is a condition for a rootless state by presence condition—by way of co-nascence and post-nascence. By way of co-nascence: Rooted aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by presence condition; aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness are a condition for delusion and for mind-originated materiality by presence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. By way of post-nascence: Rooted aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen body by presence condition. (2)

Sahetuko [V 3.0059] dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe sahetuko…pe…. (3)

A rooted state is a condition for rooted and rootless states by presence condition—one rooted aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by presence condition; one aggregate accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition for the three aggregates, for delusion, and for mind-originated materiality by presence condition…etc.… two aggregates…etc.… at the moment of rebirth-linking, a rooted state…etc. (3)

117. Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – ahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā kātabbaṃ). Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ [T 3.0061] aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, kusalākusale niruddhe ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo; vatthu ahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – ahetukā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; kabaḷīkāro āhāro [M 3.0051] imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

117. A rootless state is a condition for a rootless state by presence condition—by way of co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. By way of co-nascence: One rootless aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by presence condition…etc.… two aggregates…etc.… delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition for mind-originated materiality by presence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (to be done up to the non-percipient beings). By way of pre-nascence: The eye…etc.… the base… when impermanence is contemplated…etc.… distress arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rootless resultant arises taking them as object; the visual object is a condition for eye-consciousness…etc.… the tangible object is a condition for body-consciousness…etc.… the eye faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness…etc.… the body faculty is a condition for body-consciousness by presence condition; the base is a condition for the rootless aggregates and for delusion by presence condition. By way of post-nascence: The rootless aggregates and delusion are a condition for this previously arisen body by presence condition; edible food is a condition for this body by presence condition; the material life faculty is a condition for materiality produced by kamma by presence condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, vatthu sahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless state is a condition for a rooted state by presence condition—by way of co-nascence and pre-nascence. By way of co-nascence: Delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition for the associated aggregates by presence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, the base is a condition for the rooted aggregates by presence condition. By way of pre-nascence: The eye…etc.… the base… when impermanence is contemplated…etc.… distress arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rooted resultant arises taking them as object; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds; the base is a condition for the rooted aggregates by presence condition. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ [V 3.0060] cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā [T 3.0062] ca moho ca uppajjanti, vatthu vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rootless state is a condition for rooted and rootless states by presence condition—by way of co-nascence and pre-nascence. By way of co-nascence: Delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by presence condition. By way of pre-nascence: The eye…etc.… taking the base as object, aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness and delusion arise; the base is a condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness and for delusion by presence condition. (3)

118. Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato eko khandho ca moho ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe sahetuko eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. Sahajāto – sahetuko eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. (1)

118. Rooted and rootless states are a condition for a rooted state by presence condition—by way of co-nascence and pre-nascence. By way of co-nascence: One aggregate accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for the three aggregates by presence condition…etc.… two aggregates…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking, one rooted aggregate and the base are a condition for the three aggregates by presence condition…etc.… two aggregates…etc. One rooted aggregate and the base are a condition for the three aggregates by presence condition…etc.… two aggregates…etc. (1)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā ahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – sahetukā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe sahetukā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena [M 3.0052] paccayo. Sahajātā – vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca vatthu ca mohassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – vicikicchāsahagatā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – sahetukā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – sahetukā [T 3.0063] khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

Rooted states and rootless states are a condition for rootless states by presence condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. Co-nascence: Rooted aggregates and great elements are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by presence condition; doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied aggregates and delusion are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by presence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, rooted aggregates and great elements are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by presence condition. Co-nascence: Doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied aggregates and the base are a condition for delusion by presence condition. Post-nascence: Doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied aggregates and delusion are a condition for this previously arisen body by presence condition. Post-nascence: Rooted aggregates and edible food are a condition for this body by presence condition. Post-nascence: Rooted aggregates and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by presence condition. (2)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato eko khandho ca moho ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe…. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. (3)

Rooted states and rootless states are a condition for rooted states and rootless states by presence condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence. Co-nascence: One doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied aggregate and delusion are a condition for the three aggregates and mind-produced material phenomena by presence condition…and so on. Co-nascence: One doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied aggregate and the base are a condition for the three aggregates and delusion by presence condition…and so on… two aggregates…and so on. (3)

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Direct Method of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Chapter on Enumeration

Suddhaṃ

Pure

119. Hetuyā [V 3.0061] cha, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā cattāri, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe cha, nissaye nava, upanissaye nava, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane nava, kamme cattāri, vipāke cattāri, āhāre cattāri, indriye cattāri, jhāne cattāri, magge tīṇi, sampayutte cha, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā nava, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate nava (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

119. By way of root condition, six; by way of object condition, nine; by way of predominance condition, four; by way of contiguity condition, nine; by way of immediate contiguity condition, nine; by way of co-nascence condition, nine; by way of mutuality condition, six; by way of support condition, nine; by way of decisive support condition, nine; by way of pre-nascence condition, three; by way of post-nascence condition, three; by way of repetition condition, nine; by way of kamma condition, four; by way of result condition, four; by way of nutriment condition, four; by way of faculty condition, four; by way of jhāna condition, four; by way of path condition, three; by way of association condition, six; by way of dissociation condition, five; by way of presence condition, nine; by way of absence condition, nine; by way of disappearance condition, nine; by way of non-disappearance condition, nine (thus it should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

The Direct Method.

120. Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

120. A root-conditioned state is a condition for a root-conditioned state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of kamma condition. (1)

Sahetuko [M 3.0053] dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena [T 3.0064] paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A root-conditioned state is a condition for a rootless state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of kamma condition. (2)

Sahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A root-conditioned state is a condition for root-conditioned states and rootless states by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of kamma condition. (3)

121. Ahetuko dhammo ahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena [V 3.0062] paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

121. A rootless state is a condition for a rootless state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of nutriment condition... by way of faculty condition. (1)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless state is a condition for a root-conditioned state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Ahetuko dhammo sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rootless state is a condition for root-conditioned states and rootless states by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition. (3)

122. Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

122. Root-conditioned and rootless states are a condition for a root-conditioned state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā ahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Root-conditioned and rootless states are a condition for a rootless state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of post-nascence condition. (2)

Sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā sahetukassa ca ahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Root-conditioned and rootless states are a condition for root-conditioned states and rootless states by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition. (3)

126. Hetusampayuttaṃ [T 3.0066][M 3.0055][V 3.0064] dhammaṃ paṭicca hetusampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – hetusampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

126. A phenomenon associated with roots arises dependent on a phenomenon associated with roots, by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate associated with roots, three aggregates arise… dependent on two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (1)

Hetusampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetuvippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – hetusampayutte khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from roots arises dependent on a phenomenon associated with roots, by way of root condition—dependent on the aggregates associated with roots, mind-produced material form arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking… (2)

(Iminā kāraṇena vitthāretabbaṃ yathā sahetukadukaṃ ninnānākaraṇaṃ.)

(For this reason, it should be elaborated in detail, just as the Root-Conditioned Dyad, which is without variation.)

Hetusampayuttadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Phenomena Associated with Roots is concluded.

127. Hetuñceva [V 3.0065] sahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – alobhaṃ paṭicca adoso amoho (cakkaṃ). Lobhaṃ paṭicca moho (cakkaṃ); paṭisandhikkhaṇe alobhaṃ paṭicca adoso amoho (cakkaṃ). (1)

127. Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted, a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted arises by way of root condition—dependent on non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion arise (a cycle); dependent on greed, delusion arises (a cycle); at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion arise (a cycle). (1)

Hetuñceva sahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – hetuṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted, a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root arises by way of root condition—dependent on a root, the associated aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking… (2)

Hetuñceva sahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko [T 3.0067] ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – alobhaṃ paṭicca adoso amoho sampayuttakā ca khandhā (cakkaṃ). Lobhaṃ paṭicca moho sampayuttakā ca khandhā (cakkaṃ); paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted, phenomena that are both a root and rooted, and phenomena that are rooted but not a root, arise by way of root condition—dependent on non-greed, there arise non-hatred, non-delusion, and the associated aggregates (a cycle); dependent on greed, there arise delusion and the associated aggregates (a cycle); at the moment of rebirth-linking… (3)

128. Sahetukañceva [M 3.0056] na ca hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati [V 3.0066] hetupaccayā – sahetukañceva na ca hetuṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe….(1)

128. Dependent on a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root arises by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate that is rooted but not a root, three aggregates arise… two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (1)

Sahetukañceva na ca hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – sahetuke ceva na ca hetū khandhe paṭicca hetū; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted arises by way of root condition—dependent on aggregates that are rooted but not roots, the roots arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking… (2)

Sahetukañceva na ca hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – sahetukañceva na ca hetuṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā hetu ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, phenomena that are both a root and rooted, and phenomena that are rooted but not a root, arise by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate that is rooted but not a root, three aggregates and the roots arise… two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (3)

129. Hetuñceva sahetukañca sahetukañceva na ca hetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – alobhañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca adoso amoho (cakkaṃ). Lobhañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca moho (cakkaṃ); paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

129. Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted and a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted arises by way of root condition—dependent on non-greed and the associated aggregates, non-hatred and non-delusion arise (a cycle); dependent on greed and the associated aggregates, delusion arises (a cycle); at the moment of rebirth-linking… (1)

Hetuñceva sahetukañca sahetukañceva na ca hetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – sahetukañceva na ca hetuṃ ekaṃ khandhañca hetuñca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted and a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root arises by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate that is rooted but not a root and a root, three aggregates arise… two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (2)

Hetuñceva sahetukañca sahetukañceva na ca hetuñca dhammaṃ [T 3.0068] paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – sahetukañceva na ca hetuṃ ekaṃ khandhañca alobhañca paṭicca tayo khandhā adoso amoho ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted and a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, phenomena that are both a root and rooted, and phenomena that are rooted but not a root, arise by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate that is rooted but not a root and non-greed, there arise three aggregates, non-hatred, and non-delusion… two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (3)

(Saṃkhittaṃ. Evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

131. Hetuñceva [M 3.0057][V 3.0067] sahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – alobhaṃ paṭicca adoso amoho (cakkaṃ); paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (paripuṇṇaṃ nava), napurejāte nava, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava.

131. Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted, a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted arises by non-predominance condition. For example, dependent on non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion arise (a cycle); at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on… (complete nine), by non-prenascence, nine, by non-postnascence, nine, by non-repetition, nine.

Nakammapaccayādi

Non-kamma Condition, etc.

132. Hetuñceva sahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – hetuṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā cetanā. (1)

132. Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted, a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root arises by non-kamma condition. For example, dependent on a root, the associated volition. (1)

Sahetukañceva na ca hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – sahetuke ceva na ca hetū khandhe paṭicca sampayuttakā cetanā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe….

Dependent on a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root arises by non-kamma condition. For example, dependent on aggregates that are rooted but not roots, the associated volition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on.

Hetuñceva sahetukañca sahetukañceva na ca hetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – hetuñca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca sampayuttakā cetanā… navipākapaccayā… navippayuttapaccayā.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and rooted, and a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root arises by non-kamma condition. For example, dependent on a root and the associated aggregates, the associated volition… by non-result condition… by non-dissociation condition.
