Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition.

136. Hetu [V 3.0069] ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – alobho adosassa amohassa hetupaccayena paccayo (yathā paṭiccavārasadisaṃ). (1)

136. A phenomenon that is a root and rooted serves as a root condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted. Non-greed is a root condition for non-hatred and non-delusion (as similar to the Conditional Relations section). (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted serves as a root condition for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root. Roots serve as a root condition for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (2)

Hetu [M 3.0059] ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa [T 3.0070] hetupaccayena paccayo – alobho adosassa amohassa sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo (vitthāretabbaṃ). (3)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted serves as a root condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root. Non-greed is a root condition for non-hatred, non-delusion, and the associated aggregates (this should be elaborated). (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition.

137. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – hetuṃ ārabbha hetū uppajjanti. (1)

137. A phenomenon that is a root and rooted serves as an object condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted—taking a root as object, roots arise. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – hetuṃ ārabbha sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted serves as an object condition for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root: taking a root as object, aggregates that are rooted but not roots arise. (2)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa [V 3.0070] ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – hetuṃ ārabbha hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted serves as an object condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root: taking a root as object, roots and associated aggregates arise. (3)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati. Jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti. Pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Sahetuke ceva na ca hetū khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Cetopariyañāṇena sahetukā ceva na ca hetucittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti; ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa[T 3.0071], anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root serves as an object condition for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—having given alms, observed virtue… etc.… having performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on it; one reflects on past good deeds. Emerging from jhāna… etc.… emerging from the noble path, they reflect on the path, they reflect on the fruit. They reflect on abandoned defilements… etc.… they reflect on suppressed defilements; they know previously accumulated defilements. They contemplate aggregates that are rooted but not roots as impermanent… etc.… dejection arises. Through knowledge of the minds of others, one knows the mind of one endowed with a mind that is rooted but not a root; the base of the infinity of space serves as an object condition for the base of the infinity of consciousness… etc.… the base of nothingness serves as an object condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… etc.… aggregates that are rooted but not roots serve as an object condition for the knowledge of psychic power, knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of past lives, knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their deeds, and knowledge of the future. (1)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā… (yathā paṭhamagamanaṃ evaṃ ninnānaṃ). (2)

A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root serves as an object condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted—having given alms… (as in the first instance, and so on). (2)

Sahetuko [M 3.0060] ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā… (yathā paṭhamagamanaṃ evaṃ ninnānaṃ). (3)

A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root serves as an object condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—having given alms… (as in the first instance, and so on). (3)

138. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – hetuñca sampayuttake ca khandhe ārabbha hetū uppajjanti. (1)

138. Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and phenomena that are rooted but not a root, serve as an object condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted—taking a root and associated aggregates as object, roots arise. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – hetuñca sampayuttake ca khandhe ārabbha sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and phenomena that are rooted but not a root, serve as an object condition for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—taking a root and associated aggregates as object, aggregates that are rooted but not roots arise. (2)

Hetu [V 3.0071] ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – hetuñca sampayuttake ca khandhe ārabbha hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and phenomena that are rooted but not a root, serve as an object condition for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—taking a root and associated aggregates as object, roots and associated aggregates arise. (3)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

139. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – hetuṃ garuṃ katvā hetū uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – hetu ceva sahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ hetūnaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

139. A phenomenon that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, by way of object-dominance and conascence-dominance. By way of object-dominance: having made a root weighty, roots arise. By way of conascence-dominance: a dominant factor that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of dominance for its associated roots. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – hetuṃ garuṃ katvā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – hetu ceva sahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, by way of object-dominance and conascence-dominance. By way of object-dominance: having made the root weighty, aggregates that are rooted but not roots arise. By way of conascence-dominance: a dominant factor that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of dominance for its associated aggregates. (2)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena [T 3.0072] paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – hetuṃ garuṃ katvā [M 3.0061] hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – hetu ceva sahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetūnañca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, by way of object-dominance and conascence-dominance. By way of object-dominance: having made a root weighty, roots and associated aggregates arise. By way of conascence-dominance: a dominant factor that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of dominance for its associated aggregates and roots. (3)

140. Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, sahetuke ceva na ca hetū khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi [V 3.0072] uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – sahetuko ceva na ca hetu adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

140. A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, by way of object-dominance and conascence-dominance. By way of object-dominance: having given alms, observed virtue... having performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on it, having made it weighty; one reflects on past good deeds... having emerged from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna, having made it weighty; noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect on the path, having made it weighty; they reflect on the fruit, having made it weighty; one savors and delights in aggregates that are rooted but not roots, having made them weighty; having made that weighty, lust arises, wrong view arises. By way of conascence-dominance: a dominant factor that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of dominance for its associated aggregates. (1)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā… (paṭhamagamanaṃyeva). Sahajātādhipati – sahetuko ceva na [T 3.0073] ca hetu adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ hetūnaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, by way of object-dominance and conascence-dominance. By way of object-dominance: having given alms… (as in the first instance). By way of conascence-dominance: a dominant factor that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of dominance for its associated roots. (2)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā… (paṭhamagamanaṃyeva). Sahajātādhipati – sahetuko ceva na ca hetu adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetūnañca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root, by way of object-dominance and conascence-dominance. By way of object-dominance: having given a gift... (as in the first instance). By way of conascence-dominance: a rooted but non-root dominant factor is a condition by way of dominance for its associated aggregates and for the roots. (3)

141. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – hetū ca sampayuttake ca khandhe garuṃ katvā hetū uppajjanti. (1)

141. Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and rooted but not a root, are a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted. By way of object-dominance: having made roots and associated aggregates weighty, roots arise. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati [M 3.0062] – hetuñca sampayuttake ca khandhe garuṃ katvā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and rooted but not a root, are a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root. By way of object-dominance: having made the root and associated aggregates weighty, rooted but non-root aggregates arise. (2)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – hetuñca sampayuttake ca khandhe garuṃ katvā hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and rooted but not a root, are a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root. By way of object-dominance: having made the root and associated aggregates weighty, roots and associated aggregates arise. (3)

Anantarapaccayo

Immediacy Condition

142. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena [V 3.0073] paccayo – purimā purimā hetū pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ hetūnaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

142. A phenomenon that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted—preceding, preceding roots are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding roots. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā [T 3.0074] hetū pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ sahetukānañceva na ca hetūnaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—preceding, preceding roots are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding rooted but non-root aggregates. (2)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā hetū pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ hetūnaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—preceding, preceding roots are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding roots and associated aggregates. (3)

143. Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ sahetukānañceva na ca hetūnaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa…pe… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

143. A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—preceding, preceding rooted but non-root aggregates are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding rooted but non-root aggregates; adaptation for change-of-lineage... adaptation for purification... etc.; for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition by way of immediacy for the attainment of fruition. (1)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ hetūnaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… (saṃkhittaṃ). (2)

A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted—preceding, preceding rooted but non-root aggregates are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding roots; adaptation for change-of-lineage... (abbreviated). (2)

Sahetuko [M 3.0063] ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ hetūnaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa…pe…. (3)

A phenomenon that is rooted but not a root is a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—preceding, preceding rooted but non-root aggregates are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding roots and associated aggregates; adaptation for change-of-lineage... etc. (3)

(Sahetuko ceva na ca hetumūlakaṃ tīṇipi ekasadisā.)

(The three sections based on 'rooted but not a root' are similar.)

144. Hetu [V 3.0074] ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo [T 3.0075] – purimā purimā hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ hetūnaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

144. Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and rooted but not a root, are a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted—preceding, preceding roots and associated aggregates are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding roots. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ sahetukānañceva na ca hetūnaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.(2)

Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and rooted but not a root, are a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—preceding, preceding roots and associated aggregates are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding rooted but non-root aggregates. (2)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ hetūnaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Phenomena that are a root and rooted, and rooted but not a root, are a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted, and for a phenomenon that is rooted but not a root—preceding, preceding roots and associated aggregates are a condition by way of immediacy for succeeding, succeeding roots and associated aggregates. (3)

Sahajātapaccayādi

Conascence Condition, etc.

145. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nissayapaccayena paccayo (tīṇipi paccayā paṭiccavāre hetusadisā).

145. A phenomenon that is a root and rooted is a condition by way of conascence for a phenomenon that is a root and rooted... a condition by way of mutuality... a condition by way of support (all three conditions are similar to the Root section in the Dependent chapter).

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

146. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – hetū hetūnaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) hetū sahetukānañceva [M 3.0064] na ca hetūnaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) hetū hetūnaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo (imesaṃ dvinnampi pañhānaṃ mūlāni pucchitabbāni).

146. A state that is both a root and root-associated is a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated by way of decisive support condition—by way of object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... and so on. By way of natural decisive support—roots are a condition for roots by way of decisive support condition. (The root section should be done.) Roots are a condition for aggregates that are root-associated and not roots by way of decisive support condition. (The root section should be done.) Roots are a condition for roots and associated aggregates by way of decisive support condition. (The root sections for these two questions should be asked.)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa [T 3.0076] upanissayapaccayena [V 3.0075] paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti, sīlaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… patthanā saddhāya…pe… patthanāya maggassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for a state that is root-associated and not a root by way of decisive support condition—by way of object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... and so on. By way of natural decisive support—relying on faith, one gives a gift... and so on... generates an attainment, utters conceit, grasps a view, observes virtue... and so on... relying on aspiration, one gives a gift... and so on... splits the Saṅgha; faith... and so on... aspiration is a condition for the path and for fruition-attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

(Sahetuko ceva na ca hetumūlake iminākārena vitthāretabbā avasesā dve pañhā.)

The remaining two questions in the section on 'root-associated and not a root' should be elaborated in this manner.

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā hetūnaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Dve mūlāni pucchitabbāni) hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā sahetukānañceva na ca hetūnaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) hetū ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā hetūnaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

States that are both a root and root-associated, and root-associated and not a root, are a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated by way of decisive support condition—by way of object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... and so on. By way of natural decisive support—roots and associated aggregates are a condition for roots by way of decisive support condition. (Two root sections should be asked.) Roots and associated aggregates are a condition for aggregates that are root-associated and not roots by way of decisive support condition. (A root section should be asked.) Roots and associated aggregates are a condition for roots and associated aggregates by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

147. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo (anantarasadisaṃ).

147. A state that is both a root and root-associated is a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated by way of repetition condition (similar to the contiguity condition).

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

148. Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – sahetukā ceva na ca hetū cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā [M 3.0065] – sahetukā ceva na ca hetū cetanā vipākānaṃ [T 3.0077] sahetukānañceva na ca hetūnaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

148. A state that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for a state that is root-associated and not a root by way of kamma condition—as co-nascent, as at a different moment. As co-nascent—volition that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on. As at a different moment—volition that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for the resultant aggregates that are root-associated and not roots by way of kamma condition. (1)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo [V 3.0076] – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – sahetukā ceva na ca hetū cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ hetūnaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – sahetukā ceva na ca hetū cetanā vipākānaṃ hetūnaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated by way of kamma condition—as co-nascent, as at a different moment. As co-nascent—volition that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for the associated roots by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on. As at a different moment—volition that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for the resultant roots by way of kamma condition. (2)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – sahetukā ceva na ca hetū cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetūnañca kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – sahetukā ceva na ca hetū cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetūnañca kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated, and for a state that is root-associated and not a root, by way of kamma condition—as co-nascent, as at a different moment. As co-nascent—volition that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for the associated aggregates and roots by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on. As at a different moment—volition that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for the resultant aggregates and roots by way of kamma condition. (3)

Vipākapaccayo

Resultant Condition

149. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko alobho adosassa amohassa ca vipākapaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ); paṭisandhikkhaṇe alobho (yathā hetupaccayā evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ, navapi vipākanti niyāmetabbaṃ).

149. A state that is both a root and root-associated is a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated by way of resultant condition—resultant non-greed is a condition for non-hatred and non-delusion by way of resultant condition (a cycle); at the moment of rebirth-linking, non-greed (should be elaborated as with the root condition, and the nine resultants should also be specified).

Āhārapaccayādi

Nutriment Condition, etc.

150. Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

150. A state that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for a state that is root-associated and not a root by way of nutriment condition… three.

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo (indriyanti niyāmetabbaṃ, navapi paripuṇṇaṃ).

A state that is both a root and root-associated is a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated by way of faculty condition (the faculty should be specified, and the nine are also complete).

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa [T 3.0078] jhānapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

A state that is root-associated and not a root is a condition for a state that is root-associated and not a root by way of jhāna condition… three.

Hetu [M 3.0066] ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa maggapaccayena paccayo [V 3.0077]… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… atthipaccayena paccayo… natthipaccayena paccayo… vigatapaccayena paccayo… avigatapaccayena paccayo.

A state that is both a root and root-associated is a condition for a state that is both a root and root-associated by way of path condition… by way of association condition… by way of presence condition… by way of absence condition… by way of disappearance condition… by way of non-disappearance condition.

Exposition of the Negative

152. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

152. A state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition for a state that is both a root and accompanied by roots by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition for a state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition for a state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, and for a state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root, by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition. (3)

153. Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo sahetukassa [T 3.0079] ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

153. A state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root is a condition for a state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of kamma condition. (1)

Sahetuko [M 3.0067][V 3.0078] ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root is a condition for a state that is both a root and accompanied by roots by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of kamma condition. (2)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root is a condition for a state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, and for a state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root, by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of kamma condition. (3)

154. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

154. States that are both roots and accompanied by roots, and states that are accompanied by roots but are not roots, are a condition for a state that is both a root and accompanied by roots by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

States that are both roots and accompanied by roots, and states that are accompanied by roots but are not roots, are a condition for a state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Hetu ceva sahetuko ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

States that are both roots and accompanied by roots, and states that are accompanied by roots but are not roots, are a condition for a state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, and for a state that is accompanied by roots but is not a root, by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition. (3)

157. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte tīṇi, aññamaññe tīṇi, nissaye tīṇi, upanissaye nava, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi, vipāke tīṇi, āhāre tīṇi, indriye tīṇi, jhāne tīṇi, magge tīṇi, sampayutte tīṇi, atthiyā tīṇi, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate tīṇi (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

157. 1. The Section on Dependence

158. Hetuñceva [V 3.0080] hetusampayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – alobhaṃ paṭicca adoso amoho (cakkaṃ). Lobhaṃ paṭicca moho (cakkaṃ); paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yathā hetusahetukadukaṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ, ninnānākaraṇaṃ).

158. Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and root-associated, a phenomenon that is both a root and root-associated arises by way of root condition: dependent on non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion arise (cycle). Dependent on greed, delusion arises (cycle); at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so forth… (it should be elaborated as in the Dyad of Root and Root-Accompanied, with no difference).

Hetuhetusampayuttadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Root and Root-Associated Phenomena is concluded.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

159. Nahetuṃ [T 3.0081][M 3.0069][V 3.0081] sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

159. A non-root, rooted phenomenon arises in dependence on a non-root, rooted phenomenon by way of root condition: in dependence on one non-root, rooted aggregate, three aggregates arise…and so forth…in dependence on two aggregates…and so forth…at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so forth…. (1)

Nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetū sahetuke khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A non-root, rootless phenomenon arises in dependence on a non-root, rooted phenomenon by way of root condition: mind-produced materiality arises in dependence on non-root, rooted aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so forth…. (2)

Nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko ca nahetu ahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

Both a non-root, rooted phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon arise in dependence on a non-root, rooted phenomenon by way of root condition: in dependence on one non-root, rooted aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality arise…and so forth…in dependence on two aggregates…and so forth…at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so forth…. (3)

160. Nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā [V 3.0082] …pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

160. A non-root, rootless phenomenon arises in dependence on a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of root condition: …and so forth…in dependence on one great element…and so forth…in dependence on the great elements, mind-produced materiality, kamma-produced materiality, and derived materiality arise. (1)

Nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca nahetū sahetukā khandhā. (2)

A non-root, rooted phenomenon arises in dependence on a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of root condition: At the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on the physical base, non-root, rooted aggregates arise. (2)

Nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko ca nahetu ahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca nahetū sahetukā khandhā, mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ. (3)

Both a non-root, rooted phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon arise in dependence on a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of root condition: At the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on the physical base, non-root, rooted aggregates arise; and in dependence on the great elements, kamma-produced materiality arises. (3)

161. Nahetuṃ sahetukañca nahetuṃ ahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca [T 3.0082] vatthuñca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe…. (1)

161. A non-root, rooted phenomenon arises in dependence on both a non-root, rooted phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of root condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on one non-root, rooted aggregate and the physical base, three aggregates arise…and so forth…in dependence on two aggregates and the physical base…and so forth…. (1)

Nahetuṃ sahetukañca nahetuṃ ahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetū sahetuke khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A non-root, rootless phenomenon arises in dependence on both a non-root, rooted phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of root condition: Mind-produced materiality arises in dependence on non-root, rooted aggregates and the great elements; at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so forth…. (2)

Nahetuṃ [M 3.0070] sahetukañca nahetuṃ ahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko ca nahetu ahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… nahetū sahetuke khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ. (3)

Both a non-root, rooted phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon arise in dependence on both a non-root, rooted phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of root condition: At the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on one non-root, rooted aggregate and the physical base, three aggregates arise…and so forth…in dependence on two aggregates and the physical base…and so forth…; kamma-produced materiality arises in dependence on non-root, rooted aggregates and the great elements. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

162. Nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

162. A non-root, rooted phenomenon arises in dependence on a non-root, rooted phenomenon by way of object condition: in dependence on one non-root, rooted aggregate, three aggregates arise…and so forth…in dependence on two aggregates…and so forth…at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so forth…. (1)

Nahetuṃ [V 3.0083] ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A non-root, rootless phenomenon arises in dependence on a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of object condition: in dependence on one non-root, rootless aggregate, three aggregates arise…and so forth…at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so forth…. (2)

Nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca nahetū sahetukā khandhā. (3)

A non-root, rooted phenomenon arises in dependence on a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of object condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on the physical base, non-root, rooted aggregates arise. (3)

Nahetuṃ sahetukañca nahetuṃ ahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… (saṃkhittaṃ. Evaṃ vibhajitabbaṃ).

A non-root, rooted phenomenon arises in dependence on both a non-root, rooted phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of object condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on one non-root, rooted aggregate and the physical base, three aggregates arise…and so forth…in dependence on two aggregates and the physical base…and so forth…. (Abbreviated. It should be analyzed thus.)

The Root Dyad

167. Hetupaccayā [M 3.0072][V 3.0085] naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava, naanantare nava, nasamanantare nava, naaññamaññe nava, naupanissaye tīṇi, napurejāte nava, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava, nakamme ekaṃ, navipāke pañca, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte ekaṃ, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

167. By way of the root condition: not by way of the object condition, three; not by way of the dominance condition, nine; not by way of the proximity condition, nine; not by way of the contiguous condition, nine; not by way of the mutuality condition, nine; not by way of the decisive support condition, three; not by way of the prenascence condition, nine; not by way of the postnascence condition, nine; not by way of the repetition condition, nine; not by way of the kamma condition, one; not by way of the resultant condition, five; not by way of the association condition, three; not by way of the dissociation condition, one; not by way of the absence condition, three; not by way of the disappearance condition, three (thus should be reckoned).

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

The Affirmative-Negative Mode.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Affirmative Mode of Conditional Relations

Nahetudukaṃ

The Non-root Dyad

168. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… āhāre ekaṃ…pe… jhāne ekaṃ, sampayutte ekaṃ, vippayutte ekaṃ…pe… vigate ekaṃ, avigate ekaṃ (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

168. Not by way of the root condition: by way of the object condition, one...and so on...by way of the nutriment condition, one...and so on...by way of the jhāna condition, one; by way of the association condition, one; by way of the dissociation condition, one...and so on...by way of the disappearance condition, one; by way of the presence condition, one (thus should be reckoned).

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.

The Negative-Affirmative Mode.

1-4. The Affirmative Mode of Conditional Relations, etc.

169. Nahetuṃ [V 3.0086] sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

169. Dependent on a rootless, rooted phenomenon, a rootless, rooted phenomenon arises by way of the root condition...three.

Nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu [T 3.0085] ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paccayā tayo mahābhūtā, mahābhūte paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, kaṭattārūpaṃ, upādārūpaṃ. (1)

Dependent on a rootless, root-free phenomenon, a rootless, root-free phenomenon arises by way of the root condition: dependent on one great element, three great elements; dependent on the great elements, mind-originated materiality, kamma-born materiality, and derived materiality. (1)

Nahetuṃ [M 3.0073] ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – vatthuṃ paccayā nahetū sahetukā khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (2)

Dependent on a rootless, root-free phenomenon, a rootless, rooted phenomenon arises by way of the root condition: dependent on the physical base, rootless, rooted aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking...and so on. (2)

Nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu sahetuko ca nahetu ahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – vatthuṃ paccayā nahetū sahetukā khandhā, mahābhūte paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…(3)

Dependent on a rootless, root-free phenomenon, both a rootless, rooted phenomenon and a rootless, root-free phenomenon arise by way of the root condition: dependent on the physical base, rootless, rooted aggregates; dependent on the great elements, mind-originated materiality; at the moment of rebirth-linking...and so on. (3)

Nahetuṃ sahetukañca nahetuṃ ahetukañca dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (ghaṭanā tīṇi, pavattipaṭisandhi paripuṇṇaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ).

Dependent on both a rootless, rooted phenomenon and a rootless, root-free phenomenon, a rootless, rooted phenomenon arises by way of the root condition (three occurrences, process and rebirth-linking complete. Abbreviated).

170. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe cattāri…pe… aññamaññe cha…pe… purejāte āsevane cattāri…pe… avigate nava (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

170. By way of the root condition, nine; by way of the object condition, four...and so on...by way of the mutuality condition, six...and so on...by way of the prenascence condition, four; by way of the repetition condition, four...and so on...by way of the presence condition, nine (thus should be reckoned).

Anulomaṃ.

The Affirmative Mode.

171. Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naārammaṇe tīṇi…pe… novigate tīṇi.

171. Not by way of the root condition, one; not by way of the object condition, three...and so on...not by way of the disappearance condition, three.

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative Mode.

1-4. Paccayānulomādi

1-4. The Affirmative Mode of Conditional Relations, etc.

172. Nahetuṃ [V 3.0087] sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetuṃ sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe….

172. A rootless, rooted phenomenon, concomitant with a rootless, rooted phenomenon, arises by way of the root condition: one rootless, rooted aggregate...and so on...at the moment of rebirth-linking...and so on.

173. Hetuyā [T 3.0086] ekaṃ, ārammaṇe dve, adhipatiyā ekaṃ, anantare dve (sabbattha dve), magge ekaṃ…pe… avigate dve.

173. By way of the root condition, one; by way of the object condition, two; by way of the dominance condition, one; by way of the proximity condition, two (everywhere two); by way of the path condition, one...and so on...by way of the presence condition, two.

Anulomaṃ.

The Affirmative Mode.

174. Nahetuṃ [M 3.0074] ahetukaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – nahetuṃ ahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe….

174. A phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless, associated with a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless, arises not by way of root condition: one aggregate that is not a root and is rootless...and so on...at the moment of rebirth-linking...and so on.

175. Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naadhipatiyā dve, napurejāte dve, napacchājāte dve, naāsevane dve, nakamme dve, navipāke dve, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, navippayutte dve.

175. Not by way of root condition, one; not by way of predominance condition, two; not by way of prenascence condition, two; not by way of postnascence condition, two; not by way of repetition condition, two; not by way of kamma condition, two; not by way of resultant condition, two; not by way of jhāna condition, one; not by way of path condition, one; not by way of dissociation condition, two.

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative Mode.

(Evaṃ avasesāpi dve gaṇanā gaṇetabbā.)

(Similarly, the remaining two enumerations should be reckoned.)
