1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Progression of Conditions.

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. The Section on Differentiation.

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition.

176. Nahetu [V 3.0088] sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati; jhānaṃ…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti; pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe…pe… nahetū sahetuke khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; cetopariyañāṇena nahetusahetukacittasamaṅgissa [T 3.0087] cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ…pe… nahetū sahetukā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; nahetū sahetuke khandhe ārabbha nahetū sahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

176. A phenomenon that is not a root but has roots is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root but has roots by way of object condition. Having given alms, undertaken the precepts... and so on... performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects upon that; one reflects on past well-performed deeds; the noble ones, having emerged from jhāna... and so on... from the path, reflect on the path, reflect on the fruition; on abandoned defilements... and so on... on suppressed defilements... and so on... previously... and so on... when aggregates that are not a root but have roots are regarded as impermanent... and so on... grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a resultant that is not a root but has roots arises taking them as object; with knowledge encompassing the minds of others, one knows the mind of one endowed with a consciousness that is not a root but has roots; the sphere of infinite space... and so on... the sphere of nothingness... and so on... aggregates that are not a root but have roots are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, for the knowledge encompassing the minds of others, for the knowledge of recollecting past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, and for the knowledge of the future by way of object condition; taking as object aggregates that are not a root but have roots, aggregates that are not a root but have roots arise. (1)

Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nahetū sahetuke khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ [M 3.0075] uppajjati, kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, nahetū sahetuke khandhe ārabbha nahetū ahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A phenomenon that is not a root but has roots is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless by way of object condition. When aggregates that are not a root but have roots are regarded as impermanent... and so on... grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a resultant that is not a root and is rootless arises taking them as object; taking as object aggregates that are not a root but have roots, aggregates that are not a root and are rootless arise. (2)

177. Nahetu [V 3.0089] ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nibbānaṃ āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… nahetū ahetuke khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… nahetū ahetuke khandhe ārabbha nahetū ahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

177. A phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless by way of object condition. Nibbāna is a condition for adverting by way of object condition; the eye... and so on... the physical basis... and so on... when aggregates that are not a root and are rootless are regarded as impermanent... and so on... grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a resultant that is not a root and is rootless arises taking them as object. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness... and so on... the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness... and so on... taking as object aggregates that are not a root and are rootless, aggregates that are not a root and are rootless arise. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… nahetū ahetuke khandhe aniccato [T 3.0088] …pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Cetopariyañāṇena nahetuahetukacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti. Nahetū ahetukā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; nahetū ahetuke khandhe ārabbha nahetū sahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root but has roots by way of object condition. The noble ones reflect on Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruition by way of object condition; the eye... and so on... the physical basis... and so on... when aggregates that are not a root and are rootless are regarded as impermanent... and so on... grief arises; when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, a resultant that is not a root but has roots arises taking them as object; with the divine eye one sees form; with the divine ear-element one hears sound. With knowledge encompassing the minds of others, one knows the mind of one endowed with a consciousness that is not a root and is rootless. Aggregates that are not a root and are rootless are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, for the knowledge encompassing the minds of others, for the knowledge of recollecting past lives, and for the knowledge of the future by way of object condition; taking as object aggregates that are not a root and are rootless, aggregates that are not a root but have roots arise. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Predominance Condition.

178. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, jhānaṃ…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Nahetū sahetuke khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – nahetusahetukādhipati [M 3.0076] sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

178. A phenomenon that is not a root but has roots is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root but has roots by way of predominance condition: by way of object-predominance and conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: Having given alms, undertaken the precepts, performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects upon that, holding it in high esteem; one reflects on past well-performed deeds, holding them in high esteem; the noble ones, having emerged from jhāna... and so on... from the path, reflect on the path, holding it in high esteem; they reflect on the fruition, holding it in high esteem. One savors and delights in aggregates that are not a root but have roots, holding them in high esteem; holding that in high esteem, lust arises, or wrong view arises. Conascence-predominance: A predominance that is not a root but has roots is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of predominance condition. (1)

Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – nahetu sahetukādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is not a root but has roots is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless by way of predominance condition. Conascence-predominance: A predominance that is not a root but has roots is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of predominance condition. (2)

Nahetu [V 3.0090] sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa ca nahetuahetukassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – nahetu sahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ [T 3.0089] khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is not a root but has roots is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root but has roots and for a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless by way of predominance condition. Conascence-predominance: A predominance that is not a root but has roots is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of predominance condition. (3)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… nahetū ahetuke khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1)

A phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless is a condition for a phenomenon that is not a root but has roots by way of predominance condition. Object-predominance: The noble ones reflect on Nibbāna, holding it in high esteem; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruition by way of predominance condition; the eye... and so on... the physical basis... and so on... one savors and delights in aggregates that are not a root and are rootless, holding them in high esteem; holding that in high esteem, lust arises, or wrong view arises. (1)

Anantarapaccayo

The Immediate Condition.

179. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nahetū sahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

179. A rootless state accompanied by roots is a condition for a rootless state accompanied by roots by way of immediate condition—preceding rootless aggregates accompanied by roots are a condition for subsequent rootless aggregates accompanied by roots by way of immediate condition; adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage…pe…the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for fruition attainment by way of immediate condition. (1)

Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – nahetu sahetukaṃ cuticittaṃ nahetuahetukassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; nahetu sahetukaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāya, nahetu sahetukaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ nahetuahetukassa bhavaṅgassa, nahetū sahetukā khandhā nahetuahetukassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless state accompanied by roots is a condition for a rootless state without roots by way of immediate condition—a rootless death consciousness accompanied by roots is a condition for a rootless rebirth consciousness without roots by way of immediate condition; a rootless life-continuum accompanied by roots is a condition for adverting; a rootless life-continuum accompanied by roots is a condition for a rootless life-continuum without roots; rootless aggregates accompanied by roots are a condition for the arising of a rootless state without roots by way of immediate condition. (2)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nahetū ahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ [M 3.0077] nahetuahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena [T 3.0090] paccayo. (1)

A rootless state without roots is a condition for a rootless state without roots by way of immediate condition—preceding rootless aggregates without roots are a condition for subsequent rootless aggregates without roots by way of immediate condition; adverting is a condition for the five consciousnesses by way of immediate condition. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – nahetu ahetukaṃ cuticittaṃ nahetusahetukassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā nahetusahetukānaṃ [V 3.0091] khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; nahetū ahetukā khandhā nahetusahetukassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless state without roots is a condition for a rootless state accompanied by roots by way of immediate condition—a rootless death consciousness without roots is a condition for a rootless rebirth consciousness accompanied by roots by way of immediate condition; adverting is a condition for rootless aggregates accompanied by roots by way of immediate condition; rootless aggregates without roots are a condition for the arising of a rootless state accompanied by roots by way of immediate condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayādi

Contiguity Condition, etc.

180. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo (iha ghaṭanā natthi, satta pañhā)… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo (cha pañhā)… nissayapaccayena paccayo (pavattipaṭisandhi satta pañhā, iha ghaṭanā natthi).

180. A rootless state accompanied by roots is a condition for a rootless state accompanied by roots by way of contiguity condition… by way of co-nascence condition (here there is no combination, seven questions)… by way of mutual condition (six questions)… by way of support condition (in the course of life and at rebirth-linking, seven questions, here there is no combination).

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

181. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… patthanā saddhāya…pe… patthanāya maggassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

181. A rootless state accompanied by roots is a condition for a rootless state accompanied by roots by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediate decisive support, natural decisive support…pe… Natural decisive support—relying on faith, one gives alms…pe… indulges in conceit, grasps at views; virtue…pe… relying on aspiration, one gives alms…pe… splits the Sangha; faith…pe… aspiration is a condition for faith…pe… for aspiration, for the path, and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhā kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; sīlaṃ…pe… patthanā kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa [T 3.0091] dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; saddhā…pe… patthanā kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless state accompanied by roots is a condition for a rootless state without roots by way of decisive support condition—immediate decisive support, natural decisive support…pe… Natural decisive support—faith is a condition for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition; virtue…pe… aspiration is a condition for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition; faith…pe… aspiration is a condition for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition. (2)

182. Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa [M 3.0078] upanissayapaccayena paccayo; kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utu… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utu… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

182. A rootless state without roots is a condition for a rootless state without roots by way of decisive support condition—immediate decisive support, natural decisive support…pe… Natural decisive support—bodily pleasure is a condition for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition; bodily pain… climate… food… lodging is a condition for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition; bodily pleasure… bodily pain… climate… food… lodging is a condition for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Nahetu [V 3.0092] ahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ …pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… patthanāya maggassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rootless state without roots is a condition for a rootless state accompanied by roots by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediate decisive support, natural decisive support…pe… Natural decisive support—relying on bodily pleasure, one gives alms…pe… splits the Sangha; relying on bodily pain… climate… food… lodging, one gives alms…pe… splits the Sangha; bodily pleasure…pe… lodging is a condition for faith…pe… for aspiration, for the path, and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

183. Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena [T 3.0092] paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu nahetuahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

183. A rootless state without roots is a condition for a rootless state without roots by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: considering the eye…pe… the physical base as impermanent…pe… grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a rootless resultant without roots arises as a registration consciousness; the visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition…pe… the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness… the physical base is a condition for the rootless aggregates without roots by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: the eye…pe… the base as impermanent…pe… sorrow arises; when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, a not-root, with-root resultant arises, taking that as object; with the divine eye, one sees a form; with the divine ear-element, one hears a sound. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for the not-root, with-root aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition

184. Nahetu [M 3.0079] sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā nahetū sahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

184. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition: the subsequently arisen not-root, with-root aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Nahetu [V 3.0093] ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā nahetū ahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition: the subsequently arisen not-root, rootless aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

185. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nahetū sahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo… anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

185. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of repetition condition: the preceding not-root, with-root aggregates are a condition for the succeeding not-root, with-root aggregates by way of repetition condition… conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage… conformity is a condition for purification… change-of-lineage is a condition for the path… purification is a condition for the path by way of repetition condition. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā [T 3.0093] purimā nahetū ahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nahetuahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of repetition condition: the preceding not-root, rootless aggregates are a condition for the succeeding not-root, rootless aggregates by way of repetition condition. (1)

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

186. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – nahetu sahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – nahetu sahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

186. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of kamma condition: conascent, and different-moment. Conascent: not-root, with-root volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. Different-moment: not-root, with-root volition is a condition for the resultant not-root, with-root aggregates by way of kamma condition. (1)

Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – nahetu sahetukā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – nahetu sahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ nahetuahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of kamma condition: conascent, and different-moment. Conascent: not-root, with-root volition is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. Different-moment: not-root, with-root volition is a condition for the resultant not-root, rootless aggregates and for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (1)

Nahetu [M 3.0080] sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa ca nahetuahetukassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – nahetu sahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā [V 3.0094] – nahetu sahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for both a not-root, with-root phenomenon and a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of kamma condition: conascent, and different-moment. Conascent: not-root, with-root volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. Different-moment: not-root, with-root volition is a condition for the resultant not-root, with-root aggregates and for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā – nahetu ahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe nahetu ahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ [T 3.0094] khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of kamma condition. Conascent: not-root, rootless volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, not-root, rootless volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Resultant Condition

187. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

187. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of resultant condition… three.

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ.

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of resultant condition… one.

Āhārapaccayo

Nutriment Condition

188. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

188. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of nutriment condition… three.

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – nahetu ahetukā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of nutriment condition—not-root, rootless nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of nutriment condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… physical food is a condition for this body by way of nutriment condition. (1)

Indriyapaccayo

Faculty Condition

189. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

189. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of faculty condition… three.

Nahetu [M 3.0081] ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – nahetu ahetukā [V 3.0095] indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo.

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of faculty condition—not-root, rootless faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of faculty condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… the life faculty of materiality is a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of faculty condition.

Jhānapaccayādi

Jhāna Condition, etc.

190. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo…pe… (cattāripi kātabbāni), maggapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

190. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of jhāna condition…pe… (all four should be done), a condition by way of path condition… three.

Sampayuttapaccayo

Association Condition

191. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena [T 3.0095] paccayo – nahetu sahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

191. A not-root, with-root phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, with-root phenomenon by way of association condition—one not-root, with-root aggregate is a condition for the other three aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – nahetu ahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A not-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a not-root, rootless phenomenon by way of association condition—one not-root, rootless aggregate is a condition for the other three aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. (2)

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

192. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – nahetū sahetukā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – nahetū sahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

192. A non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of Dissociation Condition—co-nascence and post-nascence. Co-nascence—non-root, root-accompanied aggregates are conditions for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Dissociation Condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on. Post-nascence—non-root, root-accompanied aggregates are conditions for this pre-arisen body by way of Dissociation Condition. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – nahetū ahetukā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo[V 3.0096]. Pacchājātā – nahetū ahetukā [M 3.0082] khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A non-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of Dissociation Condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence, and post-nascence. Co-nascence—non-root, rootless aggregates are conditions for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Dissociation Condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on... aggregates are conditions for the physical base by way of Dissociation Condition; the physical base is a condition for the aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. Pre-nascence—the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness... and so on... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness... and so on... the physical base is a condition for non-root, root-accompanied aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. Post-nascence—non-root, rootless aggregates are conditions for this pre-arisen body by way of Dissociation Condition. (1)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ [T 3.0096] – vatthu nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon by way of Dissociation Condition—co-nascence and pre-nascence. Co-nascence—at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition for the non-root, root-accompanied aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. Pre-nascence—the physical base is a condition for the non-root, root-accompanied aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. (2)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

193. Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – nahetu sahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

193. A non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—one non-root, root-accompanied aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates... and so on... at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on. (1)

Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ…pe…. (2)

A non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, post-nascence... and so on. (2)

Nahetu sahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa ca nahetuahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – nahetu sahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon and a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—one non-root, root-accompanied aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Presence Condition... and so on... at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on. (3)

Nahetu ahetuko dhammo nahetuahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – nahetu ahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu ahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… vatthu nahetuahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nahetū ahetukā khandhā purejātassa…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

A non-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. Co-nascence—one non-root, rootless aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Presence Condition... and so on... (up to non-percipient beings). Pre-nascence—the eye... and so on... the physical base, when seen as impermanent... and so on... sorrow arises; when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, a non-root, rootless resultant registering consciousness arises; the visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness... and so on... the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness... and so on... the eye-base... and so on... the body-base... and so on... the physical base is a condition for the non-root, rootless aggregates by way of Presence Condition. Post-nascence—non-root, rootless aggregates are conditions for the pre-arisen... and so on... edible food is a condition for this body... and so on... the material life faculty is a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of Presence Condition. (1)

Nahetu [V 3.0097] ahetuko dhammo nahetusahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu [T 3.0097][M 3.0083] nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, kusalākusale niruddhe nahetu sahetuko vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu nahetusahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-root, rootless phenomenon is a condition for a non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence and pre-nascence. Co-nascence—at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition for the non-root, root-accompanied aggregates by way of Presence Condition. Pre-nascence—the eye... and so on... the physical base, when seen as impermanent... and so on... sorrow arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a non-root, root-accompanied resultant registering consciousness arises; with the divine eye, one sees a visible form; with the divine ear element, one hears a sound. Pre-nascence of the physical base—the physical base is a condition for the non-root, root-accompanied aggregates by way of Presence Condition. (2)

194. Nahetu sahetuko ca nahetu ahetuko ca dhammā nahetusahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – nahetu sahetuko eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… nahetu sahetuko eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe…. (1)

194. Non-root, root-accompanied phenomena and non-root, rootless phenomena are conditions for a non-root, root-accompanied phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence and pre-nascence. Co-nascence—one non-root, root-accompanied aggregate and the physical base are conditions for the three aggregates... and so on... at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on... one non-root, root-accompanied aggregate and the physical base are conditions for the three aggregates... and so on. (1)

Nahetu sahetuko ca nahetu ahetuko ca dhammā nahetuahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – nahetū sahetukā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – nahetū sahetukā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nahetū sahetukā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe…. (2)

Non-root, root-accompanied phenomena and non-root, rootless phenomena are conditions for a non-root, rootless phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. Co-nascence—non-root, root-accompanied aggregates and the great elements are conditions for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Presence Condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on. Post-nascence—non-root, root-accompanied aggregates and edible food are conditions for this body by way of Presence Condition. Post-nascence—non-root, root-accompanied aggregates and the material life faculty are conditions for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of Presence Condition... and so on. (2)

1. Sappaccayaṃ [M 3.0086][V 3.0101] dhammaṃ paṭicca sappaccayo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – sappaccayaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca [T 3.0100] rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ.

1. Dependent on a conditioned phenomenon, a conditioned phenomenon arises by way of root condition—dependent on one conditioned aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on... at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on... dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis arises; dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates arise; dependent on one great element... and so on... dependent on the great elements, mind-originated materiality, kamma-born materiality, and derived materiality arise.

Sappaccayaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sappaccayo dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā.

Dependent on a conditioned phenomenon, a conditioned phenomenon arises by way of object condition... by way of non-disappearance condition.

2. Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ.

2. One by way of root condition, one by way of object condition... one by way of non-disappearance condition.

Concordant.

4. Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naārammaṇe ekaṃ, naadhipatiyā ekaṃ…pe… novigate ekaṃ.

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

9. Sappaccayo dhammo sappaccayassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā, sīlaṃ samādiyitvā, uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ [T 3.0102] paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti; pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti, cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… sappaccaye khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā [V 3.0104] rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Cetopariyañāṇena sappaccayacittasamaṅgissa [M 3.0088] cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… sappaccayā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

9. A conditioned phenomenon is a condition for a conditioned phenomenon by way of object condition—having given a gift, having undertaken the precepts, or having performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects upon that; having previously practiced well…having emerged from jhāna…the noble ones reflect upon the path after emerging from the path, they reflect upon the fruit; they know the abandoned defilements…the suppressed defilements…the previously accumulated defilements; the eye…the base…the conditioned aggregates as impermanent…sorrow arises; with the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear element, one hears sounds. Through the knowledge of others' minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with a conditioned mind; the base of the infinity of space for the base of the infinity of consciousness…the base of nothingness for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception…the form base for eye-consciousness…the tangible base for body-consciousness…the conditioned aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting by way of object condition. (1)

Appaccayo dhammo sappaccayassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unconditioned phenomenon is a condition for a conditioned phenomenon by way of object condition—the noble ones reflect on Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition by way of object condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruit, and for adverting. (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

10. Sappaccayo dhammo sappaccayassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… sappaccaye khandhe garuṃ [T 3.0103] katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – sappaccayādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

10. A conditioned phenomenon is a condition for a conditioned phenomenon by way of dominance condition: object-dominance and co-nascence-dominance. Object-dominance: having given a gift, observed morality…having performed the Uposatha, one regards it as important and reflects upon it; previously…jhānas…the noble ones, having emerged from the path, regard the path as important and reflect upon it, regard the fruit as important…the eye…the base…one regards the conditioned aggregates as important, delights in them, rejoices in them; regarding that as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence-dominance: a conditioned dominant factor is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of dominance condition. (1)

Appaccayo dhammo sappaccayassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unconditioned phenomenon is a condition for a conditioned phenomenon by way of dominance condition. Object-dominance: The noble ones, having made Nibbāna weighty, reflect upon it; Nibbāna is a condition by way of dominance condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit. (1)

Root condition.

17. Saṅkhataṃ [T 3.0105][V 3.0107] dhammaṃ paṭicca saṅkhato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – saṅkhataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā; ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ.

17. A conditioned phenomenon arises in dependence on a conditioned phenomenon by way of root condition—in dependence on one conditioned aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise… at the moment of rebirth-linking… the aggregates arise in dependence on the base, the base arises in dependence on the aggregates; in dependence on one great element… in dependence on the great elements, mind-originated materiality, kamma-born materiality, and derived materiality arise.

(Imaṃ dukaṃ yathā sappaccayadukaṃ, evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ, ninnānākaraṇaṃ.)

(This dyad should be reckoned in the same way as the Dyad of the Conditioned, with no variation.)

Saṅkhatadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of the Conditioned is completed.

Hetupaccayo

Root condition.

18. Anidassanaṃ [V 3.0108] dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassano dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā; ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca anidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

18. An invisible phenomenon arises in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of root condition—in dependence on one invisible aggregate, three aggregates and invisible mind-originated materiality arise… in dependence on two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on one invisible aggregate, three aggregates and invisible kamma-born materiality arise… in dependence on two aggregates… the aggregates arise in dependence on the base, the base arises in dependence on the aggregates; in dependence on one great element… in dependence on the great elements, invisible mind-originated materiality, kamma-born materiality, and derived materiality arise. (1)

Anidassanaṃ [M 3.0091] dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassane khandhe paṭicca sanidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ[T 3.0106]; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (2)

A visible phenomenon arises in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of root condition—visible mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on invisible aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking… visible mind-originated materiality, kamma-born materiality, and derived materiality arise in dependence on the great elements. (2)

Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano ca anidassano ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā sanidassanañca anidassanañca cittasamuṭṭhānañca [V 3.0109] rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanañca anidassanañca cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (3)

Both visible and invisible phenomena arise in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of root condition: in dependence on one invisible aggregate, three aggregates and both visible and invisible mind-originated materiality arise… in dependence on two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… in dependence on the great elements, both visible and invisible mind-originated materiality, kamma-born materiality, and derived materiality arise. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object condition.

19. Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassano dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. (1)

19. An invisible phenomenon arises in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of object condition—in dependence on one invisible aggregate, three aggregates arise… in dependence on two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… in dependence on the base, the aggregates arise. (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance condition.

20. Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassano dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā…pe… dve mahābhūte…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca anidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

20. An invisible phenomenon arises in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of dominance condition—in dependence on one invisible aggregate, three aggregates and invisible mind-originated materiality arise… in dependence on two aggregates… in dependence on one great element, three great elements arise… in dependence on two great elements… in dependence on the great elements, invisible mind-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. (1)

Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – anidassane khandhe paṭicca sanidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A visible phenomenon arises in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of dominance condition—visible mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on invisible aggregates; visible mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on the great elements. (2)

Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano ca anidassano ca dhammā uppajjanti adhipatipaccayā – anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā sanidassanañca anidassanañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanañca [T 3.0107] anidassanañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (3) (Saṃkhittaṃ, sabbe kātabbā.)

Both visible and invisible phenomena arise in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of dominance condition—in dependence on one invisible aggregate, three aggregates and both visible and invisible mind-originated materiality arise… in dependence on two aggregates… in dependence on the great elements, both visible and invisible mind-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. (3) (In brief, all should be done.)

21. Hetuyā [M 3.0092][V 3.0110] tīṇi, ārammaṇe ekaṃ, adhipatiyā tīṇi, anantare ekaṃ, samanantare ekaṃ, sahajāte tīṇi, aññamaññe ekaṃ, nissaye tīṇi, upanissaye ekaṃ, purejāte ekaṃ, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme tīṇi, vipāke tīṇi (sabbattha tīṇi), magge tīṇi, sampayutte ekaṃ, vippayutte tīṇi, atthiyā tīṇi, natthiyā ekaṃ, vigate ekaṃ, avigate tīṇi (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

21. By root condition, three; by object condition, one; by dominance condition, three; by contiguity condition, one; by immediately contiguous condition, one; by co-nascence condition, three; by reciprocity condition, one; by dependence condition, three; by strong support condition, one; by pre-nascence condition, one; by repetition condition, one; by kamma condition, three; by result condition, three (everywhere three); by path condition, three; by association condition, one; by dissociation condition, three; by presence condition, three; by absence condition, one; by disappearance condition, one; by non-disappearance condition, three (thus should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

The Non-Root Condition

22. Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassano dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā; ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca anidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

22. An invisible phenomenon arises in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of non-root condition—in dependence on one rootless invisible aggregate, three aggregates and invisible mind-originated materiality arise… (and so on)… in dependence on two aggregates… (and so on)… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking… (and so on)… in dependence on the aggregates, the base; in dependence on the base, the aggregates; in dependence on one great element… (and so on)… in dependence on the great elements, invisible mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, derived materiality… external (materiality)… nutriment-originated (materiality)… temperature-originated (materiality)… for non-percipient beings… (and so on)… in dependence on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, the delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetuke anidassane khandhe paṭicca sanidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… mahābhūte [T 3.0108] paṭicca [V 3.0111] sanidassanaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ… bāhire… āhārasamuṭṭhāne… utusamuṭṭhāne… asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (2)

A visible phenomenon arises in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of non-root condition—in dependence on rootless invisible aggregates, visible mind-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking… (and so on)… in dependence on the great elements, visible mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, derived materiality… external (materiality)… nutriment-originated (materiality)… temperature-originated (materiality)… for non-percipient beings, in dependence on the great elements, visible kamma-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. (2)

Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano ca anidassano ca dhammā uppajjanti nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā sanidassanañca [M 3.0093] anidassanañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca…pe… bāhire… āhārasamuṭṭhāne… utusamuṭṭhāne… asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanañca anidassanañca kaṭattārūpaṃ, upādārūpaṃ. (3) (Evaṃ sabbe kātabbā.)

Both visible and invisible phenomena arise in dependence on an invisible phenomenon by way of non-root condition—in dependence on one rootless invisible aggregate, three aggregates and both visible and invisible mind-originated materiality arise… (and so on)… two aggregates… (and so on)… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (and so on)… in dependence on the great elements… (and so on)… external (materiality)… nutriment-originated (materiality)… temperature-originated (materiality)… for non-percipient beings, in dependence on the great elements, both visible and invisible kamma-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. (3) (Thus all should be done.)

26. Conditioned by a non-manifest phenomenon, a non-manifest phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Conditioned by one non-manifest aggregate, three aggregates and non-manifest mind-originated materiality arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on… conditioned by the aggregates, the physical basis; conditioned by the physical basis, the aggregates. Conditioned by one great element… and so on… conditioned by the great elements, non-manifest mind-originated materiality, kamma-born materiality, and derived materiality. Conditioned by the physical basis, the non-manifest aggregates. (The other two questions should also be dealt with.)

The Object Condition

27. Anidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā anidassano dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – anidassanaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vatthuṃ paccayā khandhā, cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā anidassanā khandhā (saṃkhittaṃ).

27. Conditioned by a non-manifest phenomenon, a non-manifest phenomenon arises by way of object condition. Conditioned by one non-manifest aggregate… two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… conditioned by the physical basis, the aggregates; conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness… and so on… conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness; conditioned by the physical basis, the non-manifest aggregates (in brief).

28. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe ekaṃ, adhipatiyā tīṇi…pe… avigate [T 3.0110] tīṇi.

28. By root condition, three; by object condition, one; by dominance condition, three… and so on… by non-disappearance condition, three.

Root Condition.

34. A non-manifest phenomenon is a condition for a non-manifest phenomenon by way of Root Condition: non-manifest roots are a condition by way of Root Condition for the associated aggregates and for non-manifest mind-originated material forms; at the moment of relinking... (1)

Anidassano dhammo sanidassanassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – anidassanā hetū sanidassanānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

Anidassano dhammo sanidassanassa ca anidassanassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – anidassanā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ sanidassanānañca anidassanānañca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)
