Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

16. Āsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – kāmāsavo diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa hetupaccayena paccayo; bhavāsavo avijjāsavassa hetupaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). (1)

16. A tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon by way of root condition—the taint of sensual desire is a condition for the taint of wrong view and the taint of ignorance by way of root condition; the taint of becoming is a condition for the taint of ignorance by way of root condition (a cycle). (1)

Āsavo [V 3.0196] dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – āsavā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A tainted phenomenon is a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by way of root condition: the taints that are roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (2)

Āsavo [M 3.0160] dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – kāmāsavo diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo[T 3.0183]. (3)

A tainted phenomenon is a condition for both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by way of root condition—the taint of sensual desire is a condition for the taint of wrong view, the taint of ignorance, for the associated aggregates, and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (3)

17. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – noāsavā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

17. A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by way of root condition: the non-tainted roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so on. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – noāsavā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ āsavānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon by way of root condition—non-tainted roots are a condition for their associated taints by way of root condition. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – noāsavā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsavānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by way of root condition—non-tainted roots are a condition for their associated aggregates, for the taints, and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (3)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā noāsavassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – āsavā ca noāsavā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

Both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon are a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by way of root condition—the tainted and non-tainted roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

18. Āsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – āsave ārabbha āsavā uppajjanti. (1)

18. A tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—taking taints as an object, taints arise. (1)

Āsavo [V 3.0197] dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – āsave ārabbha noāsavā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A tainted phenomenon is a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—taking taints as an object, non-tainted aggregates arise. (2)

Āsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – āsave ārabbha āsavā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A tainted phenomenon is a condition for both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—taking taints as an object, taints and their associated aggregates arise. (3)

19. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ [T 3.0184] gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ariyā noāsave pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite [M 3.0161] kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti, cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ noāsave khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, cetopariyañāṇena noāsavacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… noāsavā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

19. A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by way of object condition: giving… virtue… Uposatha observance… formerly… jhānas… having emerged from the noble paths, noble ones review the path, review the fruit, review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruit, and for advertence by way of object condition; noble ones know the abandoned defilements… the suppressed defilements… the previously accumulated defilements; reflecting on the eye… the base, the non-tainted aggregates as impermanent… displeasure arises; one sees forms with the divine eye, hears sounds with the divine ear-faculty, knows the mind of one endowed with non-tainted consciousness through mind-reading knowledge; the base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness… the base of nothingness for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… the visible-form base for eye-consciousness… the tangible base for body-consciousness… the non-tainted aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, for mind-reading knowledge, for knowledge of past lives, for knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their kamma, for knowledge of the future, and for advertence by way of object condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā…pe… taṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha āsavā uppajjanti, sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ noāsave khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha āsavā uppajjanti. (2)

A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—having given a gift… one savors and delights in that; taking that as an object, taints arise. Virtue… Uposatha observance… formerly… jhānas… the eye… the base… one savors and delights in the non-tainted aggregates; taking that as an object, taints arise. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā…pe… (dutiyagamanaṃ) noāsave khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha āsavā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—having given a gift… (as in the second case) one savors and delights in the non-tainted aggregates; taking that as an object, taints and their associated aggregates arise. (3)

20. Āsavo [V 3.0198] ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – āsave ca sampayuttake ca khandhe ārabbha āsavā uppajjanti. (1)

20. Both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon are a condition for a tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—taking taints and their associated aggregates as an object, taints arise. (1)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā noāsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – āsave ca sampayuttake ca khandhe ārabbha noāsavā khandhā uppajjanti[T 3.0185]. (2)

Both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon are a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—taking taints and their associated aggregates as an object, non-tainted aggregates arise. (2)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – āsave ca sampayuttake ca khandhe ārabbha āsavā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

Both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon are a condition for both a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by way of object condition—taking taints and their associated aggregates as an object, taints and their associated aggregates arise. (3)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

21. Āsavo [M 3.0162] dhammo āsavassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – āsave garuṃ katvā āsavā uppajjanti (tīṇi ārammaṇasadisā, garukārammaṇā kātabbā).

21. A taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon by dominance condition. Object dominance: having made the taints weighty, taints arise (the three cases are similar to the object condition; they should be made into weighty objects).

Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā…pe… phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ garuṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ noāsave khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – noāsavā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a non-taint phenomenon by dominance condition: object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: giving… morality… observance of the Uposatha… formerly… jhānas… noble paths… fruit… Nibbāna… having made Nibbāna weighty… Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit by dominance condition; the eye… the base… having made the non-taint aggregates weighty, one savors and delights in them; having made that weighty, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: a non-taint dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by dominance condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… noāsave khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā āsavā [T 3.0186] uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – noāsavā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ āsavānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon by dominance condition: object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: giving… having made the non-taint aggregates weighty, one savors and delights in them; having made that weighty, taints arise. Co-nascence dominance: a non-taint dominant factor is a condition for the associated taints by dominance condition. (2)

Noāsavo [V 3.0199] dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… noāsave khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – noāsavā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsavānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon and a non-taint phenomenon by dominance condition: object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: giving… having made the non-taint aggregates weighty, one savors and delights in them; having made that weighty, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: a non-taint dominant factor is a condition for the associated aggregates, the taints, and mind-originated matter by dominance condition. (3)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – āsave ca sampayuttake ca khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti…pe… āsavā uppajjanti (tīṇi, garukārammaṇā).

Taint and non-taint phenomena are a condition for a taint phenomenon by dominance condition. Object dominance: having made the taints and their associated aggregates weighty, one savors them… taints arise (three cases, with weighty objects).

Anantarapaccayo

Contiguity Condition

22. Āsavo [M 3.0163] dhammo āsavassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā āsavā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ āsavānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

22. A taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon by contiguity condition: preceding taints are a condition for succeeding taints by contiguity condition. (1)

Āsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā āsavā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ noāsavānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āsavā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A taint phenomenon is a condition for a non-taint phenomenon by contiguity condition: preceding taints are a condition for succeeding non-taint aggregates by contiguity condition; taints are a condition for emergence by contiguity condition. (2)

Āsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā āsavā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ āsavānaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon and a non-taint phenomenon by contiguity condition: preceding taints are a condition for succeeding taints and their associated aggregates by contiguity condition. (3)

23. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena [T 3.0187] paccayo – purimā purimā noāsavā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ noāsavānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

23. A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a non-taint phenomenon by contiguity condition: preceding non-taint aggregates are a condition for succeeding non-taint aggregates by contiguity condition; adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage… and for the attainment of fruition by contiguity condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā noāsavā [V 3.0200] khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ āsavānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā āsavānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon by contiguity condition: preceding non-taint aggregates are a condition for succeeding taints by contiguity condition; adverting is a condition for the taints by contiguity condition. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā noāsavā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ āsavānaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon and a non-taint phenomenon by contiguity condition: preceding non-taint aggregates are a condition for succeeding taints and their associated aggregates by contiguity condition. (3)

24. Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

24. Taint and non-taint phenomena are a condition for a taint phenomenon by contiguity condition… three.

Samanantarapaccayādi

Proximity Condition, etc.

25. Āsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… nava… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nava… nissayapaccayena paccayo… nava (vatthu ca dassetabbaṃ).

25. A taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon by proximity condition… by co-nascence condition… nine… by mutuality condition… nine… by dependence condition… nine (and the physical base should be shown).

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

26. Āsavo [M 3.0164] dhammo āsavassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – āsavā āsavānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo (tīṇi).

26. A taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon by decisive support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, and natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: taints are a condition for taints by decisive support condition (three).

27. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya [T 3.0188] dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

27. A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a non-taint phenomenon by decisive support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, and natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one gives a gift… generates an attainment, produces conceit, grasps a view; morality… relying on lodging, one gives a gift… splits the Saṅgha; faith… lodging is a condition for faith… for the attainment of fruition by decisive support condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo[V 3.0201], pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati, saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-taint phenomenon is a condition for a taint phenomenon by decisive support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, and natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one produces conceit, grasps a view; morality… splits the Saṅgha; faith… lodging is a condition for lust… for longing by decisive support condition. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya…pe… pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati, saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon and a taintless phenomenon by way of decisive-support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one promotes conceit, grasps a view; virtue... relying on lodging... kills living beings... splits the Saṅgha; faith... lodging is a condition for lust... for longing by way of decisive-support condition. (3)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo… tīṇi.

A taint-phenomenon and a taintless phenomenon are conditions for a taint-phenomenon by way of decisive-support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support... three.

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

28. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ [M 3.0165]…pe… vatthuṃ (evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ), phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa, vatthu noāsavānaṃ [T 3.0189] khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

28. A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taintless phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: the eye... the object (to be expanded thus), the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness; the base is a condition for taintless aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha āsavā uppajjanti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu āsavānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one savors and delights in the eye... the object, and taking that as an object, taints arise. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for taints by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati[V 3.0202], taṃ ārabbha āsavā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu āsavānañca āsavasampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon and a taintless phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one savors and delights in the eye... the object, and taking that as an object, taints and associated aggregates arise. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for taints and aggregates associated with taints by way of pre-nascence condition. (3)

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition

29. Āsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā āsavā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

29. A taint-phenomenon is a condition for a taintless phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition: post-nascent taints are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā noāsavā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taintless phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition: post-nascent taintless aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā noāsavassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā āsavā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A taint-phenomenon and a taintless phenomenon are conditions for a taintless phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition: post-nascent taints and associated aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

30. Āsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo… nava.

30. A taint-phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon by way of repetition condition... nine.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

31. Noāsavo [T 3.0190][M 3.0166] dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – noāsavā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – noāsavā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

31. A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taintless phenomenon by way of kamma condition: co-nascent, and at different moments. Co-nascent: taintless volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... At different moments: taintless volition is a condition for the resultant aggregates and kamma-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – noāsavā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ āsavānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon by way of kamma condition: taintless volition is a condition for the associated taints by way of kamma condition. (2)

Noāsavo [V 3.0203] dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – noāsavā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsavānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon and a taintless phenomenon by way of kamma condition: taintless volition is a condition for the associated aggregates, taints, and mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (3)

Vipākāhārapaccayā

Result and Nutriment Conditions

32. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ, āhārapaccayena paccayo – noāsavā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

32. A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taintless phenomenon by way of result condition… one; by way of nutriment condition—taintless nutriments are a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of nutriment condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… physical food is a condition for this body by way of nutriment condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – noāsavā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ āsavānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon by way of nutriment condition—taintless nutriments are a condition for the associated taints by way of nutriment condition. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – noāsavā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ [T 3.0191] āsavānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taint-phenomenon and a taintless phenomenon by way of nutriment condition—taintless nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates, taints, and mind-originated material phenomena by way of nutriment condition. (3)

Indriyapaccayādi

Faculty Condition, etc.

33. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – noāsavā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ [M 3.0167] indriyapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi… jhānapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi… maggapaccayena paccayo… nava… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… nava.

33. A taintless phenomenon is a condition for a taintless phenomenon by way of faculty condition—taintless faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of faculty condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… the eye faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness… the body faculty is a condition for body-consciousness… the materiality-life faculty is a condition for kamma-originated material phenomena by way of faculty condition… three… by way of jhāna condition… three… by way of path condition… nine… by way of association condition… nine.

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

34. Āsavo [V 3.0204] dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – āsavā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – āsavā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

34. A taint-phenomenon is a condition for a taintless phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent, post-nascent. Co-nascent: taints are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: taints are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

35. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – noāsavā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu noāsavānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – noāsavā khandhā purejātassa [T 3.0192] imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

35. A non-āsava phenomenon is a condition for a non-āsava phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent, pre-nascent, and post-nascent. Co-nascent: non-āsava aggregates are a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of dissociation condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… etc.… aggregates are a condition for the base by way of dissociation condition, the base is a condition for the aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness… etc.… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness… etc.… the base is a condition for non-āsava aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: non-āsava aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu āsavānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-āsava phenomenon is a condition for an āsava phenomenon by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: the base is a condition for the āsavas by way of dissociation condition. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu āsavānaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-āsava phenomenon is a condition for an āsava phenomenon and a non-āsava phenomenon by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: the base is a condition for the āsavas and their associated aggregates by way of dissociation condition. (3)

36. Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā noāsavassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – āsavā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – āsavā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

36. An āsava phenomenon and a non-āsava phenomenon are a condition for a non-āsava phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent, post-nascent. Co-nascent: āsavas and their associated aggregates are a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: āsavas and their associated aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

37. Āsavo [M 3.0168] dhammo āsavassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – kāmāsavo diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa atthipaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). (1)

37. An āsava phenomenon is a condition for an āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—the āsava of sensual desire is a condition for the āsava of views and the āsava of ignorance by way of presence condition (a cycle). (1)

Āsavo [V 3.0205] dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – āsavā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – āsavā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An āsava phenomenon is a condition for a non-āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—co-nascent and post-nascent. Co-nascent: āsavas are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced materiality by way of presence condition. Post-nascent: āsavas are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of presence condition. (2)

Āsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – kāmāsavo diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena [T 3.0193] paccayo (cakkaṃ). (3)

An āsava phenomenon is a condition for an āsava phenomenon and a non-āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—the āsava of sensual desire is a condition for the āsava of views, the āsava of ignorance, their associated aggregates, and mind-produced materiality by way of presence condition (a cycle). (3)

38. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – noāsavo eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu noāsavānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – noāsavā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

38. A non-āsava phenomenon is a condition for a non-āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, and faculty. Co-nascent: one non-āsava aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates… etc.… (up to non-percipient beings). Pre-nascent: the eye… etc.… the base is seen as impermanent… etc.… grief arises; with the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear element, one hears sounds. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… etc.… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness… etc.… the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness… etc.… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness… etc.… the base is a condition for the non-āsava aggregates by way of presence condition. Post-nascent: the non-āsava aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of presence condition; physical nutriment is a condition for this body by way of presence condition; the material life faculty is a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of presence condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātā – noāsavā khandhā āsavānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha āsavā uppajjanti, vatthu āsavānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-āsava phenomenon is a condition for an āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—co-nascent and pre-nascent. Co-nascent: non-āsava aggregates are a condition for the āsavas by way of presence condition. Pre-nascent: the eye… etc.… one delights in and enjoys the base; with that as object, āsavas arise; the base is a condition for the āsavas by way of presence condition. (2)

Noāsavo [M 3.0169] dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – noāsavo eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ āsavānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… (cakkaṃ). (3)

A non-āsava phenomenon is a condition for an āsava phenomenon and a non-āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—co-nascent and pre-nascent. Co-nascent: one non-āsava aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates, the āsavas, and mind-produced materiality by way of presence condition… etc.… two aggregates… etc.… (a cycle). (3)

39. Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa dhammassa atthipaccayena [T 3.0194] paccayo – sahajātaṃ[V 3.0206], purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – kāmāsavo ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa atthipaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). Kāmāsavo ca vatthu ca diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa atthipaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). (1)

39. An āsava phenomenon and a non-āsava phenomenon are a condition for an āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—co-nascent and pre-nascent. Co-nascent: the āsava of sensual desire and its associated aggregates are a condition for the āsava of views and the āsava of ignorance by way of presence condition (a cycle). The āsava of sensual desire and the base are a condition for the āsava of views and the āsava of ignorance by way of presence condition (a cycle). (1)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā noāsavassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – noāsavo eko khandho ca āsavā ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā – āsavā mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; āsavā ca vatthu ca noāsavānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – āsavā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – āsavā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An āsava phenomenon and a non-āsava phenomenon are a condition for a non-āsava phenomenon by way of presence condition—co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, and faculty. Co-nascent: one non-āsava aggregate and the āsavas are a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-produced materiality by way of presence condition. Co-nascent: āsavas and the great elements are a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of presence condition; āsavas and the base are a condition for non-āsava aggregates by way of presence condition. Post-nascent: āsavas and physical nutriment are a condition for this body by way of presence condition. Post-nascent: āsavas and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of presence condition. (2)

Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – noāsavo eko khandho ca kāmāsavo ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe… (cakkaṃ). Sahajāto – kāmāsavo ca vatthu ca diṭṭhāsavassa avijjāsavassa sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). (3)

Tainted and non-tainted phenomena are a condition for a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by presence condition—co-nascence and pre-nascence. Co-nascent: one non-tainted aggregate and the taint of sensual desire are a condition for the three aggregates, the taint of views, the taint of ignorance, and mind-produced matter by presence condition… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… (cycle). Co-nascent: the taint of sensual desire and the physical basis are a condition for the taint of views, the taint of ignorance, and the associated aggregates by presence condition (cycle). (3)

Pure

40. Hetuyā [T 3.0195] satta, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe nava, nissaye nava, upanissaye [M 3.0170] nava, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre tīṇi…pe… magge nava, sampayutte nava, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā nava, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate nava.

40. By root condition, seven; by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, nine; by contiguity condition, nine; by immediate contiguity condition, nine; by co-nascence condition, nine; by reciprocity condition, nine; by dependence condition, nine; by decisive support condition, nine; by pre-nascence condition, three; by post-nascence condition, three; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, three; by result condition, one; by nutriment condition, three… and so on… by path condition, nine; by association condition, nine; by dissociation condition, five; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, nine; by disappearance condition, nine; by non-disappearance condition, nine.

Paccanīyuddhāro

The Section on Negation

41. Āsavo [V 3.0207] dhammo āsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

41. A tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition. (1)

Āsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A tainted phenomenon is a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by post-nascence condition. (2)

Āsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition. (3)

42. Noāsavo dhammo noāsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

42. A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by pre-nascence condition… by post-nascence condition… by kamma condition… by nutriment condition… by faculty condition. (1)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena [T 3.0196] paccayo. (2)

A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by pre-nascence condition. (2)

Noāsavo dhammo āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-tainted phenomenon is a condition for a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by pre-nascence condition. (3)

43. Āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

43. Tainted and non-tainted phenomena are a condition for a tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition. (1)

Āsavo [M 3.0171] ca noāsavo ca dhammā noāsavassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Tainted and non-tainted phenomena are a condition for a non-tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by post-nascence condition. (2)

Āsavo [V 3.0208] ca noāsavo ca dhammā āsavassa ca noāsavassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Tainted and non-tainted phenomena are a condition for a tainted phenomenon and a non-tainted phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition. (3)

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. The Section on Dependence

Hetupaccayo

Root condition.

47. Sāsavaṃ [M 3.0172][V 3.0209] dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – sāsavaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

47. A tainted phenomenon arises dependent on a tainted phenomenon by root condition – Dependent on one tainted aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality [arise]…pe… Dependent on two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… Dependent on aggregates, the base [arises]; dependent on the base, aggregates [arise]; dependent on one great element…pe… dependent on great elements, mind-produced materiality, kamma-produced materiality, and derived materiality [arise]. (1)

Anāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anāsavaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

An untainted phenomenon arises dependent on an untainted phenomenon by root condition – Dependent on one untainted aggregate, three aggregates [arise]…pe… Dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Anāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anāsave khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A tainted phenomenon arises dependent on an untainted phenomenon by root condition – Dependent on untainted aggregates, mind-produced materiality [arises]. (2)

Anāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo ca anāsavo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anāsavaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

Tainted and untainted phenomena arise dependent on an untainted phenomenon by root condition – Dependent on one untainted aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality [arise]…pe… Dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (3)

Sāsavañca anāsavañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anāsave khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A tainted phenomenon arises dependent on tainted and untainted phenomena by root condition – Dependent on untainted aggregates and great elements, mind-produced materiality [arises]. (1)

(Yathā [T 3.0198] cūḷantaraduke lokiyadukaṃ evaṃ kātabbaṃ ninnānākaraṇaṃ.)

As with the Minor Intermediate Dyad, so the Mundane Dyad should be treated, without any difference.

Sāsavadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tainted Dyad is concluded.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition.

48. Āsavasampayuttaṃ [V 3.0210] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – āsavasampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

48. A state associated with taints arises dependent on a state associated with taints by root condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with taints, three aggregates arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. (1)

Āsavasampayuttaṃ [M 3.0173] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – āsavasampayutte khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, domanassasahagate khandhe paṭicca moho cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (2)

A state dissociated from taints arises dependent on a state associated with taints by root condition. Dependent on the aggregates associated with taints, mind-produced materiality arises; dependent on the aggregates accompanied by displeasure, delusion and mind-produced materiality arise. (2)

Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto ca āsavavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – āsavasampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… domanassasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā moho cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

States associated with taints and states dissociated from taints arise dependent on a state associated with taints by root condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with taints, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by displeasure, three aggregates, delusion, and mind-produced materiality arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. (3)

49. Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – āsavavippayuttaṃ [V 3.0211] ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā, tayo [T 3.0199] mahābhūte paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ, dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

49. A state dissociated from taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from taints by root condition. Dependent on one aggregate dissociated from taints, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. Dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, mind-produced materiality arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking [...], dependent on the aggregates, the base arises; dependent on the base, the aggregates arise; dependent on one great element, three great elements arise; dependent on three great elements, one great element arises; dependent on two great elements, two great elements arise; dependent on the great elements, mind-produced materiality, kamma-produced materiality, and derived materiality arise. (1)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā. (2)

A state associated with taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from taints by root condition. Dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, the associated aggregates arise. (2)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto ca āsavavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (3)

States associated with taints and states dissociated from taints arise dependent on a state dissociated from taints by root condition. Dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, the associated aggregates and mind-produced materiality arise. (3)

50. Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca mohañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

50. A state associated with taints arises dependent on both a state associated with taints and a state dissociated from taints by root condition. Dependent on one aggregate and delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, three aggregates arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. (1)

Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – āsavasampayutte khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, domanassasahagate vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A state dissociated from taints arises dependent on both a state associated with taints and a state dissociated from taints by root condition. Dependent on the aggregates associated with taints and the great elements, mind-produced materiality arises; dependent on the aggregates and delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, mind-produced materiality arises. (2)

Āsavasampayuttañca [M 3.0174] āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto ca āsavavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca mohañca paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ, dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

States associated with taints and states dissociated from taints arise dependent on both a state associated with taints and a state dissociated from taints by root condition. Dependent on one aggregate and delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality arise; dependent on two aggregates [...]. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition.

51. Āsavasampayuttaṃ [T 3.0200][V 3.0212] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – āsavasampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

51. A state associated with taints arises dependent on a state associated with taints by object condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with taints, three aggregates arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. (1)

Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – domanassasahagate vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca moho. (2)

A state dissociated from taints arises dependent on a state associated with taints by object condition. Dependent on the aggregates accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, delusion arises. (2)

Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto ca āsavavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti ārammaṇapaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā moho ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

States associated with taints and states dissociated from taints arise dependent on a state associated with taints by object condition. Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, three aggregates and delusion arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. (3)

52. Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – āsavavippayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. (1) Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā. (2)

52. A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from the taints by object condition. Dependent on one aggregate dissociated from the taints, three aggregates arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on... At the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on... dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates arise. (1) A state associated with the taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from the taints by object condition. Dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, the associated aggregates arise. (2)

Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca mohañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

A state associated with the taints arises dependent on both a state associated with the taints and a state dissociated from the taints by object condition. Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness, and on delusion, three aggregates arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on.... (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

53. Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā… tīṇi.

53. A state associated with the taints arises dependent on a state associated with the taints by dominance condition... three.

Āsavavippayuttaṃ [M 3.0175][V 3.0213] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto [T 3.0201] dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – āsavavippayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… domanassasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from the taints by dominance condition: dependent on one aggregate dissociated from the taints, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on... mind-originated matter arises dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure; dependent on one great element... and so on... dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter and derived matter arise. (1)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā. (2)

A state associated with the taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from the taints by dominance condition: associated aggregates arise dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure. (2)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto ca āsavavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti adhipatipaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (3)

States both associated with and dissociated from the taints arise dependent on a state dissociated from the taints by dominance condition: the associated aggregates and mind-originated matter arise dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure. (3)

54. Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca mohañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

54. A state associated with the taints arises dependent on a state associated with the taints and a state dissociated from the taints by dominance condition. Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by displeasure, and on delusion, three aggregates arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on.... (1)

Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – āsavasampayutte khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, domanassasahagate khandhe ca mohañca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state both associated with and dissociated from the taints by dominance condition: mind-originated matter arises dependent on the aggregates associated with the taints and the great elements; mind-originated matter arises dependent on the aggregates accompanied by displeasure, and on delusion. (2)

Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto ca āsavavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti adhipatipaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca mohañca paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

States both associated with and dissociated from the taints arise dependent on a state associated with the taints and a state dissociated from the taints by dominance condition. Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by displeasure, and on delusion, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on.... (3)

(Evaṃ sabbe paccayā vitthāretabbā. Saṃkhittaṃ.)

(Thus, all conditions should be explained in detail. In brief.)

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Progression of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Enumeration Section

Suddhaṃ

The Pure

55. Hetuyā [T 3.0202][V 3.0214] nava, ārammaṇe cha, adhipatiyā nava, anantare cha, samanantare cha, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe cha, nissaye nava, upanissaye cha, purejāte cha, āsevane cha, kamme nava, vipāke ekaṃ[M 3.0176], āhāre nava, indriye nava, jhāne nava, magge nava, sampayutte cha, vippayutte nava, atthiyā nava, natthiyā cha, vigate cha, avigate nava.

55. By root condition, nine; by object condition, six; by dominance condition, nine; by contiguity condition, six; by immediate contiguity condition, six; by co-nascence condition, nine; by mutuality condition, six; by support condition, nine; by decisive support condition, six; by pre-nascence condition, six; by repetition condition, six; by kamma condition, nine; by result condition, one; by nutriment condition, nine; by faculty condition, nine; by jhāna condition, nine; by path condition, nine; by association condition, six; by dissociation condition, nine; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, six; by disappearance condition, six; by non-disappearance condition, nine.

Anulomaṃ.

Positive Method

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. The Negative Method of Conditions

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. Analysis Section

Nahetupaccayo

Non-Root Condition

56. Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

56. A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state associated with the taints by non-root condition: delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness. (1)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ āsavavippayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva āsaññasattā). (1)

A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from the taints by non-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate dissociated from the taints, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking... and so on... (as far as the non-percipient beings). (1)

Naārammaṇapaccayo

Non-Object Condition

57. Āsavasampayuttaṃ [V 3.0215] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – āsavasampayutte khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

57. A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state associated with the taints by non-object condition: mind-originated matter arises dependent on aggregates associated with the taints. (1)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – āsavavippayutte khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe [T 3.0203] paṭicca vatthu, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). (1)

A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state dissociated from the taints by non-object condition: mind-originated matter arises dependent on aggregates dissociated from the taints; mind-originated matter arises dependent on delusion accompanied by displeasure, doubt, or restlessness; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on... dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis arises; dependent on one great element... and so on... (as far as the non-percipient beings). (1)

Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – āsavasampayutte khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, domanassasahagate vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A state dissociated from the taints arises dependent on a state associated with the taints and a state dissociated from the taints by non-object condition: mind-originated matter arises dependent on aggregates associated with the taints and the great elements; mind-originated matter arises dependent on aggregates accompanied by displeasure, doubt, and restlessness, and on delusion. (1)

Naadhipatipaccayo

Non-Dominance Condition

58. Āsavasampayuttaṃ [M 3.0177] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

58. A state associated with the taints arises dependent on a state associated with the taints, not by way of dominance condition (in brief).

Napurejātapaccayādi

Not by way of Pre-nascence Condition, and so on

59. Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe āsavasampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

59. A state associated with the taints arises dependent on a state associated with the taints, not by way of pre-nascence condition: in the immaterial realm, dependent on one aggregate associated with the taints, three aggregates arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on.... (1)

Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho, āsavasampayutte khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from the taints arises in dependence on a phenomenon associated with the taints, not by way of prenascence condition—in the immaterial realm, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises in dependence on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness; mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on aggregates associated with the taints. (2)

Āsavasampayuttaṃ [V 3.0216] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto ca āsavavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti napurejātapaccayā – arūpe vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā moho ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

Phenomena associated with the taints and dissociated from the taints arise in dependence on a phenomenon associated with the taints, not by way of prenascence condition—in the immaterial realm, three aggregates and delusion arise in dependence on one aggregate accompanied by doubt and restlessness... two aggregates.... (3)

60. Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe āsavavippayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… āsavavippayutte [T 3.0204] khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). (1)

60. A phenomenon dissociated from the taints arises in dependence on a phenomenon dissociated from the taints, not by way of prenascence condition—in the immaterial realm, three aggregates arise in dependence on one aggregate dissociated from the taints... two aggregates...; mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on aggregates dissociated from the taints; mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on delusion accompanied by sorrow, doubt, and restlessness; at the moment of rebirth-linking... (down to non-percipient beings). (1)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā. (2)

A phenomenon associated with the taints arises in dependence on a phenomenon dissociated from the taints, not by way of prenascence condition—in the immaterial realm, the associated aggregates arise in dependence on delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness. (2)

61. Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca mohañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe…. (1)

61. A phenomenon associated with the taints arises in dependence on phenomena both associated with and dissociated from the taints, not by way of prenascence condition—in the immaterial realm, three aggregates arise in dependence on one aggregate accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and delusion... two aggregates.... (1)

Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – āsavasampayutte khandhe ca mahābhūte ca [M 3.0178] paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, domanassasahagate vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from the taints arises in dependence on phenomena both associated with and dissociated from the taints, not by way of prenascence condition—mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on the aggregates associated with the taints and the great elements; mind-originated materiality arises in dependence on aggregates accompanied by sorrow, doubt, and restlessness, and delusion. (2)

(Napacchājātapaccayā nava, naāsevanapaccayā nava.)

(Not by way of postnascence condition, nine; not by way of repetition condition, nine.)

Nakammapaccayādi

Not by Way of Kamma Condition, and so on.

62. Āsavasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – āsavasampayutte khandhe paṭicca sampayuttakā cetanā. (1)

62. A phenomenon associated with the taints arises in dependence on a phenomenon associated with the taints, not by way of kamma condition—associated volition arises in dependence on the aggregates associated with the taints. (1)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ [V 3.0217] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – āsavavippayutte khandhe paṭicca vippayuttakā cetanā. (1)

A phenomenon dissociated from the taints arises in dependence on a phenomenon dissociated from the taints, not by way of kamma condition—dissociated volition arises in dependence on aggregates dissociated from the taints. (1)

Āsavavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – domanassasahagataṃ vicikicchāsahagataṃ [T 3.0205] uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā cetanā. (2)

A phenomenon associated with the taints arises in dependence on a phenomenon dissociated from the taints, not by way of kamma condition—associated volition arises in dependence on delusion accompanied by sorrow, doubt, and restlessness. (2)

Āsavasampayuttañca āsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – domanassasahagate vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca paṭicca sampayuttakā cetanā… navipākapaccayā… naāhārapaccayā… naindriyapaccayā… najhānapaccayā… namaggapaccayā… nasampayuttapaccayā… navippayuttapaccayā… nonatthipaccayā… novigatapaccayā.

A phenomenon associated with the taints arises in dependence on phenomena both associated with and dissociated from the taints, not by way of kamma condition—associated volition arises in dependence on aggregates accompanied by sorrow, doubt, and restlessness, and delusion... not by way of resultant condition... not by way of nutriment condition... not by way of faculty condition... not by way of jhāna condition... not by way of path condition... not by way of association condition... not by way of dissociation condition... not by way of absence condition... not by way of disappearance condition.

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Chapter on Enumeration

Suddhaṃ

Pure

63. Nahetuyā dve, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava, naanantare tīṇi, nasamanantare tīṇi, naaññamaññe tīṇi, naupanissaye tīṇi, napurejāte satta, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava, nakamme cattāri, navipāke nava, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye ekaṃ, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte cha, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

63. Not by way of root condition—two; not by way of object condition—three; not by way of decisive support condition—nine; not by way of contiguity condition—three; not by way of immediate contiguity condition—three; not by way of mutuality condition—three; not by way of strong support condition—three; not by way of prenascence condition—seven; not by way of postnascence condition—nine; not by way of repetition condition—nine; not by way of kamma condition—four; not by way of resultant condition—nine; not by way of nutriment condition—one; not by way of faculty condition—one; not by way of jhāna condition—one; not by way of path condition—one; not by way of association condition—three; not by way of dissociation condition—six; not by way of absence condition—three; not by way of disappearance condition—three.

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. Conditional Relations and Their Negations

Hetudukaṃ

Root Dyad

64. Hetupaccayā [M 3.0179][V 3.0218] naārammaṇe tīṇi…pe… napurejāte cha…pe… navipāke nava…pe… nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte cattāri, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

64. By way of root condition: not by way of object condition, three; ... not by way of prenascence condition, six; ... not by way of resultant condition, nine; ... not by way of association condition, three; not by way of dissociation condition, four; not by way of absence condition, three; not by way of disappearance condition, three.

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

Direct-Reverse Order

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Reverse-Direct Order of Conditions

Nahetudukaṃ

Non-Root Dyad

65. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe dve, anantare dve, samanantare dve…pe… kamme dve, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre dve…pe… magge ekaṃ[T 3.0206], sampayutte dve, vippayutte dve…pe… avigate dve.

65. By way of non-root condition: by way of object condition, two; by way of contiguity condition, two; by way of immediate contiguity condition, two; ... by way of kamma condition, two; by way of resultant condition, one; by way of nutriment condition, two; ... by way of path condition, one; by way of association condition, two; by way of dissociation condition, two; ... by way of non-disappearance condition, two.

2. Sahajātavāro
