Thus, the other two enumerations—the co-nascence section, the condition section, the support section, the conjunction section, and the association section—are similar to the dependent section.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

112. Gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca dhammo ganthassa ceva ganthasampayuttassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ ganthānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

112. A state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters is a condition for a state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters by way of root condition—fetters and states associated with fetters, being roots, are a condition for associated fetters by way of root condition. (1)

Gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca dhammo ganthasampayuttassa ceva no ca ganthassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters is a condition for a state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter by way of root condition—fetters and states associated with fetters, being roots, are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (2)

Gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca dhammo ganthassa ceva ganthasampayuttassa ca ganthasampayuttassa [T 3.0344] ceva [V 3.0362] no ca ganthassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ ganthānañca hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters is a condition for a state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters, and for a state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter, by way of root condition—fetters and states associated with fetters, being roots, are a condition for the associated aggregates and the fetters by way of root condition. (3)

113. Ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho dhammo ganthasampayuttassa ceva no ca ganthassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ ganthānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

113. A state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter is a condition for a state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter by way of root condition—states associated with fetters but not fetters, being roots, are a condition for associated fetters by way of root condition. (1)

Ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho dhammo ganthassa ceva ganthasampayuttassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ ganthānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter is a condition for a state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters by way of root condition—states associated with fetters but not fetters, being roots, are a condition for associated fetters by way of root condition. (2)

Ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho dhammo ganthassa ceva ganthasampayuttassa ca ganthasampayuttassa ceva no ca ganthassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena [M 3.0296] paccayo – ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ ganthānañca hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter is a condition for a state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters, and for a state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter, by way of root condition—states associated with fetters but not fetters, being roots, are a condition for the associated aggregates and the fetters by way of root condition. (3)

114. Gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho ca dhammā ganthassa ceva ganthasampayuttassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

114. States that are both fetters and associated with fetters, and states that are associated with fetters but are not fetters, are a condition for a state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters by way of root condition—fetters and states associated with fetters, and states associated with fetters but not fetters, being roots, are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (1)

Gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho ca dhammā ganthasampayuttassa ceva no ca ganthassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

States that are both fetters and associated with fetters, and states that are associated with fetters but are not fetters, are a condition for a state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter by way of root condition—fetters and states associated with fetters, and states associated with fetters but not fetters, being roots, are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (2)

Gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho ca dhammā ganthassa [T 3.0345] ceva ganthasampayuttassa ca ganthasampayuttassa ceva no ca ganthassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ ganthānañca hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

States that are both fetters and associated with fetters, and states that are associated with fetters but are not fetters, are a condition for a state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters, and for a state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter, by way of root condition—fetters and states associated with fetters, and states associated with fetters but not fetters, being roots, are a condition for the associated aggregates and the fetters by way of root condition. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayādi

Object Condition, etc.

115. Gantho [V 3.0363] ceva ganthasampayutto ca dhammo ganthassa ceva ganthasampayuttassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ganthe ārabbha ganthā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) ganthe ārabbha ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) ganthe ārabbha ganthā ca ganthasampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

115. A state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters is a condition for a state that is both a fetter and associated with fetters by way of object condition—taking a fetter as object, fetters arise. (The root should be elaborated.) Taking a fetter as object, aggregates that are associated with fetters but are not fetters arise. (The root should be elaborated.) Taking a fetter as object, fetters and aggregates associated with fetters arise. (3)

Ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho dhammo ganthasampayuttassa ceva no ca ganthassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ganthasampayutte ceva no ca ganthe khandhe ārabbha ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) ganthasampayutte ceva no ca ganthe khandhe ārabbha ganthā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) ganthasampayutte ceva no ca ganthe khandhe ārabbha ganthā ca ganthasampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter is a condition for a state that is associated with fetters but is not a fetter by way of object condition—taking aggregates that are associated with fetters but not fetters as object, aggregates that are associated with fetters but not fetters arise. (The root should be elaborated.) Taking aggregates that are associated with fetters but not fetters as object, fetters arise. (The root should be elaborated.) Taking aggregates that are associated with fetters but not fetters as object, fetters and aggregates associated with fetters arise. (3)

(Evaṃ itarepi tīṇi pañhā kātabbā ārammaṇasadisaṃyeva. Adhipatiyāpi anantarepi upanissayepi vibhāgo natthi.)

Thus, the other three questions should be elaborated in the same way as for the object condition. There is no distinction with regard to predominance, immediacy, or decisive support.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Direct Order of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. The Section on Enumeration

Suddhaṃ

Simple.

116. Hetuyā [M 3.0297] nava, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe nava, nissaye nava, upanissaye nava, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi[T 3.0346], āhāre tīṇi, indriye tīṇi, jhāne tīṇi, magge nava, sampayutte nava, atthiyā nava, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate nava.

116. By root condition, nine; by object condition, nine; by predominance condition, nine; by contiguity condition, nine; by immediate contiguity condition, nine; by co-nascence condition, nine; by reciprocity condition, nine; by dependence condition, nine; by decisive support condition, nine; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, three; by nutriment condition, three; by faculty condition, three; by jhāna condition, three; by path condition, nine; by association condition, nine; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, nine; by disappearance condition, nine; by non-disappearance condition, nine.

(Arūpaṃyeva paccayaṃ, ekekassa tīṇi tīṇi kātabbā. Ārammaṇañca sahajātañca upanissayañca navasupi parivattetabbaṃ. Evaṃ pañhāvārepi sabbaṃ kātabbaṃ.)

The immaterial is indeed the condition; for each, three should be done. The object, co-nascence, and decisive support—these should be applied in all nine cases. Thus, everything should be done in this way in the question section as well.

Ganthaganthasampayuttadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Bonds and What is Conjoined with Bonds is completed.

31. Ganthavippayuttaganthaniyadukaṃ

31. The Dyad of What is Disjoined from Bonds but Liable to Bonds

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. The Section on Dependent Origination

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition.

117. Ganthavippayuttaganthaniyaṃ [V 3.0364] dhammaṃ paṭicca ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – ganthavippayuttaṃ ganthaniyaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… (yathā cūḷantaraduke lokiyadukaṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ ninnānākaraṇaṃ).

117. A state disjoined from bonds but liable to bonds arises dependent on a state disjoined from bonds but liable to bonds through a root condition: dependent on one aggregate disjoined from bonds but liable to bonds, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise...; dependent on two aggregates...; at the moment of rebirth-linking...; dependent on one great element... (This should be elaborated like the worldly dyad in the minor intermediate dyad, without any variation).

Ganthavippayuttaganthaniyadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of What is Disjoined from Bonds but Liable to Bonds is completed.

Ganthagocchakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Group of Bonds is completed.

6-7. Oghayogagocchakaṃ

6-7. The Group of Floods and Yokes

Root Condition.

1. Nīvaraṇaṃ [M 3.0298][V 3.0366] dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ thīnamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ (syā.) uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ kukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ kukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (1)

1. A hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state through a root condition: Dependent on the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise; dependent on the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of restlessness and ignorance arise; dependent on the hindrance of ill will, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise; dependent on the hindrance of ill will, the hindrances of restlessness and ignorance arise; dependent on the hindrance of ill will, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, remorse, and ignorance arise; dependent on the hindrance of ill will, the hindrances of restlessness, remorse, and ignorance arise; dependent on the hindrance of doubt, the hindrance of restlessness arises; dependent on the hindrance of restlessness, the hindrance of ignorance arises. (1)

Nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇe paṭicca [T 3.0348] sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (2)

A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state through a root condition: dependent on the hindrances, the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter arise. (2)

Nīvaraṇaṃ [V 3.0367] dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ sampayuttakā ca khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ (cakkaṃ). (3)

A hindrance state and a non-hindrance state arise dependent on a hindrance state through a root condition: dependent on the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance, along with the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter, arise (cycle). (3)

2. Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

2. A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a non-hindrance state through a root condition: dependent on one non-hindrance aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise...; dependent on two aggregates...; at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (1)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇe khandhe paṭicca nīvaraṇā. (2)

A hindrance state arises dependent on a non-hindrance state through a root condition: dependent on the non-hindrance aggregates, hindrances arise. (2)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā nīvaraṇā ca cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

A hindrance state and a non-hindrance state arise dependent on a non-hindrance state through a root condition: dependent on one non-hindrance aggregate, three aggregates, hindrances, and mind-produced matter arise...; dependent on two aggregates.... (3)

3. Nīvaraṇañca [M 3.0299] nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ). (1)

3. A hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by root condition: dependent on the hindrance of sensual desire and the associated aggregates, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise (cycle). (1)

Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca nīvaraṇañca paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… nīvaraṇe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by root condition: dependent on one non-hindrance aggregate and a hindrance, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]; dependent on the hindrances and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises. (2)

Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca paṭicca tayo khandhā thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… (cakkaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ). (3)

Hindrance states and non-hindrance states arise dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by root condition: dependent on one non-hindrance aggregate and the hindrance of sensual desire, three aggregates, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise [...]; dependent on two aggregates [...]. (cycle. Abbreviated.) (3)

5. Nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (1)

5. A hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state by non-root condition: the hindrance of ignorance arises dependent on the hindrance of doubt; the hindrance of ignorance arises dependent on the hindrance of restlessness. (1)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). (1)

A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a non-hindrance state by non-root condition: dependent on one rootless, non-hindrance aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise…pe… two…pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking…pe… (up to the non-percipient beings). (1)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ [M 3.0300] dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (2)

A hindrance state arises dependent on a non-hindrance state by non-root condition: the hindrance of ignorance arises dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and the aggregates accompanied by restlessness. (2)

6. Nīvaraṇañca [V 3.0369] nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchānīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (1)

6. A hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by non-root condition: the hindrance of ignorance arises dependent on the hindrance of doubt and its associated aggregates; the hindrance of ignorance arises dependent on the hindrance of restlessness and its associated aggregates. (1)

Naārammaṇapaccayādi

Non-Object Condition, etc.

7. Nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – nīvaraṇe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

7. A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state by non-object condition: dependent on a hindrance, mind-produced matter arises. (1)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – nonīvaraṇe khandhe [T 3.0350] paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). (1)

A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a non-hindrance state by non-object condition: dependent on non-hindrance aggregates, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… (up to the non-percipient beings). (1)

Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – nīvaraṇe ca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ)… naadhipatipaccayā… naanantarapaccayā… nasamanantarapaccayā… naaññamaññapaccayā… naupanissayapaccayā.

A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by non-object condition: dependent on a hindrance and its associated aggregates, mind-produced matter arises (abbreviated)… by non-dominance condition… by non-contiguity condition… by non-immediate contiguity condition… by non-mutuality condition… by non-decisive support condition.

Napurejātapaccayo

Non-Prenascence Condition

8. Nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, arūpe kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, arūpe vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, arūpe uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (1)

8. A hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state by non-prenascence condition: in the immaterial sphere, dependent on the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of sloth-torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise; in the immaterial sphere, dependent on the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of restlessness and ignorance arise; in the immaterial sphere, dependent on the hindrance of doubt, the hindrances of restlessness and ignorance arise; in the immaterial sphere, dependent on the hindrance of restlessness, the hindrance of ignorance arises. (1)

Nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe nīvaraṇe paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā, nīvaraṇe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (Avasesā pañhā sabbe vitthāretabbā. Arūpaṃ paṭhamaṃ kātabbaṃ, rūpaṃ pacchā yathā labhati.)

A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state by non-prenascence condition: in the immaterial sphere, dependent on a hindrance, associated aggregates arise; dependent on a hindrance, mind-produced matter arises. (All remaining questions should be elaborated. The immaterial should be treated first, the material afterwards, as it is obtained.)

9. Nīvaraṇañca [M 3.0301][V 3.0370] nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe nonīvaraṇe khandhe ca kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ). (1)

9. A hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by non-prenascence condition: in the immaterial sphere, dependent on non-hindrance aggregates and the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of sloth-torpor and restlessness arise (cycle). (1)

Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca nīvaraṇe ca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… nīvaraṇe ca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, nīvaraṇe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A non-hindrance state arises dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by non-prenascence condition: in the immaterial sphere, dependent on one non-hindrance aggregate and a hindrance, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… dependent on a hindrance and its associated aggregates, mind-produced matter arises; dependent on a hindrance and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises. (2)

Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo [T 3.0351] ca dhammā uppajjanti napurejātapaccayā – arūpe nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca paṭicca tayo khandhā thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ). (3)

Hindrance states and non-hindrance states arise dependent on a hindrance state and a non-hindrance state by non-prenascence condition: in the immaterial sphere, dependent on one non-hindrance aggregate and the hindrance of sensual desire, three aggregates, the hindrances of sloth-torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise (cycle. Abbreviated). (3)

13. A hindrance state conditions a hindrance state by root condition... three.

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… (yāva ajjhattikā mahābhūtā), vatthuṃ paccayā nonīvaraṇā khandhā. (1)

A non-hindrance state conditions a non-hindrance state by root condition: one non-hindrance aggregate conditions three aggregates and mind-originated materiality... (up to the internal great elements); the base conditions the non-hindrance aggregates. (1)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nīvaraṇo dhammo [T 3.0352] uppajjati hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇe khandhe paccayā nīvaraṇā, vatthuṃ paccayā nīvaraṇā. (2)

A non-hindrance state conditions a hindrance state by root condition: the non-hindrance aggregates condition the hindrances; the base conditions the hindrances. (2)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā nīvaraṇā ca cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vatthuṃ paccayā nīvaraṇā, mahābhūte paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā. (3)

A non-hindrance state conditions both hindrance and non-hindrance states by root condition: one non-hindrance aggregate conditions three aggregates, the hindrances, and mind-originated materiality... two aggregates... the base conditions the hindrances; the great elements condition mind-originated materiality; the base conditions the hindrances and associated aggregates. (3)

14. Nīvaraṇañca [V 3.0372] nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paccayā nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paccayā thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ). Kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca vatthuñca paccayā thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ). (1)

14. Both a hindrance and a non-hindrance state condition a hindrance state by root condition: the sensual desire hindrance and the associated aggregates condition the sloth-torpor hindrance, the restlessness hindrance, and the ignorance hindrance (a cycle). The sensual desire hindrance and the base condition the sloth-torpor hindrance, the restlessness hindrance, and the ignorance hindrance (a cycle). (1)

Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paccayā nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca nīvaraṇañca paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… nīvaraṇañca vatthuñca paccayā sampayuttakā khandhā, nīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, nīvaraṇe ca mahābhūte ca paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

Both a hindrance and a non-hindrance state condition a non-hindrance state by root condition: one non-hindrance aggregate and a hindrance condition three aggregates and mind-originated materiality... two aggregates... a hindrance and the base condition the associated aggregates; a hindrance and the associated aggregates condition mind-originated materiality; the hindrances and the great elements condition mind-originated materiality. (2)

Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paccayā nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca paccayā tayo khandhā thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ [T 3.0353] avijjānīvaraṇaṃ…pe… dve khandhe [M 3.0303]…pe… (cakkaṃ). Kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca vatthuñca paccayā thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ sampayuttakā ca khandhā (cakkaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ). (3)

Both a hindrance and a non-hindrance state condition both hindrance and non-hindrance states by root condition: one non-hindrance aggregate and the sensual desire hindrance condition three aggregates, the sloth-torpor hindrance, the restlessness hindrance, and the ignorance hindrance... two aggregates... (a cycle). The sensual desire hindrance and the base condition the sloth-torpor hindrance, the restlessness hindrance, the ignorance hindrance, and the associated aggregates (a cycle, in brief). (3)

Non-Root Condition

16. Nīvaraṇaṃ [V 3.0373] dhammaṃ paccayā nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (1)

16. A hindrance state conditions a hindrance state by non-root condition: the doubt hindrance conditions the ignorance hindrance; the restlessness hindrance conditions the ignorance hindrance. (1)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nonīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ nonīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā) cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā ahetukā nonīvaraṇā khandhā. (1)

A non-hindrance state conditions a non-hindrance state by non-root condition: one rootless non-hindrance aggregate conditions three aggregates and mind-originated materiality... two aggregates... (up to non-percipient beings); the eye-base conditions eye-consciousness... the body-base conditions body-consciousness; the base conditions the rootless non-hindrance aggregates. (1)

Nonīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (2)

A non-hindrance state conditions a hindrance state by non-root condition: the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness condition the ignorance hindrance; the base conditions the ignorance hindrance. (2)

17. Nīvaraṇañca nonīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paccayā nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchānīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, vicikicchānīvaraṇañca vatthuñca paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇañca vatthuñca paccayā avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

17. Both a hindrance and a non-hindrance state condition a hindrance state by non-root condition: the doubt hindrance and the associated aggregates condition the ignorance hindrance; the restlessness hindrance and the associated aggregates condition the ignorance hindrance; the doubt hindrance and the base condition the ignorance hindrance; the restlessness hindrance and the base condition the ignorance hindrance (in brief). (1)

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. Negative Conditional Relations

Suddhaṃ

Pure.

18. Nahetuyā [M 3.0304][V 3.0374] cattāri, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava, naanantare tīṇi, nasamanantare tīṇi, naaññamaññe tīṇi, naupanissaye tīṇi, napurejāte nava, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane [T 3.0354] nava, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye ekaṃ, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte nava, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

18. By non-root condition, four; by non-object condition, three; by non-dominance condition, nine; by non-proximity condition, three; by non-contiguity condition, three; by non-mutuality condition, three; by non-decisive support condition, three; by non-prenascence condition, nine; by non-postnascence condition, nine; by non-repetition condition, nine; by non-kamma condition, three; by non-result condition, nine; by non-nutriment condition, one; by non-faculty condition, one; by non-jhāna condition, one; by non-path condition, one; by non-association condition, three; by non-dissociation condition, nine; by non-absence condition, three; by non-disappearance condition, three.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. Positive-Negative Enumeration

19. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

19. By root condition, not by object condition, three; not by dominance condition, nine (abbreviated).

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Negative-Positive Enumeration

20. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe cattāri, anantare cattāri, samanantare cattāri…pe… magge tīṇi, avigate cattāri.

20. By non-root condition, by object condition, four; by proximity condition, four; by contiguity condition, four… and so on… by path condition, three; by presence condition, four.

5. Saṃsaṭṭhavāro

1-4. Paccayacatukkaṃ

1–4. The Tetrad of Conditions

21. Nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ. Sabbaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ).

21. A hindering state conjoined with a hindering state arises by root condition: the sensual desire hindrance conjoined with the sloth and torpor hindrance, the restlessness hindrance, and the ignorance hindrance (a cycle. All hindrances should be elaborated).

22. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe nava (sabbattha nava), vipāke ekaṃ…pe… avigate nava.

22. By root condition, nine; by object condition, nine (nine in all cases); by result condition, one… and so on… by presence condition, nine.

Anulomaṃ.

Positive

23. Nīvaraṇaṃ [M 3.0305][V 3.0375] dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

23. A hindering state conjoined with a hindering state arises not by root condition: the doubt hindrance conjoined with the ignorance hindrance, the restlessness hindrance conjoined with the ignorance hindrance (abbreviated).

24. Nahetuyā cattāri, naadhipatiyā nava, napurejāte nava, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, navippayutte nava.

24. Not by root condition, four; not by dominance condition, nine; not by prenascence condition, nine; not by postnascence condition, nine; not by repetition condition, nine; not by kamma condition, three; not by result condition, nine; not by jhāna condition, one; not by path condition, one; not by dissociation condition, nine.

Paccanīyaṃ.

Negative

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

25. Nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

25. A hindering state is a condition for a hindering state by root condition: hindering roots are a condition for associated hindering states by root condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A hindering state is a condition for a non-hindering state by root condition: hindering roots are a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by root condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇo [V 3.0376] dhammo nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A hindering state is a condition for a hindering state and for a non-hindering state by root condition: hindering roots are a condition for associated aggregates, for hindering states, and for mind-originated matter by root condition. (3)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nonīvaraṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A non-hindering state is a condition for a non-hindering state by root condition: non-hindering roots are a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on…. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

26. Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0306] dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nīvaraṇe ārabbha nonīvaraṇā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

26. A hindering state is a condition for a hindering state by object condition: taking a hindering state as object, hindering states arise. (The root should be questioned.) Taking a hindering state as object, non-hindering aggregates arise. (The root should be established.) Taking a hindering state as object, both hindering states and associated aggregates arise. (3)

27. Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ…pe… phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa[T 3.0356], maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ariyā nonīvaraṇe pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nonīvaraṇe khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Cetopariyañāṇena nonīvaraṇacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… nonīvaraṇā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

27. A non-hindering state is a condition for a non-hindering state by object condition: having given a gift… and so on… observed morality… and so on… performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects upon it; having previously practiced well… and so on… having emerged from jhāna, one reflects upon the jhāna… and so on… noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect upon the path… and so on… the fruition… and so on… Nibbāna… and so on… Nibbāna is a condition by object condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruition, and for advertence; noble ones reflect upon the abandoned defilements that are non-hindering, the suppressed defilements… and so on… previously accumulated deeds… and so on… the eye… and so on… the physical basis, the non-hindering aggregates as impermanent… and so on… sorrow arises; with the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear element, one hears sounds. Through the knowledge of penetration of minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with a non-hindering mind; the base of infinite space for the base of infinite consciousness… and so on… the base of nothingness for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… and so on… the form base for eye-consciousness… and so on… the tangible base for body-consciousness… and so on… the non-hindering aggregates are a condition by object condition for the knowledge of psychic power, the knowledge of penetration of minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to kamma, the knowledge of the future, and for advertence. (1)

Nonīvaraṇo [V 3.0377] dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nonīvaraṇe khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi …pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. (2)

A non-hindering state is a condition for a hindering state by object condition: a gift… and so on… morality… and so on… Uposatha observance… and so on… previously well-practiced deeds… and so on… jhānas… and so on… the eye… and so on… the physical basis. One savors and delights in the non-hindering aggregates; taking that as object, lust arises, wrong view… and so on… doubt… and so on… restlessness… and so on… sorrow arises. (2)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nonīvaraṇe khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A non-hindering state is a condition for a hindering state and for a non-hindering state by object condition: a gift… and so on… morality… and so on… Uposatha observance… and so on… previously well-practiced deeds… and so on… jhānas… and so on… the eye… and so on… the physical basis. One savors and delights in the non-hindering aggregates; taking that as object, both hindering states and associated aggregates arise. (3)

Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0307] ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (ārabbha [T 3.0357] kātabbā).

Hindering and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for a hindering phenomenon by object condition… three (to be elaborated).

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

28. Nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – nīvaraṇe garuṃ katvā nīvaraṇā uppajjanti… tīṇi (ārammaṇasadisaṃ). (3)

28. A hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon by dominance condition. Object dominance: having given importance to the hindrances, hindrances arise… three (similar to the object condition). (3)

29. Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ…pe… phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nonīvaraṇe khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – nonīvaraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

29. A non-hindering phenomenon is a condition for a non-hindering phenomenon by dominance condition—object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: having given alms… observed morality… performed the Uposatha observance, having given importance to that, one reflects upon it; previously well-practiced deeds… having emerged from jhāna… having emerged from the noble path, one reflects upon the path… the fruit… Nibbāna… Nibbāna is a condition by dominance condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit; the eye… the base, having given importance to the non-hindering aggregates, one relishes and delights in them; having given importance to that, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: a non-hindering dominant factor is a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by dominance condition. (1)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati[V 3.0378]. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nonīvaraṇe khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – nonīvaraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon by dominance condition—object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: giving… morality… the Uposatha observance… previously… jhāna… the eye… the base, having given importance to the non-hindering aggregates, one relishes and delights in them; having given importance to that, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: a non-hindering dominant factor is a condition for associated hindrances by dominance condition. (2)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa [T 3.0358] ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nonīvaraṇe khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – nonīvaraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-hindering phenomenon is a condition for both a hindering and a non-hindering phenomenon by dominance condition—object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: giving… morality… the Uposatha observance… previously… jhāna… the eye… the base, having given importance to the non-hindering aggregates, one relishes and delights in them; having given importance to that, hindrances and associated aggregates arise. Co-nascence dominance: a non-hindering dominant factor is a condition for associated aggregates, for hindrances, and for mind-originated matter by dominance condition. (3)

Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0308] ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati… tīṇi (ārammaṇādhipatiyeva).

Hindering and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for a hindering phenomenon by dominance condition—object dominance… three (object dominance only).

Anantarapaccayo

Contiguity Condition

30. Nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nīvaraṇā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) purimā purimā nīvaraṇā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nonīvaraṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; nīvaraṇā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) purimā purimā nīvaraṇā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

30. A hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon by contiguity condition—preceding hindrances are a condition for subsequent hindrances by contiguity condition. (The root should be questioned.) Preceding hindrances are a condition for subsequent non-hindering aggregates by contiguity condition; hindrances are a condition for emergence by contiguity condition. (The root should be questioned.) Preceding hindrances are a condition for subsequent hindrances and associated aggregates by contiguity condition. (3)

31. Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nonīvaraṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nonīvaraṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo…pe… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ [T 3.0359]) purimā purimā nonīvaraṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā nīvaraṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ [V 3.0379] pucchitabbaṃ) purimā purimā nonīvaraṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā nīvaraṇānaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

31. A non-hindering phenomenon is a condition for a non-hindering phenomenon by contiguity condition—preceding non-hindering aggregates are a condition for subsequent non-hindering aggregates by contiguity condition… and so on… for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the attainment of fruition by contiguity condition. (The root should be questioned.) Preceding non-hindering aggregates are a condition for subsequent hindrances by contiguity condition; adverting is a condition for the hindrances by contiguity condition. (The root should be questioned.) Preceding non-hindering aggregates are a condition for subsequent hindrances and associated aggregates by contiguity condition; adverting is a condition for the hindrances and associated aggregates by contiguity condition. (3)

32. Nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) purimā purimā nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nonīvaraṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) purimā purimā nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

32. Hindering and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for a hindering phenomenon by contiguity condition—preceding hindrances and associated aggregates are a condition for subsequent hindrances by contiguity condition. (The root should be questioned.) Preceding hindrances and associated aggregates are a condition for subsequent non-hindering aggregates by contiguity condition; hindrances and associated aggregates are a condition for emergence by contiguity condition. (The root should be questioned.) Preceding hindrances and associated aggregates are a condition for subsequent hindrances and associated aggregates by contiguity condition. (3)

Samanantarapaccayādi

Proximity Condition, and so on.

33. Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0309] dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nissayapaccayena paccayo.

33. A hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon by proximity condition… by co-nascence condition… by mutuality condition… by support condition.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

34. Nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – nīvaraṇāni nīvaraṇānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

34. A hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon by decisive support condition—object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: hindrances are a condition for hindrances by decisive support condition… three.

35. Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa [T 3.0360] dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ…pe… maggaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ…pe… mānaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā [V 3.0380] …pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… paññāya, rāgassa…pe… patthanāya, kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

35. A state free from hindrances is a condition for a state free from hindrances by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one gives alms… virtue… the Uposatha observance… generates jhāna, insight… the path… higher knowledge… attainment; cultivates conceit, grasps wrong view; relying on virtue… wisdom… conceit… wrong view… aspiration… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… season… food… lodging, one gives alms… splits the Saṅgha; faith… lodging are a condition for faith… wisdom, for lust… aspiration, for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, for the path, for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo (tīṇi upanissayā). Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state free from hindrances is a condition for a hindering state by way of decisive support condition (three decisive supports). Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one cultivates conceit, grasps wrong view; relying on virtue… lodging, one kills living beings… splits the Saṅgha; faith… lodging are a condition for lust… aspiration by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ [T 3.0361] upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state free from hindrances is a condition for a hindering state and for a state free from hindrances by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one cultivates conceit, grasps wrong view; relying on virtue… lodging, one kills living beings… splits the Saṅgha; faith… lodging are a condition for the hindrances and the associated aggregates by way of decisive support condition. (3)

Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0310] ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā nīvaraṇānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

Hindering states and states free from hindrances are a condition for a hindering state by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: the hindrances and the associated aggregates are a condition for the hindrances by way of decisive support condition… three.

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

36. Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati…pe… tīṇi (purejātaṃ ārammaṇasadisaṃ kusalākusalassa vibhajitabbaṃ).

36. A state free from hindrances is a condition for a state free from hindrances by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: the eye… the base as impermanent… grief arises… three. (Pre-nascence should be analyzed similarly to the object condition for the wholesome and unwholesome.)

Pacchājāta-āsevanapaccayā

Post-nascence Condition; Repetition Condition

37. Nīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… nava.

37. A hindering state is a condition for a state free from hindrances by way of post-nascence condition… three… by way of repetition condition… nine.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

38. Nonīvaraṇo [V 3.0381] dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – nonīvaraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – nonīvaraṇā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nonīvaraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nonīvaraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

38. A state free from hindrances is a condition for a state free from hindrances by way of kamma condition: co-nascent and non-co-nascent. Co-nascent: Volition free from hindrances is a condition by way of kamma condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena; at the moment of relinking… Non-co-nascent: Volition free from hindrances is a condition by way of kamma condition for the resultant aggregates and kamma-originated material phenomena. (The root should be asked) Volition free from hindrances is a condition by way of kamma condition for the associated hindrances. (The root should be asked) Volition free from hindrances is a condition by way of kamma condition for the associated aggregates, the hindrances, and mind-originated material phenomena. (3)

Vipākapaccayādi

Result Condition, and so on.

39. Nonīvaraṇo [T 3.0362] dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo… jhānapaccayena paccayo… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo.

39. A state free from hindrances is a condition for a state free from hindrances by way of result condition… one… by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition… by way of jhāna condition… by way of path condition… by way of association condition.

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

40. Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0311] dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (evaṃ avasesā cattāri pañhā kātabbā).

40. A hindering state is a condition for a non-hindering state by way of dissociation condition: co-nascent, post-nascent (thus, the remaining four questions should be treated similarly).

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

41. Nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ thinamiddhanīvaraṇassa uddhaccanīvaraṇassa avijjānīvaraṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). (1)

41. A hindering state is a condition for a hindering state by way of presence condition: the hindrance of sensual desire is a condition for the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness, and the hindrance of ignorance by way of presence condition (a cycle). (1)

Nīvaraṇo dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (evaṃ nīvaraṇamūle tīṇi ). (3)

A hindering state is a condition for a non-hindering state by way of presence condition: co-nascent, post-nascent. (Thus, there are three in the hindrance root.) (3)

42. Nonīvaraṇo [V 3.0382] dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

42. A non-hindering state is a condition for a non-hindering state by way of presence condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, and faculty (abbreviated). (1)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (2)

A non-hindering state is a condition for a hindering state by way of presence condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent (abbreviated). (2)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ) (3)

A non-hindering state is a condition for a hindering state and a non-hindering state by way of presence condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent (abbreviated). (3)

43. Nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca sampayuttakā ca khandhā thinamiddhanīvaraṇassa uddhaccanīvaraṇassa avijjānīvaraṇassa atthipaccayena [T 3.0363] paccayo; kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca vatthu ca thinamiddhanīvaraṇassa uddhaccanīvaraṇassa avijjānīvaraṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

43. Hindering states and non-hindering states are a condition for a hindering state by way of presence condition: co-nascent and pre-nascent. Co-nascent: the hindrance of sensual desire and the associated aggregates are a condition for the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness, and the hindrance of ignorance by way of presence condition; the hindrance of sensual desire and the physical base are a condition for the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness, and the hindrance of ignorance by way of presence condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – nonīvaraṇo eko khandho ca nīvaraṇā ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… nīvaraṇā ca vatthu ca nonīvaraṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo[M 3.0312]; nīvaraṇā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

Hindering phenomena and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for non-hindering phenomena by presence condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, faculty. By co-nascence—one non-hindering aggregate and the hindrances are a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated matter by presence condition... and so on... two aggregates... and so on... the hindrances and the physical base are a condition for the non-hindering aggregates by presence condition; the hindrances and associated aggregates are a condition for mind-originated matter by presence condition; the hindrances and the great elements are a condition for mind-originated matter by presence condition. By post-nascence—the hindrances and associated aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by presence condition. By post-nascence—the hindrances, associated aggregates, and physical nutriment are a condition for this body by presence condition. By post-nascence—the hindrances, associated aggregates, and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-produced matter by presence condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – nonīvaraṇo eko khandho ca kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ thinamiddhanīvaraṇassa uddhaccanīvaraṇassa avijjānīvaraṇassa [V 3.0383] ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; dve khandhā ca…pe… kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca [T 3.0364] vatthu ca thinamiddhanīvaraṇassa uddhaccanīvaraṇassa avijjānīvaraṇassa ca sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). (3)

Hindering phenomena and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for hindering phenomena and non-hindering phenomena by presence condition—co-nascence and pre-nascence. By co-nascence—one non-hindering aggregate and the hindrance of sensual desire are a condition for the three aggregates, for the hindrance of sloth and torpor, for the hindrance of restlessness, for the hindrance of ignorance, and for mind-originated matter by presence condition; two aggregates... and so on... the hindrance of sensual desire and the physical base are a condition for the hindrance of sloth and torpor, for the hindrance of restlessness, for the hindrance of ignorance, and for the associated aggregates by presence condition (cycle). (3)

Suddhaṃ

Pure

44. Hetuyā cattāri, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe nava, nissaye nava, upanissaye nava, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre tīṇi, indriye tīṇi, jhāne tīṇi, magge tīṇi, sampayutte nava, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā nava, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate nava.

44. By root condition, four; by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, nine; by contiguity condition, nine; by proximity condition, nine; by co-nascence condition, nine; by mutuality condition, nine; by dependence condition, nine; by decisive support condition, nine; by pre-nascence condition, three; by post-nascence condition, three; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, three; by result condition, one; by nutriment condition, three; by faculty condition, three; by jhāna condition, three; by path condition, three; by association condition, nine; by dissociation condition, five; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, nine; by disappearance condition, nine; by non-disappearance condition, nine.

Anulomaṃ.

Paccanīyuddhāro

45. Nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

45. A hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0313] dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A hindering phenomenon is a condition for a non-hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition... by post-nascence condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon and for a non-hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition. (3)

46. Nonīvaraṇo [V 3.0384] dhammo nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena [T 3.0365] paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

46. A non-hindering phenomenon is a condition for a non-hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition... by pre-nascence condition... by post-nascence condition... by kamma condition... by nutriment condition... by faculty condition. (1)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition... by pre-nascence condition. (2)

Nonīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-hindering phenomenon is a condition for a hindering phenomenon and for a non-hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition... by pre-nascence condition. (3)

47. Nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

47. Hindering phenomena and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for a hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nonīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Hindering phenomena and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for a non-hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition... by post-nascence condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇo ca nonīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa ca nonīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Hindering phenomena and non-hindering phenomena are a condition for a hindering phenomenon and for a non-hindering phenomenon by object condition... by co-nascence condition... by decisive support condition. (3)

48. By non-root condition, nine; by non-object condition, nine; by non-dominance condition, nine (nine in all cases)... by non-disappearance condition, nine; by non-non-disappearance condition, nine.

Hetudukaṃ

Root Dyad

49. Hetupaccayā [M 3.0314][V 3.0385] naārammaṇe cattāri…pe… nasamanantare cattāri, naaññamaññe dve, naupanissaye cattāri…pe… namagge cattāri, nasampayutte dve, navippayutte cattāri, nonatthiyā cattāri, novigate cattāri.

49. By root condition: by non-object condition, four... by non-proximity condition, four; by non-mutuality condition, two; by non-decisive support condition, four... by non-path condition, four; by non-association condition, two; by non-dissociation condition, four; by non-absence condition, four; by non-disappearance condition, four.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Negative-Affirmative Conditional Relations

50. Nahetupaccayā [T 3.0366] ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava (anulomamātikā)…pe… avigate nava.

50. By non-root condition: by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, nine (affirmative matrix)... and so on... by non-disappearance condition, nine.

45. Nīvaraṇiyadukaṃ

45. The Hindrance-related Dyad

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. Section on Dependence

51. Nīvaraṇiyaṃ [V 3.0386] dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇiyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā…pe… (nīvaraṇiyadukaṃ yathā lokiyadukaṃ evaṃ kātabbaṃ ninnānākaraṇaṃ).

51. Dependent on a hindrance-related phenomenon, a hindrance-related phenomenon arises by root condition... and so on... (The Hindrance-related Dyad is to be worked out in the same way as the Worldly Dyad; there is no difference.)

Dvikkhattuṃ kāmacchandena, catukkhattuṃ paṭighena ca;

Uddhaccaṃ vicikicchā ca, ubhopete sakiṃ sakiṃ;

Nīvaraṇānaṃ nīvaraṇehi, aṭṭhavidhaṃ payojanaṃ.

Twice with sensual desire, four times with aversion; restlessness and doubt, each once. There is an eightfold application of hindrances by means of hindrances.

(Nīvaraṇadukassa mātikā idha katā.)

(Here is given the matrix of the Hindrance Dyad.)

Nīvaraṇiyadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Hindering Dyad is completed.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

52. Nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ [V 3.0387] dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

52. Dependent on a phenomenon associated with hindrances, a phenomenon associated with hindrances arises by way of root condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with hindrances, three aggregates…and so on…dependent on two aggregates…and so on. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ [M 3.0315] dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayutte [T 3.0367] khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon associated with hindrances, a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances arises by way of root condition. Dependent on the aggregates associated with hindrances, mind-originated matter arises. (2)

Nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon associated with hindrances, phenomena associated with hindrances and phenomena dissociated from hindrances arise by way of root condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with hindrances, three aggregates and mind-originated matter…and so on…dependent on two aggregates…and so on. (3)

53. Nīvaraṇavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇavippayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva ajjhattikā mahābhūtā). (1)

53. Dependent on a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances, a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances arises by way of root condition. Dependent on one aggregate dissociated from hindrances, three aggregates and mind-originated matter…and so on…dependent on two aggregates…and so on…at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so on… (up to the internal great elements). (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayuttañca [V 3.0388] nīvaraṇavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayutte khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

Dependent on a phenomenon associated with hindrances and a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances, a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances arises by way of root condition. Dependent on the aggregates associated with hindrances and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises (in brief).

66. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇasampayuttā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo.
