66. A state associated with hindrances is a condition for a state associated with hindrances by way of root condition—the roots associated with hindrances are conditions for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (The root should be investigated.) The roots associated with hindrances are conditions for mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition. (The root should be investigated.) The roots associated with hindrances are conditions for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition. (3)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇavippayuttā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A state dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a state dissociated from hindrances by way of root condition—roots dissociated from hindrances are conditions for associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

67. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – rāgaṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; diṭṭhiṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; vicikicchaṃ ārabbha vicikicchā…pe… diṭṭhi…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; uddhaccaṃ ārabbha uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā, domanassaṃ uppajjati; domanassaṃ ārabbha domanassaṃ uppajjati; diṭṭhi [T 3.0372] …pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ uppajjati. (1)

67. A state associated with the hindrances is a condition for a state associated with the hindrances by way of object condition: one savors and delights in lust; based on that, lust arises, wrong view... doubt... restlessness... displeasure arises; one savors and delights in wrong view; based on that, lust arises, wrong view... doubt... restlessness... displeasure arises; based on doubt, doubt... wrong view... restlessness... displeasure arises; based on restlessness, restlessness arises, wrong view... doubt, displeasure arises; based on displeasure, displeasure arises; wrong view... doubt... restlessness arises. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā nīvaraṇasampayutte pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti; nīvaraṇasampayutte khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, cetopariyañāṇena nīvaraṇasampayuttacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti; nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state associated with hindrances is a condition for a state dissociated from hindrances by way of object condition—noble ones reflect on the abandoned defilements associated with hindrances, reflect on the suppressed defilements, know the previously accumulated defilements; one contemplates the aggregates associated with hindrances as impermanent, suffering, and not-self; one knows the mind of one whose mind is associated with hindrances through mind-penetrating knowledge; the aggregates associated with hindrances are conditions for mind-penetrating knowledge, knowledge of past lives, knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their actions, knowledge of the future, and adverting by way of object condition. (2)

68. Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā [V 3.0395] vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ…pe… phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nīvaraṇavippayutte khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati (yāva āvajjanāya). (1)

68. A state dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a state dissociated from hindrances by way of object condition—having performed generosity… virtue… Uposatha practice, one reflects upon that; having previously practiced well… having emerged from jhāna, one reflects upon the jhāna… having emerged from the noble path, one reflects upon the path… the fruit… Nibbāna… Nibbāna is a condition for the change-of-lineage, purification, path, and fruit, and for adverting by way of object condition; one contemplates the eye… the base, and the aggregates dissociated from hindrances as impermanent, suffering, and not-self; with the divine eye, one sees forms (up to adverting). (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto [M 3.0321] dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nīvaraṇavippayutte khandhe assādeti abhinandati[T 3.0373], taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. (2)

A state dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a state associated with hindrances by way of object condition: one savors and delights in generosity… virtue… Uposatha practice… previously… jhāna… the eye… the base, and the aggregates dissociated from hindrances; based on that, lust arises, wrong view… doubt… restlessness… displeasure arises. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

69. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – rāgaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati; diṭṭhiṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti…pe…. Sahajātādhipati – nīvaraṇasampayuttādhipati nīvaraṇasampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

69. A state associated with hindrances is a condition for a state associated with hindrances by way of dominance condition: object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: Having made lust weighty, one savors and delights in it. Having made that weighty, lust arises, wrong view arises. Having made wrong view weighty, one savors and delights in it… Co-nascence dominance: A dominant factor associated with hindrances is a condition for the aggregates associated with hindrances by way of dominance condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – nīvaraṇasampayuttādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nīvaraṇasampayuttādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state associated with hindrances is a condition for a state dissociated from hindrances by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance—a dominant factor associated with hindrances is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dominance condition. (The root should be investigated.) A dominant factor associated with hindrances is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of dominance condition. (3)

70. Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo[V 3.0396]. Sahajātādhipati – nīvaraṇavippayuttādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

70. A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of dominance condition: object-dominance, co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: Having performed generosity... virtue... Uposatha practice, one reflects upon it, respecting it; having previously practiced well... having emerged from jhāna, one reflects upon the jhāna, respecting it... having emerged from the noble path, one reflects upon the path, respecting it... the fruit... Nibbāna... Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, purification, the path, and the fruit by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant factor dissociated from hindrances is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena [T 3.0374] paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nīvaraṇavippayutte khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of dominance condition: object-dominance. One savors and delights in generosity… virtue… previously… jhāna… the eye… the base, and the aggregates dissociated from hindrances, regarding them as weighty; regarding that as weighty, lust arises, wrong view arises. (2)

Anantarapaccayo

Immediate Condition

71. Nīvaraṇasampayutto [M 3.0322] dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇasampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo (idha purimā purimāti natthi). (2)

71. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of immediate condition: the preceding, preceding aggregates associated with hindrances are a condition for the subsequent, subsequent aggregates associated with hindrances by way of immediate condition. (The root should be questioned.) The aggregates associated with hindrances are a condition for emergence by way of immediate condition (here, there is no “the preceding, preceding”). (2)

(Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) purimā purimā nīvaraṇavippayuttā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nīvaraṇavippayuttānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

(The root should be questioned.) The preceding, preceding aggregates dissociated from hindrances are a condition for the subsequent, subsequent aggregates dissociated from hindrances by way of immediate condition; adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage; change-of-lineage for the path; the path for the fruit; the fruit for the attainment of fruition, by way of immediate condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – āvajjanā nīvaraṇasampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of immediate condition: adverting is a condition for the aggregates associated with hindrances by way of immediate condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayādi

Contiguity Condition, etc.

72. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nissayapaccayena paccayo.

72. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of contiguity condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of mutuality condition… by way of dependence condition.

Upanissayapaccayo

Strong Dependence Condition

73. Nīvaraṇasampayutto [V 3.0397] dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – rāgaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; dosaṃ… mohaṃ… mānaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya [T 3.0375] pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; rāgo…pe… patthanā rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

73. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of strong dependence condition: object strong dependence, immediate strong dependence, natural strong dependence… Natural strong dependence: Relying on lust, one kills living beings… splits the Saṅgha; relying on hatred… aspiration, one kills living beings… splits the Saṅgha; lust… aspiration is a condition for lust… aspiration by way of strong dependence condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… vipassanaṃ… maggaṃ… abhiññaṃ… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; dosaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; rāgo…pe… patthanā saddhāya [M 3.0323] …pe… paññāya… kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of strong dependence condition: immediate strong dependence, natural strong dependence… Natural strong dependence: Relying on lust, one gives gifts… generates attainment; relying on hatred… aspiration, one gives gifts… generates attainment; lust… aspiration is a condition for faith… wisdom… bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the path, or the attainment of fruition by way of strong dependence condition. (2)

74. Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ…pe… maggaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… paññāya…pe… maggassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

74. A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of strong dependence condition: object strong dependence, immediate strong dependence, natural strong dependence… Natural strong dependence: Relying on faith, one gives gifts… generates attainment; relying on virtue… lodging, one gives gifts… generates attainment; faith… lodging is a condition for faith… wisdom… the path, or the attainment of fruition by way of strong dependence condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya [T 3.0376] pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… mānassa… diṭṭhiyā… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of strong dependence condition: object strong dependence, immediate strong dependence, natural strong dependence… Natural strong dependence: Relying on faith, one generates conceit, grasps at wrong view; relying on virtue… lodging, one kills living beings… splits the Saṅgha; faith… lodging is a condition for lust… aspiration by way of strong dependence condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayo

Prenascence Condition

75. Nīvaraṇavippayutto [V 3.0398] dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nīvaraṇavippayuttānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

75. A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of prenascence condition: object-prenascence, base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: One contemplates the eye… base as impermanent, suffering, and not-self. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-faculty, one hears sounds. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the tangible base for body-consciousness, by way of prenascence condition. Base-prenascence: The eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the body base for body-consciousness, by way of prenascence condition; the base is a condition for the aggregates dissociated from hindrances by way of prenascence condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo… doso… moho…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu nīvaraṇasampayuttānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of prenascence condition—object-prenascence, base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: one savors and rejoices in the eye… the base; dependent on that, lust… hatred… delusion… arises. Base-prenascence: the base is a condition for the aggregates associated with hindrances by way of prenascence condition. (2)

Pacchājātāsevanapaccayā

Postnascence and Repetition Conditions

76. Nīvaraṇasampayutto [M 3.0324] dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… dve, āsevanapaccayena paccayo… dve.

76. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of postnascence condition… (two cases), by way of repetition condition… (two cases).

Kammapaccayādi

Kamma Condition, and so on.

77. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇasampayuttā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā[T 3.0377]. Sahajātā – nīvaraṇasampayuttā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – nīvaraṇasampayuttā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) nīvaraṇasampayuttā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

77. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of kamma condition—volition associated with hindrances is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (The root method should be applied.) Conascent, non-conascent. Conascent—volition associated with hindrances is a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. Non-conascent—volition associated with hindrances is a condition for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of kamma condition. (The root method should be applied.) Volition associated with hindrances is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. (3)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto [V 3.0399] dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā (saṃkhittaṃ). Vipākapaccayā… ekaṃ.

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of kamma condition: conascent, non-conascent (in brief). By way of result condition… (one case).

Āhārapaccayādi

Nutriment Condition, and so on.

78. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo… jhānapaccayena paccayo… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… dve.

78. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition… by way of jhāna condition… by way of path condition… by way of association condition… (two cases).

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

79. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

79. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of dissociation condition—conascent, postnascent (in brief). (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of dissociation condition: conascent, prenascent, postnascent (in brief). (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu nīvaraṇasampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of dissociation condition. Prenascent: the base is a condition for the aggregates associated with hindrances by way of dissociation condition. (2)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

80. Nīvaraṇasampayutto [M 3.0325] dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa atthipaccayena [T 3.0378] paccayo – nīvaraṇasampayutto eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe…. (1)

80. A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of presence condition—one aggregate associated with hindrances is a condition for the other three aggregates by way of presence condition… and so on. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of presence condition—conascent, postnascent. Conascent: the aggregates associated with hindrances are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of presence condition. Postnascent: the aggregates associated with hindrances are a condition for this prenascent body by way of presence condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto [V 3.0400] dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ca nīvaraṇavippayuttassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇasampayutto eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon associated with hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances and for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of presence condition—one aggregate associated with hindrances is a condition for the other three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of presence condition… and so on… two aggregates are a condition for the other two aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of presence condition. (3)

81. Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

81. A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of presence condition: conascent, prenascent, postnascent, nutriment, and faculty (in brief). (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo…pe… diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; vatthu nīvaraṇasampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of presence condition. Prenascent: one savors and rejoices in the eye… the base; dependent on that, lust… wrong view… doubt… restlessness… displeasure arises. The base is a condition for the aggregates associated with hindrances by way of presence condition. (2)

82. Nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇavippayutto ca dhammā nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – nīvaraṇasampayutto eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca [T 3.0379] vatthu ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

82. Both a phenomenon associated with hindrances and a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances are a condition for a phenomenon associated with hindrances by way of presence condition—conascent, prenascent. Conascent: one aggregate associated with hindrances and the base are a condition for the other three aggregates by way of presence condition… and so on… two aggregates and the base are a condition for the other two aggregates by way of presence condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇavippayutto ca dhammā nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ [M 3.0326] rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nīvaraṇasampayuttā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

Both a phenomenon associated with hindrances and a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances are a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from hindrances by way of presence condition—conascent, postnascent, nutriment, faculty. Conascent: the aggregates associated with hindrances and the great elements are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of presence condition. Postnascent: the aggregates associated with hindrances and physical nutriment are a condition for this body by way of presence condition. Postnascent: the aggregates associated with hindrances and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of presence condition. (2)

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Direct Order of Conditional Relations

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Enumeration Chapter

Suddhaṃ

Pure

83. Hetuyā [V 3.0401] cattāri, ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā pañca, anantare cattāri, samanantare cattāri, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye satta, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte dve, pacchājāte dve, āsevane dve, kamme cattāri, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre cattāri, indriye cattāri, jhāne cattāri, magge cattāri, sampayutte dve, vippayutte tīṇi, atthiyā satta, natthiyā cattāri, vigate cattāri, avigate satta.

83. By way of root condition, four; by way of object condition, four; by way of predominance condition, five; by way of contiguity condition, four; by way of immediate contiguity condition, four; by way of co-nascence condition, five; by way of mutuality condition, two; by way of dependence condition, seven; by way of decisive support condition, four; by way of pre-nascence condition, two; by way of post-nascence condition, two; by way of repetition condition, two; by way of kamma condition, four; by way of result condition, one; by way of nutriment condition, four; by way of faculty condition, four; by way of jhana condition, four; by way of path condition, four; by way of association condition, two; by way of dissociation condition, three; by way of presence condition, seven; by way of absence condition, four; by way of disappearance condition, four; by way of non-disappearance condition, seven.

Anulomaṃ.

Direct Order.

Paccanīyuddhāro

Section on the Negative Method

84. Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

84. A phenomenon associated with the hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with the hindrances by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo [T 3.0380]… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon associated with the hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of kamma condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ca nīvaraṇavippayuttassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon associated with the hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with the hindrances and a phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances by way of co-nascence condition. (3)

85. Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo [V 3.0402]… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena [M 3.0327] paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

85. A phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of kamma condition... by way of nutriment condition... by way of faculty condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇavippayutto dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances is a condition for a phenomenon associated with the hindrances by way of object condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇavippayutto ca dhammā nīvaraṇasampayuttassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. (1)

A phenomenon associated with the hindrances and a phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances are a condition for a phenomenon associated with the hindrances by way of co-nascence and pre-nascence. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇavippayutto ca dhammā nīvaraṇavippayuttassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

A phenomenon associated with the hindrances and a phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances are a condition for a phenomenon dissociated from the hindrances by way of co-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. (2)

Root Condition

90. Nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇiyo ca dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇiyassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

90. A phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related is a condition for a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related by way of root condition. Roots that are both hindrances and hindrance-related are a condition for the associated hindrances by way of root condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇo ceva [T 3.0382] nīvaraṇiyo ca dhammo nīvaraṇiyassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related is a condition for a phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance by way of root condition. Roots that are both hindrances and hindrance-related are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇiyo ca dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇiyassa ca nīvaraṇiyassa ceva [V 3.0405] no ca nīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā [M 3.0329] ceva nīvaraṇiyā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related is a condition for a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related, and for a phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance, by way of root condition. Roots that are both hindrances and hindrance-related are a condition for their associated aggregates, for the hindrances, and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition. (3)

Nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇiyassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance is a condition for a phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance by way of root condition. Roots that are hindrance-related but not hindrances are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

91. Nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇiyo ca dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇiyassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

91. A phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related is a condition for a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related by way of object condition. Taking a hindrance as object, hindrances arise. (The root should be questioned.) Taking a hindrance as object, aggregates that are hindrance-related but not hindrances arise. (The root should be questioned.) Taking a hindrance as object, hindrances and their associated aggregates arise. (3)

Nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇiyassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi… vicikicchā… uddhaccaṃ… domanassaṃ uppajjati; pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā gotrabhuṃ paccavekkhanti, vodānaṃ…pe… pahīne kilese [T 3.0383] …pe… vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nīvaraṇiye ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati, assādeti abhinandati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… (yāva āvajjanā tāva kātabbā). (1)

A phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance is a condition for a phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance by way of object condition. Having performed giving…pe… virtue…pe… the Uposatha observance, one reflects on it, delights in it, and approves of it; taking that as object, lust arises, wrong view… doubt… restlessness… displeasure arises. Previously well-practiced deeds…pe… jhānas…pe… noble ones reflect on change-of-lineage, on purification…pe… on abandoned defilements…pe… on suppressed defilements…pe… on previously accumulated deeds…pe… the eye…pe… the physical base—one contemplates the hindrance-related but non-hindrance aggregates as impermanent…pe…, delights in them, approves of them…pe… displeasure arises. With the divine eye, one sees a form…pe… (This is to be done up to adverting.) (1)

Nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇiyassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nīvaraṇiye ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo…pe… diṭṭhi… vicikicchā… uddhaccaṃ… domanassaṃ uppajjati. (2)

A phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance is a condition for a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related by way of object condition. Having performed giving…pe… virtue…pe… the Uposatha observance…pe… previously well-practiced deeds…pe… jhānas…pe… the eye…pe… the physical base—one delights in and approves of the hindrance-related but non-hindrance aggregates. Taking that as object, lust…pe… wrong view… doubt… restlessness… displeasure arises. (2)

Nīvaraṇiyo [V 3.0406] ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇiyassa ca nīvaraṇiyassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā [M 3.0330]…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nīvaraṇiye ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti (evaṃ itarepi tīṇi kātabbā). (3)

A phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance is a condition for a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-related, and for a phenomenon that is hindrance-related but not a hindrance, by way of object condition. Having performed giving…pe… virtue…pe… the Uposatha observance…pe… previously well-practiced deeds…pe… jhānas…pe… the eye…pe… the physical base—one delights in and approves of the hindrance-related but non-hindrance aggregates. Taking that as object, hindrances and their associated aggregates arise. (Likewise, the other three should be done.) (3)

(Ārammaṇasadisā adhipatipaccayā, purejātampi ārammaṇasadisaṃ. Upanissayepi lokuttaraṃ na kātabbaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ, evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ yathā nīvaraṇadukaṃ, evaṃ paccavekkhitvā kātabbaṃ.)

(The dominance conditions are similar to the object condition; the prenascent condition is also similar to the object condition. In the dependence condition, the supramundane should not be included. This is a summary; it should be elaborated as with the Hindrance Dyad, and should be done after reflecting on it.)

Nīvaraṇanīvaraṇiyadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Hindrance and Hindrance-Related is concluded.

92. Nīvaraṇañceva [T 3.0384][V 3.0407] nīvaraṇasampayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ. Sabbepi nīvaraṇā kātabbā). (1)

92. Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated arises by way of root condition. Conditioned by the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise. (This is a cycle. All hindrances should be included.) (1)

Nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇe paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā. (2)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance arises by way of root condition. Conditioned by a hindrance, the associated aggregates arise. (2)

Nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ sampayuttakā ca khandhā (cakkaṃ). (3)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, phenomena that are both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, and phenomena that are hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, arise by way of root condition. Conditioned by the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance, and the associated aggregates arise. (This is a cycle.) (3)

93. Nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca [V 3.0408] nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

93. Conditioned by a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance arises by way of root condition. Conditioned by one hindrance-associated aggregate that is not a hindrance, three aggregates arise…pe… conditioned by two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva [M 3.0331] no ca nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayutte ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe paṭicca nīvaraṇā. (2)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated arises by way of root condition. Conditioned by the hindrance-associated aggregates that are not hindrances, the hindrances arise. (2)

Nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇasampayutto [T 3.0385] ceva no ca nīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā nīvaraṇā ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, phenomena that are both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, and phenomena that are hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, arise by way of root condition. Conditioned by one hindrance-associated aggregate that is not a hindrance, three aggregates and the hindrances arise…pe… conditioned by two aggregates…pe…. (3)

94. Nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañca nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (cakkaṃ). (1)

94. Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, and a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated arises by way of root condition. Conditioned by the hindrance of sensual desire and the associated aggregates, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise. (Cycle.) (1)

Nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañca nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca nīvaraṇañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe…. (2)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, and a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance arises by way of root condition. Conditioned by one hindrance-associated aggregate that is not a hindrance and a hindrance, three aggregates arise…pe… conditioned by two aggregates…pe…. (2)

Nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañca nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca kāmacchandanīvaraṇañca paṭicca tayo khandhā thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… (cakkaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ.). (3)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, and a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, phenomena that are both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, and phenomena that are hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, arise by way of root condition. Conditioned by one hindrance-associated aggregate that is not a hindrance and the hindrance of sensual desire, three aggregates, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise…pe… conditioned by two aggregates…pe… (Cycle. Abbreviated.) (3)

Nahetupaccayo

Non-Root Condition

96. Nīvaraṇañceva [M 3.0332] nīvaraṇasampayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ [T 3.0386] paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (1)

96. Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated arises by way of non-root condition. Conditioned by the hindrance of doubt, the hindrance of ignorance arises; conditioned by the hindrance of restlessness, the hindrance of ignorance arises. (1)

Nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ. (1)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated arises by way of non-root condition. Conditioned by the aggregates accompanied by doubt and by restlessness, the hindrance of ignorance arises. (1)

Nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañca nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchānīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccanīvaraṇañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca avijjānīvaraṇaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated, and a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance, a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated arises by way of non-root condition. Conditioned by the hindrance of doubt and the associated aggregates, the hindrance of ignorance arises; conditioned by the hindrance of restlessness and the associated aggregates, the hindrance of ignorance arises. (Abbreviated.) (1)

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

100. Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0333] ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttassa [T 3.0387][V 3.0411] ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

100. A phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated is a condition for a phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated by way of root condition. The roots that are both hindrances and hindrance-associated are a condition for the associated hindrances by way of root condition. (1)

Nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is both a hindrance and hindrance-associated is a condition for a phenomenon that is hindrance-associated but not a hindrance by way of root condition. The roots that are both hindrances and hindrance-associated are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (2)

Nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ca nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance is a condition for a state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance, and for a state that is associated with a hindrance but not a hindrance, by way of root condition. The roots, which are hindrances and states associated with hindrances, are a condition for the associated aggregates and for the hindrances by way of root condition. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

101. Nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) nīvaraṇe ārabbha nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

101. A state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance is a condition for a state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance by way of object condition. Taking a hindrance as object, hindrances arise. (The root should be applied.) Taking a hindrance as object, aggregates that are associated with a hindrance but are not hindrances arise. (The root should be applied.) Taking a hindrance as object, hindrances and associated aggregates arise. (3)

Nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇasampayutte ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe ārabbha nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nīvaraṇasampayutte ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe ārabbha nīvaraṇā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) nīvaraṇasampayutte ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe ārabbha nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā [T 3.0388] ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A state associated with a hindrance but not itself a hindrance is a condition for a state associated with a hindrance but not itself a hindrance by way of object condition. Taking as object the aggregates that are associated with a hindrance but are not a hindrance, aggregates that are associated with a hindrance but are not hindrances arise. (The root should be questioned.) Taking as object the aggregates that are associated with a hindrance but are not a hindrance, hindrances arise. (The root should be questioned.) Taking as object the aggregates that are associated with a hindrance but are not a hindrance, hindrances and associated aggregates arise. (3)

Nīvaraṇo [M 3.0334] ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi. (3)

A state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance, and a state that is associated with a hindrance but not a hindrance, are a condition for a state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance by way of object condition… three. (3)

Adhipatipaccayādi

Dominance Condition, etc.

102. Nīvaraṇo [V 3.0412] ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca dhammo nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati… tīṇi (garukārammaṇāyeva).

102. A state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance is a condition for a state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance by way of dominance condition: as object-dominance… three (only with weighty objects).

Nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati nīvaraṇasampayutte ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe garuṃ katvā nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā khandhā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) ārammaṇādhipati – nīvaraṇasampayutte ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe garuṃ katvā nīvaraṇā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) ārammaṇādhipati – nīvaraṇasampayutte ceva no ca nīvaraṇe khandhe garuṃ katvā nīvaraṇā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state associated with a hindrance but not itself a hindrance is a condition for a state associated with a hindrance but not itself a hindrance by way of dominance condition: as object-dominance and co-nascence-dominance. As object-dominance: having regarded as weighty the aggregates associated with a hindrance but not themselves hindrances, aggregates associated with a hindrance but not themselves hindrances arise. As co-nascence-dominance: the dominant states associated with a hindrance but not themselves hindrances are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (The root should be applied.) As object-dominance: having regarded as weighty the aggregates associated with a hindrance but not themselves hindrances, hindrances arise. As co-nascence-dominance: the dominant states associated with a hindrance but not themselves hindrances are a condition for the associated hindrances by way of dominance condition. (The root should be applied.) As object-dominance: having regarded as weighty the aggregates associated with a hindrance but not themselves hindrances, hindrances and the associated aggregates arise. As co-nascence-dominance: the dominant states associated with a hindrance but not themselves hindrances are a condition for the associated aggregates and the hindrances by way of dominance condition. (3)

103. Nīvaraṇo ceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇo ca dhammā nīvaraṇassa ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo [T 3.0389] – ārammaṇādhipati… tīṇi. (3)

103. A state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance, and a state that is associated with a hindrance but not itself a hindrance, are a condition for a state that is a hindrance and associated with a hindrance by way of dominance condition: as object-dominance… three. (3)

Anantarapaccayena paccayo (āvajjanāpi vuṭṭhānampi natthi, sabbattha purimā purimā kātabbā)… samanantarapaccayena paccayo… nava… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… nava… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nava… nissayapaccayena paccayo… nava… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… nava (ārammaṇasadisaṃ, vipāko natthi)… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… pañca.

It is a condition by way of proximity condition (there is neither adverting nor emergence; in all cases, the preceding should be applied)… it is a condition by way of contiguity condition… nine… it is a condition by way of conascence condition… nine… it is a condition by way of mutuality condition… nine… it is a condition by way of support condition… nine… it is a condition by way of decisive support condition… nine (similar to object condition; there is no resultant)… it is a condition by way of repetition condition… five.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

104. Nīvaraṇasampayutto [M 3.0335][V 3.0413] ceva no ca nīvaraṇo dhammo nīvaraṇasampayuttassa ceva no ca nīvaraṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ nīvaraṇānañca kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

104. A state that is associated with a hindrance but is not a hindrance is a condition for a state that is associated with a hindrance but is not a hindrance by way of kamma condition. Volition that is associated with a hindrance but is not a hindrance is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (The root should be applied.) Volition that is associated with a hindrance but is not a hindrance is a condition for the associated hindrances by way of kamma condition. (The root should be applied.) Volition that is associated with a hindrance but is not a hindrance is a condition for the associated aggregates and the hindrances by way of kamma condition. (3)

105. A state that is associated with a hindrance but is not a hindrance is a condition for a state that is associated with a hindrance but is not a hindrance by way of nutriment condition… three… by way of faculty condition… three… by way of jhāna condition… three… by way of path condition… three… by way of association condition… nine… by way of presence condition… nine… by way of absence condition… nine… by way of disappearance condition… nine… by way of non-disappearance condition… nine.

10. Parāmāsaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā noparāmāso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – parāmāsaṃ paccayā sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (1)

10. Conditioned by a phenomenon of grasping, a phenomenon not of grasping arises by root condition—conditioned by grasping, the associated aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. (1)

Noparāmāsaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā noparāmāso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noparāmāsaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva ajjhattikā mahābhūtā), vatthuṃ paccayā noparāmāsā khandhā. (1)

Conditioned by a phenomenon not of grasping, a phenomenon not of grasping arises by root condition—conditioned by one aggregate not of grasping, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise… and so on… conditioned by two aggregates… and so on… at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on… (up to the internal great elements), conditioned by the base, the aggregates not of grasping arise. (1)

Noparāmāsaṃ [T 3.0394] dhammaṃ paccayā parāmāso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noparāmāse khandhe paccayā parāmāso, vatthuṃ paccayā parāmāso. (2)

Conditioned by a phenomenon not of grasping, a phenomenon of grasping arises by root condition—conditioned by the aggregates not of grasping, grasping arises; conditioned by the base, grasping arises. (2)

Noparāmāsaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā parāmāso ca noparāmāso ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā [V 3.0420] – noparāmāsaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā parāmāso [M 3.0340] ca cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vatthuṃ paccayā parāmāso, mahābhūte paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā parāmāso ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā. (3)

Due to a non-clinging state, both a clinging state and a non-clinging state arise by root condition—due to one non-clinging aggregate, three aggregates, clinging, and mind-originated matter arise… and so on… due to two aggregates… and so on… due to the base, clinging arises; due to the great elements, mind-originated matter arises; due to the base, clinging and the associated aggregates arise. (3)

11. Parāmāsañca noparāmāsañca dhammaṃ paccayā noparāmāso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noparāmāsaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca parāmāsañca paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… parāmāsañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, parāmāsañca mahābhūte ca paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, parāmāsañca vatthuñca paccayā noparāmāsā khandhā (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

11. Due to a state of both clinging and non-clinging, a non-clinging state arises by root condition—due to one non-clinging aggregate and clinging, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise… and so on… due to two aggregates and… and so on… due to clinging and the associated aggregates, mind-originated matter arises; due to clinging and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises; due to clinging and the base, the non-clinging aggregates arise (summarized). (1)

5. Saṃsaṭṭhavāro

5. The Concomitance Section

Parāmāsaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho noparāmāso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – parāmāsaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā sampayuttakā khandhā (evaṃ pañca pañhā kātabbā arūpeyeva, saṃsaṭṭhavāropi sampayuttavāropi evaṃ kātabbā).

Concomitant with a clinging state, a non-clinging state arises by root condition—the associated aggregates concomitant with clinging arise (thus five questions should be made only in the formless realm; the Concomitance Section and the Association Section should also be done thus).
