Suddhaṃ

Pure

374. Hetuyā [V 3.0639] pañca, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā tīṇi, anantare tīṇi, samanantare tīṇi, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe pañca, nissaye pañca, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte ekaṃ, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme pañca, vipāke pañca (sabbattha pañca), sampayutte tīṇi, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā pañca, natthiyā tīṇi, vigate tīṇi, avigate pañca.

374. By root condition, five; by object condition, three; by dominance condition, three; by contiguity condition, three; by immediate contiguity condition, three; by conascence condition, five; by reciprocity condition, five; by support condition, five; by decisive support condition, three; by prenascence condition, one; by repetition condition, one; by kamma condition, five; by result condition, five (in all cases, five); by association condition, three; by dissociation condition, five; by presence condition, five; by absence condition, three; by disappearance condition, three; by non-disappearance condition, five.

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. Negative Permutation of Conditions

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. Analysis Section

Nahetupaccayo

Non-Root Condition

375. Upādā dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca noupādā khandhā. (1)

375. Dependent on a phenomenon subject to clinging, a phenomenon not subject to clinging arises by way of non-root condition: at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, aggregates not subject to clinging arise dependent on the physical base. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ noupādā ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate [M 3.0519] khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, a phenomenon not subject to clinging arises by way of non-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate not subject to clinging, three aggregates not subject to clinging and mind-originated matter arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking... and so on... dependent on one great element... and so on... for non-percipient beings, dependent on one great element, three great elements arise... and so on... dependent on two great elements, two great elements arise; dependent on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetuke noupādā khandhe paṭicca upādā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca upādā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā)[T 4.0184]. (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, a phenomenon subject to clinging arises by way of non-root condition: dependent on rootless aggregates not subject to clinging, mind-originated matter subject to clinging arises; at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking... and so on... dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter subject to clinging, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise... and so on... (up to non-percipient beings). (2)

Noupādā [V 3.0640] dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ noupādā ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā upādā ca noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, both phenomena subject to clinging and phenomena not subject to clinging arise by way of non-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate not subject to clinging, three aggregates and both mind-originated matter subject to clinging and not subject to clinging arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates... and so on... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking... and so on.... (3)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe noupādā ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe…. (1)

Dependent on a phenomenon subject to clinging and a phenomenon not subject to clinging, a phenomenon not subject to clinging arises by way of non-root condition: at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate not subject to clinging and the physical base, three aggregates arise... and so on... dependent on two aggregates and... and so on.... (1)

Naārammaṇapaccayādi

Non-Object Condition, etc.

376. Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – noupādā khandhe paṭicca noupādā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā) dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā. (1)

376. Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, a phenomenon not subject to clinging arises by way of non-object condition: dependent on aggregates not subject to clinging, mind-originated matter not subject to clinging arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on... dependent on one great element... and so on... (up to non-percipient beings) dependent on two great elements, two great elements arise. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – noupādā khandhe paṭicca upādā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca upādā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ (yāva asaññasattā). (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, a phenomenon subject to clinging arises by way of non-object condition: dependent on aggregates not subject to clinging, mind-originated matter subject to clinging arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on... dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter subject to clinging, kamma-originated matter, and derived matter arise (up to non-percipient beings). (2)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti naārammaṇapaccayā – noupādā khandhe paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, both phenomena subject to clinging and phenomena not subject to clinging arise by way of non-object condition: dependent on aggregates not subject to clinging, both mind-originated matter subject to clinging and not subject to clinging arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking... and so on.... (3)

Naadhipatipaccayā pañca, naanantarapaccayā tīṇi…pe… naupanissayapaccayā pañca, napurejātapaccayā pañca, napacchājātapaccayā pañca, naāsevanapaccayā pañca.

By way of non-dominance condition, five; by way of non-contiguity condition, three... and so on... by way of non-decisive support condition, five; by way of non-prenascence condition, five; by way of non-postnascence condition, five; by way of non-repetition condition, five.

Nakammapaccayo

Non-Kamma Condition

377. Noupādā [M 3.0520] dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā [T 4.0185] – noupādā [V 3.0641] khandhe paṭicca sampayuttakā cetanā; bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā. (1)

377. Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, a phenomenon not subject to clinging arises by way of non-kamma condition: dependent on aggregates not subject to clinging, associated volition arises; external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated... and so on... dependent on two great elements, two great elements arise. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – bāhire āhārasamuṭṭhāne utusamuṭṭhāne mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, a phenomenon subject to clinging arises by way of non-kamma condition: dependent on external, nutriment-originated, and temperature-originated great elements, derived matter arises. (2)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti nakammapaccayā – bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā upādā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon not subject to clinging, both phenomena subject to clinging and phenomena not subject to clinging arise by way of non-kamma condition: dependent on one external, nutriment-originated, or temperature-originated great element, three great elements and derived matter arise... and so on... dependent on two great elements... and so on.... (3)

Navipākapaccayo

Non-Result Condition

378. Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati navipākapaccayā – noupādā ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā, evaṃ tīṇi noupādāmūlake).

378. Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, an unclung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-result condition: dependent on one unclung-to aggregate, the three other aggregates and unclung-to mind-originated matter arise …and so on… two aggregates …and so on… one great element …and so on… (up to non-percipient beings; thus the three cases with an unclung-to root).

Naāhārapaccayo

Non-nutriment condition.

379. Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati naāhārapaccayā – bāhiraṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā. (1)

379. Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, an unclung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-nutriment condition: for external, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, dependent on one great element …and so on… dependent on two great elements, two great elements arise. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā dhammo uppajjati naāhārapaccayā – bāhiraṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-nutriment condition: dependent on the great elements of external, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, derived matter arises. (2)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti naāhārapaccayā – bāhiraṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā upādā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte…pe…. (3)

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, both clung-to and unclung-to phenomena arise by way of non-nutriment condition: for external, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, dependent on one great element, the three other great elements and clung-to matter arise …and so on… dependent on two great elements …and so on…. (3)

Naindriyapaccayo

Non-faculty condition.

380. Noupādā [T 4.0186] dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati naindriyapaccayā – bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

380. Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, an unclung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-faculty condition: for external, nutriment-originated, and temperature-originated matter, dependent on one great element …and so on…. (1)

Noupādā [M 3.0521][V 3.0642] dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā dhammo uppajjati naindriyapaccayā – bāhire āhārasamuṭṭhāne utusamuṭṭhāne asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca rūpajīvitindriyaṃ.

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-faculty condition: dependent on the great elements of external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, the material life faculty arises.

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti naindriyapaccayā – bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (3)

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, both clung-to and unclung-to phenomena arise by way of non-faculty condition: for external, nutriment-originated, and temperature-originated matter, dependent on one great element …and so on…. (3)

Najhānapaccayādi

Non-jhāna condition, and so on.

381. Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – pañcaviññāṇasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā. (1)

381. Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, an unclung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-jhāna condition: dependent on one aggregate associated with the five sense-consciousnesses, the three other aggregates arise …and so on… dependent on two aggregates …and so on… for external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter …and so on… dependent on two great elements, two great elements arise. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – bāhire āhārasamuṭṭhāne utusamuṭṭhāne asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca upādā kaṭattārūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-jhāna condition: dependent on the great elements of external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, clung-to kamma-originated matter arises. (2)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti najhānapaccayā – bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā…pe… dve mahābhūte…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca upādā kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (3)

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, both clung-to and unclung-to phenomena arise by way of non-jhāna condition: for external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, dependent on one great element, the three other great elements arise …and so on… dependent on two great elements …and so on… dependent on the great elements, clung-to kamma-originated matter and derived matter arise. (3)

Upādā dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati namaggapaccayā pañca… nasampayuttapaccayā… tīṇi.

Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, an unclung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-path condition, five cases; … by way of non-association condition, three cases.

Navippayuttapaccayādi

Non-dissociation condition, and so on.

382. Noupādā [T 4.0187] dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā dhammo uppajjati navippayuttapaccayā – arūpe noupādā ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

382. Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, an unclung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the immaterial sphere, dependent on one unclung-to aggregate, the three other aggregates arise …and so on… dependent on two aggregates …and so on…; for external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, dependent on one great element …and so on…. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā dhammo uppajjati navippayuttapaccayā – bāhire āhārasamuṭṭhāne [V 3.0643] utusamuṭṭhāne asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca upādā kaṭattārūpaṃ, upādārūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-dissociation condition: dependent on the great elements of external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient beings' matter, clung-to kamma-originated matter and derived matter arise. (2)

Noupādā [M 3.0522] dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti navippayuttapaccayā – bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā upādā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā upādā ca rūpaṃ, asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ… nonatthipaccayā… novigatapaccayā. (3)

Dependent on an unclung-to phenomenon, both clung-to and unclung-to phenomena arise by way of non-dissociation condition: for external, nutriment-originated, or temperature-originated matter, dependent on one great element, the three other great elements and clung-to matter arise …and so on… dependent on two great elements, the two other great elements and clung-to matter arise. For non-percipient beings' matter, dependent on one great element, the three other great elements, kamma-originated matter, and derived matter arise …and so on… dependent on two great elements, the two other great elements, kamma-originated matter, and derived matter arise … by way of non-absence condition … by way of non-disappearance condition. (3)

383. Nahetuyā pañca, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā pañca, naanantare tīṇi, nasamanantare tīṇi, naaññamaññe tīṇi, naupanissaye tīṇi, napurejāte pañca, napacchājāte pañca, naāsevane pañca, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke tīṇi, naāhāre tīṇi, naindriye tīṇi, najhāne tīṇi, namagge pañca, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte tīṇi, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

383. Not by way of root condition, five; not by way of object condition, three; not by way of dominance condition, five; not by way of contiguity condition, three; not by way of immediate contiguity condition, three; not by way of mutuality condition, three; not by way of decisive support condition, three; not by way of prenascent condition, five; not by way of postnascent condition, five; not by way of repetition condition, five; not by way of kamma condition, three; not by way of result condition, three; not by way of nutriment condition, three; not by way of faculty condition, three; not by way of jhāna condition, three; not by way of path condition, five; not by way of association condition, three; not by way of dissociation condition, three; not by way of non-absence condition, three; not by way of non-disappearance condition, three.

384. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā pañca…pe… nakamme [T 4.0188] ekaṃ, navipāke tīṇi…pe… nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte ekaṃ, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

384. By way of root condition: not by way of object condition, three; not by way of dominance condition, five …and so on… not by way of kamma condition, one; not by way of result condition, three …and so on… not by way of association condition, three; not by way of dissociation condition, one; not by way of non-absence condition, three; not by way of non-disappearance condition, three.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Negative-Positive Analysis

385. Nahetupaccayā [V 3.0644] ārammaṇe tīṇi, anantare tīṇi, samanantare tīṇi, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe pañca, nissaye pañca, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte ekaṃ, āsevane ekaṃ…pe… magge ekaṃ…pe… avigate pañca.

385. Not by way of root condition: by way of object condition, three; by way of contiguity condition, three; by way of immediate contiguity condition, three; by way of conascence condition, five; by way of mutuality condition, five; by way of support condition, five; by way of decisive support condition, three; by way of prenascent condition, one; by way of repetition condition, one …and so on… by way of path condition, one …and so on… by way of non-disappearance condition, five.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

386. Upādā [M 3.0523] dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – vatthuṃ paccayā noupādā khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

386. Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by root condition: dependent on the physical basis, the not-clung-to aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe…. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi (noupādāmūlake tīṇipi paṭiccasadisā, ninnānākaraṇā). (3)

Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by root condition … three cases. (The three cases rooted in the not-clung-to are similar to those in the Conditional Relations Section, without any difference.) (3)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noupādā ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon and a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by root condition: dependent on one not-clung-to aggregate and the physical basis, the three other aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates and the physical basis …pe…; at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe…. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

387. Upādā [V 3.0645] dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā noupādā khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

387. Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by object condition: dependent on the eye base, eye-consciousness arises …pe… dependent on the body base, body-consciousness arises; dependent on the physical basis, the not-clung-to aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe…. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā… ekaṃ (paṭiccasadisaṃ). (1)

Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by object condition … one case. (This is similar to the Conditional Relations Section.) (1)

Upādā dhammañca noupādā dhammañca dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – cakkhuviññāṇasahagataṃ [T 4.0189] ekaṃ khandhañca cakkhāyatanañca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… kāyaviññāṇasahagataṃ…pe… noupādā ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon and a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by object condition: dependent on one aggregate associated with eye-consciousness and on the eye base, the three other aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe…; associated with body-consciousness …pe…; dependent on one not-clung-to aggregate and the physical basis, the three other aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe…; at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… (in brief). (1)

388. Hetuyā pañca, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā pañca, anantare tīṇi, samanantare tīṇi, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe pañca, nissaye pañca, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte tīṇi, āsevane tīṇi, kamme pañca…pe… avigate pañca (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

388. By root condition, five; by object condition, three; by dominance condition, five; by contiguity condition, three; by immediate contiguity condition, three; by conascence condition, five; by mutuality condition, five; by support condition, five; by decisive support condition, three; by prenascent condition, three; by repetition condition, three; by kamma condition, five …pe… by non-disappearance condition, five. (Thus it should be reckoned.)

1. The Chapter on Analysis

Nahetupaccayādi

By Non-Root Condition, etc.

389. Upādā [M 3.0524][V 3.0646] dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā ahetukā noupādā khandhā; ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vatthuṃ paccayā vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

389. Conditioned by a clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-root condition: conditioned by the eye base, eye-consciousness…pe… conditioned by the body base, body-consciousness; conditioned by the physical basis, rootless non-clinging aggregates; at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking…pe… conditioned by the physical basis, delusion accompanied by doubt and by restlessness. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ noupādā ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā) vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paccayā vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho (tīṇipi paṭiccasadisā, ninnānākaraṇā). (3)

Conditioned by a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-root condition: conditioned by one rootless non-clinging aggregate, three non-clinging aggregates and mind-originated materiality …pe… two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking …pe… one great element …pe… (up to non-percipient beings); conditioned by the aggregates accompanied by doubt and by restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and by restlessness (all three are similar to the Conditional Relations Section, without any difference). (3)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – cakkhuviññāṇasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca cakkhāyatanañca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve [T 4.0190] khandhe ca…pe… kāyaviññāṇasahagataṃ…pe… ahetukaṃ noupādā ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

Conditioned by a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-root condition: conditioned by one aggregate associated with eye-consciousness and the eye base, three aggregates …pe… and two aggregates …pe… associated with body-consciousness …pe… conditioned by one rootless non-clinging aggregate and the physical basis, three aggregates …pe… and two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… conditioned by the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness and the physical basis, delusion accompanied by doubt and by restlessness. (1)

Naārammaṇapaccayā tīṇi, naāsevanapaccayā pañca.

By non-object condition, three; by non-repetition condition, five.

Nakammapaccayādi

By Non-Kamma Condition, etc.

390. Upādā dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – vatthuṃ paccayā noupādā cetanā. (1)

390. Conditioned by a clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-kamma condition: conditioned by the physical basis, non-clinging volition. (1)

Noupādā [V 3.0647] dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – noupādā khandhe paccayā sampayuttakā cetanā; bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte paccayā dve mahābhūtā. (1)

Conditioned by a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-kamma condition: conditioned by non-clinging aggregates, associated volition; external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated …pe… conditioned by two great elements, two great elements. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paccayā upādā dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – bāhire āhārasamuṭṭhāne utusamuṭṭhāne mahābhūte paccayā upādārūpaṃ. (2)

Conditioned by a non-clinging phenomenon, a clinging phenomenon arises by non-kamma condition: conditioned by the external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated great elements, derived materiality. (2)

Noupādā [M 3.0525] dhammaṃ paccayā upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti nakammapaccayā – bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paccayā tayo mahābhūtā upādā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte…pe…. (3)

Conditioned by a non-clinging phenomenon, clinging and non-clinging phenomena arise by non-kamma condition: conditioned by one external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated great element, three great elements and derived materiality …pe… two great elements …pe…. (3)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – noupādā khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā noupādā cetanā. (1)

Conditioned by a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-kamma condition: conditioned by non-clinging aggregates and the physical basis, non-clinging volition. (1)

Navipākapaccayā pañca, naāhārapaccayā tīṇi, naindriyapaccayā tīṇi.

By non-result condition, five; by non-nutriment condition, three; by non-faculty condition, three.

Najhānapaccayādi

By Non-Jhāna Condition, etc.

391. Upādā dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā [T 4.0191] – cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ. (1)

391. Conditioned by a clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-jhāna condition: conditioned by the eye base, eye-consciousness …pe… conditioned by the body base, body-consciousness. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – pañcaviññāṇasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūte paccayā dve mahābhūtā. (1)

Conditioned by a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by non-jhāna condition: conditioned by one aggregate accompanied by the five kinds of consciousness, three aggregates …pe… two aggregates …pe… external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, of non-percipient beings …pe… conditioned by two great elements, two great elements. (1)

Noupādā dhammaṃ paccayā upādā dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – bāhire āhārasamuṭṭhāne utusamuṭṭhāne asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paccayā upādā kaṭattārūpaṃ. (2)

Conditioned by a non-clung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises by non-jhāna condition: conditioned by external, nutriment-originated, and temperature-originated great elements, and by the great elements of non-percipient beings, clung-to kamma-produced materiality. (2)

Noupādā [V 3.0648] dhammaṃ paccayā upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā uppajjanti najhānapaccayā – bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paccayā tayo mahābhūtā upādā ca kaṭattārūpaṃ…pe… dve…pe…. (3)

Conditioned by a non-clung-to phenomenon, clung-to and non-clung-to phenomena arise by non-jhāna condition: conditioned by one great element—be it external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, or of non-percipient beings—three great elements and clung-to kamma-produced materiality …pe… two …pe…. (3)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammaṃ paccayā noupādā dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – cakkhuviññāṇasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhañca cakkhāyatanañca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe…. (1)

Conditioned by a clung-to phenomenon and a non-clung-to phenomenon, a non-clung-to phenomenon arises by non-jhāna condition: conditioned by one aggregate associated with eye-consciousness and the eye base, three aggregates …pe… and two aggregates …pe…. (1)

Namaggapaccayā pañca, nasampayuttapaccayā tīṇi, navippayuttapaccayā tīṇi, nonatthipaccayā tīṇi, novigatapaccayā tīṇi.

By non-path condition, five; by non-association condition, three; by non-dissociation condition, three; by non-absence condition, three; by non-disappearance condition, three.

1-4. Paccayānulomādi

1-4. The Conditional-Positive, etc.

393. Noupādā [V 3.0649] dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho noupādā dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noupādā ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe saṃsaṭṭhā dve khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (saṃkhittaṃ).

393. Mixed with a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by way of root condition—mixed with one not-clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise... pe... mixed with two aggregates, two aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking... pe... (in brief).

Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ, adhipatiyā ekaṃ (sabbattha ekaṃ), avigate ekaṃ.

By way of root condition, one; by way of object condition, one; by way of dominance condition, one (in all, one); by way of non-disappearance condition, one.

Anulomaṃ.

Positive.

Noupādā dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho noupādā dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ noupādā ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe saṃsaṭṭho vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho (saṃkhittaṃ).

A not-clung-to phenomenon mixed with a not-clung-to phenomenon arises by way of non-root condition—mixed with one rootless not-clung-to aggregate, three aggregates... pe... two aggregates... pe... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking... pe... delusion concomitant with doubt and restlessness, mixed with aggregates concomitant with doubt and restlessness, arises (in brief).

Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naadhipatiyā ekaṃ, napurejāte ekaṃ, napacchājāte ekaṃ, naāsevane ekaṃ, nakamme ekaṃ, navipāke ekaṃ, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, navippayutte ekaṃ.

By way of non-root condition, one; by way of non-dominance condition, one; by way of non-prenascence condition, one; by way of non-postnascence condition, one; by way of non-repetition condition, one; by way of non-kamma condition, one; by way of non-result condition, one; by way of non-jhāna condition, one; by way of non-path condition, one; by way of non-dissociation condition, one.

Paccanīyaṃ.

Negative.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition.

394. Noupādā [M 3.0527][V 3.0650] dhammo noupādā dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – noupādā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

394. A not-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a not-clung-to phenomenon by way of root condition—not-clung-to roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for the not-clung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... pe... (1)

Noupādā dhammo upādā dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – noupādā [T 4.0193] hetū upādā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A not-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of root condition—not-clung-to roots are a condition for clung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... pe... (2)

Noupādā dhammo upādā ca noupādā ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – noupādā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ upādā ca noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A not-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for both clung-to and not-clung-to phenomena by way of root condition—not-clung-to roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for both clung-to and not-clung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... pe... (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition.

395. Upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ… rūpe…pe… rase vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… rasāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo, upādā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

395. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a not-clung-to phenomenon by way of object condition—the eye... pe... the body... forms... pe... tastes, one regards the physical base as impermanent... pe... grief arises; with the divine eye one sees forms; with the divine ear-element one hears sounds. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness... pe... the taste base is a condition for tongue-consciousness by way of object condition; the clung-to aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of the kinds of psychic power, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ [V 3.0651]…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ariyā pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe…pe… phoṭṭhabbe noupādā khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; cetopariyañāṇena [T 4.0194] noupādācittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti[M 3.0528], ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; noupādā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A not-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a not-clung-to phenomenon by way of object condition—having given a gift... pe... undertaken the precepts... pe... performed the observance-day kamma, one reviews it, savors it, and delights in it; taking that as object, lust arises... pe... grief arises; having previously... pe... attained the jhānas... pe... noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, the fruition... pe... Nibbāna... pe... Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruition, and for adverting, by way of object condition. Noble ones review the defilements they have abandoned, the defilements they have suppressed... pe... having previously... pe... one regards the not-clung-to aggregates connected with tangible objects as impermanent... pe... grief arises; with the knowledge of others’ minds one knows the mind of one who is endowed with not-clung-to consciousness; the base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness... pe... the base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... pe... the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object condition; the not-clung-to aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of the kinds of psychic power, the knowledge of others’ minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of beings' passing away and rebirth according to their kamma, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

396. Upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ… rūpe…pe… rase vatthuṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1)

396. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of dominance condition. By way of object-dominance: having esteemed the eye …pe… the body … forms …pe… tastes, the base, one savors and delights in it; having esteemed that, lust arises, wrong view arises. (1)

Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; phoṭṭhabbe noupādā khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – noupādādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of dominance condition: by way of object-dominance and conascence-dominance. By way of object-dominance: having given a gift …pe… undertaken the precepts …pe… performed the Uposatha observance, one esteems it and reviews it, savors and delights in it; having esteemed that, lust arises, wrong view arises. Having esteemed previously well-practiced deeds …pe… having emerged from jhāna, one esteems the jhāna …pe… having emerged from the noble path, the noble ones esteem the path …pe… the fruit …pe… Nibbāna and review it. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit by way of dominance condition. Having esteemed tangible objects and the non-clung-to aggregates, one savors and delights in them; having esteemed them, lust arises, wrong view arises. By way of conascence-dominance: a non-clung-to dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for non-clung-to mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (1)

Noupādā [V 3.0652] dhammo upādā [T 4.0195] dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – noupādādhipati upādā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of dominance condition. By way of conascence-dominance: a non-clung-to dominant factor is a condition for clung-to mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (2)

Noupādā dhammo upādā ca noupādā ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – noupādādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ upādā ca noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon and a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of dominance condition. By way of conascence-dominance: a non-clung-to dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for clung-to and non-clung-to mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (3)

Anantarapaccayādi

Proximity Condition, etc.

397. Noupādā [M 3.0529] dhammo noupādā dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā noupādā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ noupādā khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

397. A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of proximity condition. Preceding non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for succeeding non-clung-to aggregates by way of proximity condition; conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage …pe… for the attainment of fruition by way of proximity condition. (1)

Samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccasadisaṃ)… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccasadisaṃ)… nissayapaccayena paccayo (paccayavāre nissayasadisaṃ).

… is a condition by way of contiguity condition … by way of conascence condition (as in the Dependent Origination Section) … by way of mutuality condition (as in the Dependent Origination Section) … by way of support condition (as in the Support section of the Condition-triplets).

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

398. Upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – cakkhusampadaṃ…pe… kāyasampadaṃ… vaṇṇasampadaṃ… saddasampadaṃ… gandhasampadaṃ… rasasampadaṃ… bhojanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati, cakkhusampadā…pe… kāyasampadā… vaṇṇasampadā… saddasampadā… gandhasampadā… rasasampadā… bhojanaṃ saddhāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

398. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: by way of object decisive support, natural decisive support …pe…. By way of natural decisive support: relying on excellence of the eye faculty …pe… excellence of the body faculty … excellence of appearance … excellence of voice … excellence of fragrance … excellence of taste … food, one gives a gift …pe… splits the Sangha. Excellence of the eye faculty …pe… excellence of the body faculty … excellence of appearance … excellence of voice … excellence of fragrance … excellence of taste … food is a condition for faith …pe… for the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo[T 4.0196], anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ [V 3.0653]…pe… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: by way of object decisive support, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support …pe…. By way of natural decisive support: relying on faith, one gives a gift …pe… generates an attainment, utters conceit, adopts a wrong view; relying on virtue …pe… wisdom … lust …pe… aspiration … bodily pleasure … bodily pain … climate … lodging, one gives a gift …pe… splits the Sangha. Faith …pe… lodging is a condition for faith …pe… for the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Purejātapaccayo

Prenascence Condition

399. Upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… rasāyatanaṃ [M 3.0530] jivhāviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… vatthu noupādā khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

399. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of prenascence condition: by way of object-prenascence and base-prenascence. By way of object-prenascence: regarding the eye …pe… the physical base as impermanent …pe… displeasure arises; with the divine eye one sees a form; with the divine ear element one hears a sound. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the taste base for tongue-consciousness …pe…. By way of base-prenascence: the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body base …pe… the physical base is a condition for the non-clung-to aggregates by way of prenascence condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – phoṭṭhabbe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of prenascence condition. By way of object-prenascence: regarding tangible objects as impermanent …pe… displeasure arises; the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of prenascence condition. (1)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā noupādā dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca kāyāyatanañca kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo; phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca vatthu ca noupādā khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A clung-to phenomenon and a non-clung-to phenomenon are conditions for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of prenascence condition: by way of object-prenascence and base-prenascence. The tangible-object base and the body base are conditions for body-consciousness by way of prenascence condition; the tangible-object base and the physical base are conditions for the non-clung-to aggregates by way of prenascence condition. (1)

Pacchājātāsevanapaccayā

Postnascence and Repetition Conditions

400. Noupādā [T 4.0197] dhammo noupādā dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa noupādā kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) pacchājātā noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādā kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) pacchājātā noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādā kāyassa ca noupādā kāyassa ca pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

400. A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of postnascence condition. Postnascent non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent non-clung-to body by way of postnascence condition. (The root should be questioned.) Postnascent non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clung-to body by way of postnascence condition. (The root should be questioned.) Postnascent non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for both this prenascent clung-to body and non-clung-to body by way of postnascence condition. (3)

Āsevanapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ.

…is a condition by way of repetition condition... one.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma-condition

401. Noupādā [V 3.0654] dhammo noupādā dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – noupādā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – noupādā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ noupādā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

401. An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of kamma-condition: by conascence and at a different moment. By conascence: unclung-to volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for unclung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe.... At a different moment: unclung-to volition is a condition for the resultant aggregates and for unclung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of kamma-condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo upādā dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – noupādā cetanā upādā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – noupādā cetanā upādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of kamma-condition: by conascence and at a different moment. By conascence: unclung-to volition is a condition for clung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe.... At a different moment: unclung-to volition is a condition for clung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of kamma-condition. (2)

Noupādā [M 3.0531] dhammo upādā ca noupādā ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – noupādā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ upādā [T 4.0198] ca noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – noupādā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ upādā ca noupādā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon and an unclung-to phenomenon by way of kamma-condition: by conascence and at a different moment. By conascence: unclung-to volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for clung-to and unclung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe.... At a different moment: unclung-to volition is a condition for the resultant aggregates and for clung-to and unclung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of kamma-condition. (3)

Vipākapaccayo

Resultant-condition

402. Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko noupādā eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… tīṇi.

402. An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of resultant-condition. A resultant unclung-to one aggregate is a condition for three aggregates...pe... two aggregates...pe...; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe... Three.

Āhārapaccayo

Nutriment-condition

403. Upādā dhammo upādā dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādā kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa noupādā kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ pucchitabbaṃ) kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādā kāyassa ca noupādā kāyassa ca āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

403. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of nutriment-condition. Edible food is a condition for this clung-to body by way of nutriment-condition. (The root should be questioned.) Edible food is a condition for this unclung-to body by way of nutriment-condition. (The root should be questioned.) Edible food is a condition for both this clung-to body and this unclung-to body by way of nutriment-condition. (3)

Noupādā [V 3.0655] dhammo noupādā dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – noupādā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (noupādāmūlake tīṇi, paṭisandhikkhaṇe tīṇipi kātabbā). (3)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of nutriment-condition. Unclung-to nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates and for unclung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of nutriment-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe... (In the unclung-to root section there are three; at the moment of rebirth-linking all three should be stated.) (3)

Indriyapaccayo

Faculty-condition

404. Upādā dhammo upādā dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – rūpajīvitindriyaṃ upādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyindriyaṃ [T 4.0199] kāyaviññāṇassa rūpajīvitindriyaṃ noupādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) rūpajīvitindriyaṃ upādā ca noupādā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (3)

404. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of faculty-condition: the material life faculty is a condition for clung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of faculty-condition. (The root should be stated.) The eye faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness...pe... the body faculty is a condition for body-consciousness; the material life faculty is a condition for unclung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of faculty-condition. (The root should be stated.) The material life faculty is a condition for both clung-to and unclung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of faculty-condition. (3)

Noupādā [M 3.0532] dhammo noupādā dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe….

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of faculty-condition... three; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe....

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā noupādā dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – cakkhundriyañca cakkhuviññāṇañca cakkhuviññāṇasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo…pe… kāyindriyañca…pe….

Clung-to and unclung-to phenomena are a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of faculty-condition. The eye faculty and eye-consciousness are a condition for the aggregates associated with eye-consciousness by way of faculty-condition...pe... the body faculty and...pe....

Jhānapaccayādi

Jhāna-condition, etc.

405. No upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi, maggapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ.

405. An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of jhāna-condition... three; by way of path-condition... three; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe... by way of association-condition... one.

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation-condition

406. Upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu noupādā khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ [V 3.0656] – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… vatthu noupādā khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

406. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation-condition: by conascence and prenascence. By conascence: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition for the unclung-to aggregates by way of dissociation-condition. By prenascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness...pe... the body-base...pe... the physical base is a condition for the unclung-to aggregates by way of dissociation-condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – noupādā khandhā noupādā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe noupādā khandhā noupādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa noupādā kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo[T 4.0200]. (1)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation-condition: by conascence and postnascence. By conascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for unclung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of dissociation-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, unclung-to aggregates are a condition for unclung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of dissociation-condition. By postnascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent unclung-to body by way of dissociation-condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo upādā dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – noupādā khandhā upādā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādā kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation-condition: by conascence and postnascence. By conascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for clung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of dissociation-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe.... By postnascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clung-to body by way of dissociation-condition. (2)

Noupādā dhammo upādā dhammassa ca noupādā dhammassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – noupādā khandhā upādā [M 3.0533] ca noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādā kāyassa ca noupādā kāyassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon and an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation-condition: by conascence and postnascence. By conascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for clung-to and unclung-to mind-originated material phenomena by way of dissociation-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe.... By postnascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clung-to body and unclung-to body by way of dissociation-condition. (3)

Atthipaccayo

Presence-condition

407. Upādā dhammo upādā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; rūpajīvitindriyaṃ upādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

407. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of presence-condition—nutriment and faculty. Edible food is a condition for this clung-to body by way of presence-condition; the material life faculty is a condition for clung-to kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence-condition. (1)

Upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu noupādā khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ [V 3.0657] – cakkhuṃ aniccato…pe… (saṃkhittaṃ. Purejātasadisaṃ ninnānākaraṇaṃ). Kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa noupādā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; rūpajīvitindriyaṃ noupādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena [T 4.0201] paccayo. (2)

A clinging phenomenon is a condition for a non-clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—conascence, prenascence, nutriment, and faculty. Conascent: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition for the non-clinging aggregates by way of presence condition. Prenascent: the eye as impermanent...pe... (abbreviated; similar to prenascence, with no difference). Edible food is a condition for this non-clinging body by way of presence condition; the material life faculty is a condition for the non-clinging materiality produced by kamma by way of presence condition. (2)

Upādā dhammo upādā dhammassa ca noupādā dhammassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo – āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādā kāyassa ca noupādā kāyassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo; rūpajīvitindriyaṃ upādā ca noupādā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A clinging phenomenon is a condition for both a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—nutriment and faculty. Edible food is a condition for this clinging body and non-clinging body by way of presence condition; the material life faculty is a condition for both the clinging and non-clinging materiality produced by kamma by way of presence condition. (3)

408. Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajāto – noupādā eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo …pe… dve mahābhūtā dvinnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo (yāva asaññasattā). Purejātaṃ – phoṭṭhabbe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa noupādā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

408. A non-clinging phenomenon is a condition for a non-clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—conascence, prenascence, postnascence. Conascent: one non-clinging aggregate is a condition for the other three non-clinging aggregates and for the non-clinging material forms produced by consciousness by way of presence condition...pe... two aggregates...pe... at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe... one great element is a condition for the other three great elements by way of presence condition...pe... two great elements are a condition for the other two great elements by way of presence condition (up to non-percipient beings). Prenascent: the tangible as impermanent...pe... grief arises. The tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of presence condition. Postnascent: the non-clinging aggregates are a condition for this prenascent non-clinging body by way of presence condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo upādā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – noupādā khandhā upādā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ [M 3.0534] atthipaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clinging phenomenon is a condition for a clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—conascence and postnascence. Conascent: the non-clinging aggregates are a condition for the clinging material forms produced by consciousness by way of presence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe... Postnascent: the non-clinging aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clinging body by way of presence condition. (2)

Noupādā dhammo upādā ca noupādā ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajāto – noupādā eko khandho [T 4.0202] tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ upādā ca noupādā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādā kāyassa ca noupādā kāyassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-clinging phenomenon is a condition for both a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—conascence and postnascence. Conascent: one non-clinging aggregate is a condition for the other three non-clinging aggregates and for both the clinging and non-clinging material forms produced by consciousness by way of presence condition; two aggregates...pe... at the moment of rebirth-linking...pe... Postnascent: the non-clinging aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clinging body and non-clinging body by way of presence condition. (3)

409. Upādā [V 3.0658] ca noupādā ca dhammā upādā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa upādā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca upādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

409. Clinging and non-clinging phenomena are a condition for a clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—postnascence, nutriment, faculty. Postnascent: non-clinging aggregates and edible food are a condition for this clinging body by way of presence condition. Postnascent: non-clinging aggregates and the material life faculty are a condition for the clinging materiality produced by kamma by way of presence condition. (1)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā noupādā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – cakkhuviññāṇasahagato eko khandho ca cakkhāyatanañca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe… noupādā eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe noupādā eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. Purejātaṃ – phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca kāyāyatanañca kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca vatthu ca noupādā khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa noupādā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – noupādā [T 4.0203] khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca noupādā kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

Clinging and non-clinging phenomena are a condition for a non-clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, faculty. Conascent: one aggregate associated with eye-consciousness and the eye-base are a condition for the other three aggregates by way of presence condition...pe... two aggregates and...pe... one non-clinging aggregate and the physical base are a condition for the other three non-clinging aggregates by way of presence condition...pe... two aggregates and...pe... at the moment of rebirth-linking, one non-clinging aggregate and the physical base are a condition for the other three non-clinging aggregates by way of presence condition...pe... two aggregates and...pe... Prenascent: the tangible base and the body-base are a condition for body-consciousness by way of presence condition. The tangible base and the physical base are a condition for the non-clinging aggregates by way of presence condition. Postnascent: non-clinging aggregates and edible food are a condition for this non-clinging body by way of presence condition. Postnascent: non-clinging aggregates and the material life faculty are a condition for the non-clinging materiality produced by kamma by way of presence condition. (2)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā upādā dhammassa ca noupādā dhammassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo – pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Pacchājātā – noupādā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa upādā kāyassa ca noupādā kāyassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā [M 3.0535] – noupādā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca upādā ca noupādā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

Clinging and non-clinging phenomena are a condition for both a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon by way of presence condition—postnascence, nutriment, faculty. Postnascent: non-clinging aggregates and edible food are a condition for this clinging body and non-clinging body by way of presence condition. Postnascent: non-clinging aggregates and the material life faculty are a condition for both the clinging and non-clinging materiality produced by kamma by way of presence condition. (3)

Suddhaṃ

Pure

410. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe dve, adhipatiyā cattāri, anantare ekaṃ, samanantare ekaṃ[V 3.0659], sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe pañca, nissaye pañca, upanissaye dve, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme tīṇi, vipāke tīṇi, āhāre cha, indriye satta, jhāne tīṇi, magge tīṇi, sampayutte ekaṃ, vippayutte cattāri, atthiyā nava, natthiyā ekaṃ, vigate ekaṃ, avigate nava.

410. In root condition, three; in object condition, two; in dominance condition, four; in contiguity condition, one; in immediate proximity condition, one; in conascence condition, five; in mutuality condition, five; in support condition, five; in decisive support condition, two; in prenascence condition, three; in postnascence condition, three; in repetition condition, one; in kamma condition, three; in result condition, three; in nutriment condition, six; in faculty condition, seven; in jhāna condition, three; in path condition, three; in association condition, one; in dissociation condition, four; in presence condition, nine; in absence condition, one; in disappearance condition, one; in non-disappearance condition, nine.

Anulomaṃ.

Positive Application

Paccanīyuddhāro

Negative Exposition

411. Upādā dhammo upādā dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

411. A clinging phenomenon is a condition for a clinging phenomenon by nutriment condition … by faculty condition. (1)

Upādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is fuel for clinging is a condition for a state that is not fuel for clinging by way of object condition … by way of conascence condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition … by way of nutriment condition … by way of faculty condition. (2)

Upādā dhammo upādā dhammassa ca noupādā dhammassa ca āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena [T 4.0204] paccayo. (3)

A state that is fuel for clinging is a condition for a state that is fuel for clinging and for a state that is not fuel for clinging by way of nutriment condition … by way of faculty condition. (3)

412. Noupādā dhammo noupādā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

412. A state that is not fuel for clinging is a condition for a state that is not fuel for clinging by way of object condition … by way of conascence condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition … by way of postnascence condition … by way of kamma condition. (1)

Noupādā dhammo upādā dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is not fuel for clinging is a condition for a state that is fuel for clinging by way of conascence condition … by way of postnascence condition … by way of kamma condition. (2)

Noupādā [M 3.0536] dhammo upādā dhammassa ca noupādā dhammassa ca sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is not fuel for clinging is a condition for a state that is fuel for clinging and for a state that is not fuel for clinging by way of conascence condition … by way of postnascence condition … by way of kamma condition. (3)

Upādā [V 3.0660] ca noupādā ca dhammā upādā dhammassa pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (1)

States that are fuel for clinging and states that are not fuel for clinging are a condition for a state that is fuel for clinging by way of postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. (1)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā noupādā dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

States that are fuel for clinging and states that are not fuel for clinging are a condition for a state that is not fuel for clinging by way of conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. (2)

Upādā ca noupādā ca dhammā upādā dhammassa ca noupādā dhammassa ca pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (3)

States that are fuel for clinging and states that are not fuel for clinging are a condition for a state that is fuel for clinging and for a state that is not fuel for clinging by way of postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. (3)

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. Condition-Negative

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Enumeration Section

Suddhaṃ

Pure

413. Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe nava (sabbattha nava), nasampayutte nava, navippayutte cha, noatthiyā cattāri, nonatthiyā nava, novigate nava, noavigate cattāri.

413. In not-root condition, nine; in not-object condition, nine (in all cases, nine); in not-association condition, nine; in not-dissociation condition, six; in not-presence condition, four; in not-absence condition, nine; in not-disappearance condition, nine; in not-non-disappearance condition, four.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. Condition-Positive-Negative

414. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā tīṇi, naanantare tīṇi, nasamanantare tīṇi, naaññamaññe tīṇi, naupanissaye tīṇi [T 4.0205] (sabbattha tīṇi), nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte ekaṃ, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

414. In root condition: in not-object condition, three; in not-dominance condition, three; in not-contiguity condition, three; in not-immediate proximity condition, three; in not-mutuality condition, three; in not-decisive support condition, three (in all cases, three); in not-association condition, three; in not-dissociation condition, one; in not-absence condition, three; in not-disappearance condition, three.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Condition-Negative-Positive

415. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe dve, adhipatiyā cattāri…pe… (anulomamātikā vitthāretabbā)…pe… avigate nava.

415. In not-root condition: in object condition, two; in dominance condition, four … (the positive application matrix should be elaborated) … in non-disappearance condition, nine.

Upādādukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Couplet on Fuel for Clinging is finished.

68. Upādinnadukaṃ

68. The Couplet on the Clung-to

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

416. Upādinnaṃ [M 3.0537][V 3.0661] dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

416. Dependent on a clung-to state, a clung-to state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise … etc. … two aggregates … etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-born matter arise … etc. … two aggregates … etc. Dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis; dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates. Dependent on one great element … etc. … dependent on the great elements, kamma-born matter and derived matter arise. (1)

Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – upādinne khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on a clung-to state, a not-clung-to state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on the clung-to aggregates, mind-originated matter arises. (2)

Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a clung-to state, clung-to and not-clung-to states arise by way of root condition. Dependent on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise … etc. … two aggregates … etc. (3)

Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anupādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ [V 3.0662] paṭicca tayo khandhā [T 4.0206] cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

Dependent on a not-clung-to state, a not-clung-to state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on one not-clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise … etc. … two aggregates … etc. … Dependent on one great element … etc. … dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter and derived matter arise. (1)

Upādinnañca anupādinnañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – upādinne khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

Dependent on a clung-to state and a not-clung-to state, a not-clung-to state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on the clung-to aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

417. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. (1)

417. Dependent on a clung-to state, a clung-to state arises by way of object condition: dependent on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates arise. (1)

Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – anupādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

Dependent on a not-clung-to state, a not-clung-to state arises by way of object condition: dependent on one not-clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

418. Anupādinnaṃ [M 3.0538] dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – anupādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

418. An unclung-to state arises in dependence on an unclung-to state by way of dominance condition: in dependence on one unclung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise…pe… in dependence on two aggregates…pe… in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, mind-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. (In brief.)

Suddhaṃ

Pure

419. Hetuyā pañca, ārammaṇe dve, adhipatiyā ekaṃ, anantare dve, samanantare dve, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye pañca, upanissaye dve, purejāte dve, āsevane ekaṃ[V 3.0663], kamme pañca, vipāke pañca, āhāre pañca, indriye pañca, jhāne pañca, magge pañca, sampayutte dve, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā pañca, natthiyā dve, vigate dve, avigate [T 4.0207] pañca.

419. By root condition, five; by object condition, two; by dominance condition, one; by contiguity condition, two; by proximity condition, two; by co-nascence condition, five; by reciprocity condition, two; by support condition, five; by decisive support condition, two; by pre-nascence condition, two; by repetition condition, one; by kamma condition, five; by result condition, five; by nutriment condition, five; by faculty condition, five; by jhāna condition, five; by path condition, five; by association condition, two; by dissociation condition, five; by presence condition, five; by absence condition, two; by disappearance condition, two; by non-disappearance condition, five.
