1. Analysis Section

Nahetupaccayo

Not-Root Condition

420. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ, asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

420. A clung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to state by way of not-root condition: in dependence on a rootless clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… in dependence on two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, in dependence on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-originated materiality arise…pe… in dependence on two aggregates…pe… the aggregates are a condition for the base, the base is a condition for the aggregates, in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, kamma-originated materiality and derived materiality arise; for non-percipient beings, in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, kamma-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. (1)

Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetuke upādinne khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to state by way of not-root condition: in dependence on the rootless clung-to aggregates, mind-originated materiality arises. (2)

Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā uppajjanti nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

Both clung-to and unclung-to states arise in dependence on a clung-to state by way of not-root condition: in dependence on a rootless clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise…pe… in dependence on two aggregates…pe…. (3)

421. Anupādinnaṃ [M 3.0539] dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ anupādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ. Vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

421. An unclung-to state arises in dependence on an unclung-to state by way of not-root condition: in dependence on a rootless unclung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise…pe… in dependence on two aggregates…pe… in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, mind-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. External… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated, in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, derived materiality arises. In dependence on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, the delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Upādinnañca [V 3.0664] anupādinnañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetuke upādinne [T 4.0208] khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on both a clung-to state and an unclung-to state by way of not-root condition: in dependence on the rootless clung-to aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated materiality arises. (1)

Naārammaṇapaccayo

Not-Object Condition

422. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe upādinne khandhe paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ, khandhe paṭicca vatthu, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

422. A clung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to state by way of not-object condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on the clung-to aggregates, kamma-originated materiality arises; the aggregates are a condition for the physical base; in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, kamma-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. For non-percipient beings, in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, kamma-originated materiality and derived materiality arise. (1)

Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – upādinne khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to state by way of not-object condition: in dependence on the clung-to aggregates, mind-originated materiality arises. (2)

Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – anupādinne khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ. (1)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on an unclung-to state by way of not-object condition: in dependence on the unclung-to aggregates, mind-originated materiality arises; in dependence on one great element…pe… external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated, in dependence on one great element…pe… in dependence on the great elements, derived materiality arises. (1)

Upādinnañca anupādinnañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – upādinne khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on both a clung-to state and an unclung-to state by way of not-object condition: in dependence on the clung-to aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated materiality arises. (1)

Naadhipatipaccayādi

Not-Dominance Condition, etc.

423. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā… naanantarapaccayā… nasamanantarapaccayā… naaññamaññapaccayā… naupanissayapaccayā.

423. A clung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to state not by dominance condition... not by contiguity condition... not by proximity condition... not by reciprocity condition... not by decisive support condition.

Napurejātapaccayādi

Not-Pre-nascence Condition, etc.

424. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe [M 3.0540] upādinnaṃ [V 3.0665] ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā [T 4.0209] kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). (1)

424. A clung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to state not by pre-nascence condition: in the formless realm, in dependence on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise...pe... in dependence on two aggregates...pe...; at the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-originated materiality arise...pe... in dependence on two aggregates...pe... (as far as non-percipient beings). (1)

Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – upādinne khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to state not by pre-nascence condition: in dependence on the clung-to aggregates, mind-originated materiality arises. (2)

Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe anupādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… anupādinne khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). (1)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on an unclung-to state not by pre-nascence condition: in the formless realm, in dependence on one unclung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise...pe... in dependence on two aggregates...pe...; in dependence on the unclung-to aggregates, mind-originated materiality arises; in dependence on one great element...pe... (as far as non-percipient beings). (1)

Upādinnañca anupādinnañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – upādinne khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ… napacchājātapaccayā… naāsevanapaccayā. (1)

An unclung-to state arises in dependence on a clung-to and an unclung-to state not by pre-nascence condition: in dependence on the clung-to aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated materiality arises... not by post-nascence condition... not by repetition condition. (1)

Nakammapaccayo

Not-Kamma Condition

425. Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – anupādinne khandhe paṭicca anupādinnā cetanā… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ. (1)

425. Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises not by kamma condition: dependent on the not-clung-to aggregates, not-clung-to volition arises... external... nutriment-originated... temperature-originated...pe... dependent on the great elements, derived materiality arises. (1)

Navipākapaccayo

Not by result condition

426. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati navipākapaccayā – asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

426. Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises not by result condition: for non-percipient beings, dependent on one great element...pe... dependent on the great elements, kamma-born materiality and derived materiality arise. (1)

Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati navipākapaccayā – anupādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… (yāva utusamuṭṭhānaṃ).

Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises not by result condition: dependent on one not-clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise...pe... dependent on two aggregates...pe... dependent on one great element...pe... (as far as temperature-originated).

Naāhārapaccayo

Not by nutriment condition

427. Upādinnaṃ [T 4.0210] dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati naāhārapaccayā – asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

427. Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises not by nutriment condition: for non-percipient beings, dependent on one great element…pe…. (1)

Anupādinnaṃ [V 3.0666] dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati naāhārapaccayā – bāhiraṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe…. (1)

Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises not by nutriment condition: external… temperature-originated…pe…. (1)

Naindriyapaccayo

Not by faculty condition

428. Upādinnaṃ [M 3.0541] dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati naindriyapaccayā – asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca rūpajīvitindriyaṃ. (1)

428. Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises not by faculty condition: for non-percipient beings, dependent on the great elements, the material life faculty arises. (1)

Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati naindriyapaccayā – bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe…. (1)

Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises not by faculty condition: external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated…pe…. (1)

Najhānapaccayādi

Not by jhāna condition, etc.

429. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – pañcaviññāṇasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… asaññasattānaṃ…pe….

429. Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises not by jhāna condition: dependent on one aggregate associated with the five consciousnesses, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe… for non-percipient beings…pe….

Anupādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe….

Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises not by jhāna condition: external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated…pe….

Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati namaggapaccayā (nahetusadisaṃ, moho natthi)… nasampayuttapaccayā.

Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises not by path condition (not similar to root condition, delusion is absent)... not by association condition.

Navippayuttapaccayādi

Not by dissociation condition, etc.

430. Upādinnaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno dhammo uppajjati navippayuttapaccayā – arūpe upādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe….

430. Dependent on a clung-to phenomenon, a clung-to phenomenon arises not by dissociation condition: in the formless realm, dependent on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe…; for non-percipient beings, dependent on one great element…pe….

Anupādinnaṃ [V 3.0667] dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno dhammo uppajjati navippayuttapaccayā – arūpe anupādinnaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… bāhiraṃ [T 4.0211]… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nonatthipaccayā… novigatapaccayā.

Dependent on a not-clung-to phenomenon, a not-clung-to phenomenon arises not by dissociation condition: in the formless realm, dependent on one not-clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe…; external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated…pe… not by presence condition… not by disappearance condition.

Suddhaṃ

Pure

431. Nahetuyā pañca, naārammaṇe cattāri, naadhipatiyā pañca, naanantare cattāri, nasamanantare cattāri, naaññamaññe cattāri, naupanissaye cattāri, napurejāte cattāri, napacchājāte pañca, naāsevane pañca, nakamme [M 3.0542] ekaṃ, navipāke dve, naāhāre dve, naindriye dve, najhāne dve, namagge pañca, nasampayutte cattāri, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā cattāri, novigate cattāri.

431. Not by root condition, five; not by object condition, four; not by predominance condition, five; not by contiguity condition, four; not by immediate contiguity condition, four; not by mutuality condition, four; not by decisive support condition, four; not by prenascence condition, four; not by postnascence condition, five; not by repetition condition, five; not by kamma condition, one; not by result condition, two; not by nutriment condition, two; not by faculty condition, two; not by jhāna condition, two; not by path condition, five; not by association condition, four; not by dissociation condition, two; not by presence condition, four; not by disappearance condition, four.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

432. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe cattāri, naadhipatiyā pañca…pe… napurejāte cattāri, napacchājāte pañca, naāsevane pañca, nakamme ekaṃ, navipāke ekaṃ…pe… nasampayutte cattāri, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā cattāri, novigate cattāri.

432. By root condition: not by object condition, four; not by predominance condition, five…pe… not by prenascence condition, four; not by postnascence condition, five; not by repetition condition, five; not by kamma condition, one; not by result condition, one…pe… not by association condition, four; not by dissociation condition, two; not by presence condition, four; not by disappearance condition, four.

A clung-to phenomenon arises in dependence on a clung-to phenomenon by way of root condition—one clung-to aggregate conditions three aggregates…pe… two aggregates…pe… At the moment of rebirth-linking, one clung-to aggregate conditions three aggregates and kamma-produced materiality…pe… two aggregates…pe… The aggregates condition the physical base; the physical base conditions the aggregates; one great element…pe… The great elements condition kamma-produced materiality and derived materiality; the physical base conditions the clung-to aggregates. Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

445. Upādinno [M 3.0547] dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – upādinnā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ [V 3.0674] khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe upādinnā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

445. An appropriated phenomenon is a condition for an appropriated phenomenon by way of root condition: appropriated roots are a condition for their associated aggregates by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, appropriated roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of root condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – upādinnā hetū cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

An appropriated phenomenon is a condition for an unappropriated phenomenon by way of root condition: appropriated roots are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. (2)

Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – upādinnā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

An appropriated phenomenon is a condition for an appropriated phenomenon and an unappropriated phenomenon by way of root condition: appropriated roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. (3)

Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – anupādinnā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of root condition: unclung-to roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

446. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ upādinne rūpe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ upādinne khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, upādinnaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… upādinnaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

446. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of object condition: by regarding the eye ...pe... the body, clung-to forms ... smells ... tastes ... tangibles ... the physical base, the clung-to aggregates as impermanent ...pe... displeasure arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, resultant consciousness arises taking that as its object; the clung-to form base is a condition for eye-consciousness ...pe... the clung-to smell base is a condition for nose-consciousness ...pe... the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena [T 4.0218] paccayo – cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ upādinne rūpe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ upādinne khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā upādinnaṃ rūpaṃ passati. Cetopariyañāṇena upādinnacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, upādinnā [M 3.0548] khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of object condition: by regarding the eye ...pe... the body, clung-to forms ... smells ... tastes ... tangibles ... the physical base, the clung-to aggregates as impermanent ...pe... displeasure arises; with the divine eye one sees a clung-to form; with the knowledge of others' minds one knows the mind of one who possesses clung-to consciousness; the clung-to aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the future, and for advertence by way of object condition. (2)

447. Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ [V 3.0675]…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ariyā pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe…pe… anupādinne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe anupādinne khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā anupādinnaṃ rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Cetopariyañāṇena anupādinnacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ…pe… anupādinnā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya [T 4.0219] ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

447. An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of object condition: having given a gift ...pe... observed virtuous behavior ...pe... performed the uposatha observance, one reviews it, savors it, and delights in it; taking that as object, lust ...pe... displeasure arises. Having previously performed good deeds ...pe... attained jhānas ...pe... noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, they review the fruit ...pe... they review Nibbāna ...pe... Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruit, and for advertence by way of object condition. Noble ones review the abandoned defilements ...pe... the suppressed defilements ...pe... previously ...pe... they review unclung-to forms ... sounds ... smells ... tastes ... tangibles, the unclung-to aggregates as impermanent ...pe... and displeasure arises; with the divine eye one sees an unclung-to form; with the divine ear-element one hears a sound. With the knowledge of others' minds one knows the mind of one who possesses unclung-to consciousness; the base of infinite space ...pe... the base of nothingness ...pe... unclung-to aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings, the knowledge of the future, and for advertence by way of object condition. (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – anupādinne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe anupādinne khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, ākāsānañcāyatanakusalaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanavipākassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanakusalaṃ…pe… anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… saddāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of object condition: by regarding unclung-to forms … sounds … smells … tastes … tangibles, unclung-to aggregates as impermanent …pe… displeasure arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, a resultant consciousness arises taking that as its object; the wholesome attainment of the base of infinite space is a condition for the resultant attainment of the base of infinite consciousness …pe… the wholesome attainment of the base of nothingness …pe…; the unclung-to form base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the sound base …pe… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object condition. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

448. Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ upādinne rūpe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ upādinne khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1)

448. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dominance condition. This is object-dominance: having esteemed the eye ...pe... the body, clung-to forms ... smells ... tastes ... tangibles ... the physical base, clung-to aggregates, one savors and delights in them; having esteemed them, lust arises, wrong view arises. (1)

Anupādinno [M 3.0549] dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ [V 3.0676] katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, adhipatipaccayena paccayo; anupādinne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe anupādinne khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati[T 4.0220], diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – anupādinnādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dominance condition: by object-dominance and conascence-dominance. Object-dominance: having given a gift ...pe... observed virtuous behavior ...pe... performed the uposatha observance, one esteems it, reviews it, savors it, and delights in it; having esteemed it, lust arises, wrong view arises. Previously ...pe... having attained jhānas ...pe... noble ones, having emerged from the path, esteem the path and review it; they esteem the fruit ...pe... they esteem Nibbāna and review it. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit by way of dominance condition. Having esteemed unclung-to forms ... sounds ... smells ... tastes ... tangibles, unclung-to aggregates, one savors and delights in them; having esteemed them, lust arises, wrong view arises. Conascence-dominance: an unclung-to dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of dominance condition. (1)

Anantarapaccayo

Immediacy Condition

449. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā upādinnā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ upādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Pañcaviññāṇaṃ vipākamanodhātuyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. Vipākamanodhātu vipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

449. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of immediacy condition: earlier clung-to aggregates are a condition for later clung-to aggregates by way of immediacy condition. The five sense-consciousnesses are a condition for the resultant mind-element by way of immediacy condition. The resultant mind-element is a condition for the resultant mind-consciousness-element by way of immediacy condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāya, vipākamanoviññāṇadhātu kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātuyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of immediacy condition: the life-continuum is a condition for adverting by way of immediacy condition; the resultant mind-consciousness-element is a condition for the functional mind-consciousness-element by way of immediacy condition. (2)

450. Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā anupādinnā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ anupādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo, anulomaṃ gotrabhussa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

450. A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of immediacy condition. Earlier non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for later non-clung-to aggregates by way of immediacy condition; adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage … for fruition attainment by way of immediacy condition. (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – āvajjanā pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ…pe… anupādinnā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo… samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pañca (paṭiccasadisā)… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… dve (paṭiccasadisā)… nissayapaccayena paccayo (paccayavāre [T 4.0221] nissayasadisā) pañca.

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of immediacy condition. Adverting is a condition for the five consciousnesses … non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for emergence by way of immediacy condition … by way of contiguity condition … by way of conascence condition … five (similar to the Dependent Origination section) … by way of mutuality condition … two (similar to the Dependent Origination section) … by way of support condition (similar to support in the Condition Chapter), five.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

451. Upādinno [M 3.0550][V 3.0677] dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… upādinnaṃ utu… bhojanaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utu… bhojanaṃ… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

451. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: immediacy decisive support, natural decisive support … Natural decisive support: bodily pleasure is a condition for bodily pleasure … for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition; bodily pain … clung-to temperature … food is a condition for bodily pleasure … for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition; bodily pleasure … bodily pain … temperature … food … is a condition for bodily pleasure … for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… upādinnaṃ utuṃ… bhojanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utu… bhojanaṃ saddhāya…pe… patthanāya maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, immediacy decisive support, natural decisive support … Natural decisive support: relying on bodily pleasure, one gives a gift … or splits the Sangha; relying on bodily pain … clung-to climate … food, one gives a gift … or produces an attainment; one kills a living being … or splits the Sangha. Bodily pleasure … bodily pain … climate … food is a condition for faith … for aspiration for the path, for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (2)

452. Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… patthanā… utu… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… patthanāya maggassa[T 4.0222], phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

452. A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, immediacy decisive support, natural decisive support … Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one gives a gift, mutters out of conceit, or adopts a wrong view; relying on virtue … aspiration … climate … food … lodging, one gives a gift … or splits the Sangha. Faith … aspiration … climate … food … lodging is a condition for faith … for aspiration for the path, for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, pariyiṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti; sīlaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, pariyiṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ [V 3.0678] kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: immediacy decisive support, natural decisive support … Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one torments and tortures oneself, and one experiences suffering rooted in searching; relying on virtue … aspiration … climate … food … lodging, one torments and tortures oneself, and one experiences suffering rooted in searching. Faith … lodging is a condition for bodily pleasure … for bodily pain by way of decisive support condition. Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for its result by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayo

Prenascence Condition

453. Upādinno [M 3.0551] dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ upādinne rūpe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, upādinnaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… gandhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu upādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

453. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of prenascence condition: object prenascence, base prenascence. Object prenascence: regarding the eye … the body, clung-to forms … odors … tastes … tangibles … the base as impermanent … grief arises; when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, a resultant consciousness arises taking that as its object. The clung-to form base is a condition for eye-consciousness … the odor base … the tangible base for body-consciousness … Base prenascence: the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness … the body base for body-consciousness … the base is a condition for the clung-to aggregates by way of prenascence condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ, upādinne rūpe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā upādinnaṃ rūpaṃ passati. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu [T 4.0223] anupādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of prenascence condition: object prenascence, base prenascence. Object prenascence: regarding the eye … the body, clung-to forms … odors … tastes … tangibles, the base as impermanent … grief arises; with the divine eye one sees a clung-to form. Base prenascence: the base is a condition for the non-clung-to aggregates by way of prenascence condition. (2)

454. Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – anupādinne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā anupādinnaṃ rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. (1)

454. A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of prenascence condition. Object prenascence: regarding non-clung-to forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles as impermanent … grief arises; with the divine eye one sees a non-clung-to form; with the divine ear-element one hears a sound. (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – anupādinne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; kusalākusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… saddāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of prenascence condition. Object prenascence: regarding non-clung-to forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles as impermanent … grief arises; when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, a resultant consciousness arises taking that as its object. The non-clung-to form base is a condition for eye-consciousness … the sound base … the tangible base for body-consciousness by way of prenascence condition. (2)

Upādinno [V 3.0679] ca anupādinno ca dhammā upādinnassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanañca cakkhāyatanañca cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… saddāyatanañca sotāyatanañca…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca kāyāyatanañca kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo; anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanañca vatthu ca…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca vatthu ca upādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A clung-to phenomenon and a non-clung-to phenomenon are conditions for a clung-to phenomenon by prenascence condition: as object-prenascence and as base-prenascence. The non-clung-to form-base and the eye-base are conditions for eye-consciousness… the sound-base and the ear-base… the tangible-base and the body-base are conditions for body-consciousness by prenascence condition; the non-clung-to form-base and the base… the tangible-base and the base are conditions for the clung-to aggregates by prenascence condition. (1)

Upādinno [M 3.0552] ca anupādinno ca dhammā anupādinnassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanañca vatthu ca…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca vatthu ca anupādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena [T 4.0224] paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon and a non-clung-to phenomenon are conditions for a non-clung-to phenomenon by prenascence condition: as object-prenascence and as base-prenascence. The non-clung-to form-base and the clung-to base… the tangible-base and the clung-to base are conditions for the non-clung-to aggregates by prenascence condition. (2)

Pacchājātāsevanapaccayā

Postnascence and Repetition Conditions

455. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā upādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādinnassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

455. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by postnascence condition. Subsequently arisen clung-to aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen clung-to body by postnascence condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā upādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa anupādinnassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by postnascence condition. Subsequently arisen clung-to aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen non-clung-to body by postnascence condition. (2)

Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (3)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for both a clung-to and a non-clung-to phenomenon by postnascence condition (in brief). (3)

Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by postnascence condition (in brief). (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (2)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by postnascence condition (in brief). (2)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (3)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for both a clung-to and a non-clung-to phenomenon by postnascence condition (in brief). (3)

456. Anupādinno [V 3.0680] dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

456. A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by repetition condition… one (in brief).

Kammapaccayo

Kamma-condition

457. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – upādinnā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe upādinnā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

457. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by kamma-condition: clung-to volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by kamma-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, clung-to volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by kamma-condition. (1)

Upādinno [M 3.0553] dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – upādinnā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ [T 4.0225] rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by kamma-condition: clung-to volition is a condition for mind-originated materiality by kamma-condition. (2)

Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – upādinnā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for both a clung-to and a non-clung-to phenomenon by kamma-condition: clung-to volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by kamma-condition. (3)

Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – anupādinnā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by kamma-condition: non-clung-to volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by kamma-condition. (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – anupādinnā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by kamma-condition. At a different moment: non-clung-to volition is a condition for the resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by kamma-condition. (2)

Vipākapaccayo

Result-condition

458. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – upādinno eko khandho (saṃkhittaṃ. Upādinnamūlake tīṇi. ).

458. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by result-condition: one clung-to aggregate (in brief. Three with clung-to as root).

Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko anupādinno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe…. (1)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by result-condition: one non-clung-to resultant aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by result-condition… two aggregates… (1)

Āhārapaccayo

Nutriment-condition

459. Upādinno [V 3.0681] dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – upādinnā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… upādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

459. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by nutriment-condition: clung-to nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates by nutriment-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… the clung-to edible food is a condition for this clung-to body by nutriment-condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – upādinnā āhārā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo; upādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa anupādinnassa [T 4.0226] kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by nutriment-condition: clung-to nutriments are a condition for mind-originated materiality by nutriment-condition; clung-to edible food is a condition for this non-clung-to body by nutriment-condition. (2)

Upādinno [M 3.0554] dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – upādinnā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo; upādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for both a clung-to and a non-clung-to phenomenon by nutriment-condition: clung-to nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by nutriment-condition; clung-to edible food is a condition for this clung-to and non-clung-to body by nutriment-condition. (3)

460. Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – anupādinnā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo; anupādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa anupādinnassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

460. A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by nutriment-condition: non-clung-to nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by nutriment-condition; non-clung-to edible food is a condition for this non-clung-to body by nutriment-condition. (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – anupādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by nutriment-condition: non-clung-to edible food is a condition for this clung-to body by nutriment-condition. (2)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – anupādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for both a clung-to and an unclung-to phenomenon by nutriment condition: unclung-to edible food is a condition for this clung-to and unclung-to body by nutriment condition. (3)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā upādinnassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – upādinno [V 3.0682] ca anupādinno ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

Clung-to and unclung-to phenomena are a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by nutriment condition: clung-to and unclung-to edible food is a condition for this clung-to body by nutriment condition. (1)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā anupādinnassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – upādinno ca anupādinno ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa anupādinnassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo[T 4.0227]. (2)

Clung-to and unclung-to phenomena are a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by nutriment condition: clung-to and unclung-to edible food is a condition for this unclung-to body by nutriment condition. (2)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – upādinno ca anupādinno ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Clung-to and unclung-to phenomena are a condition for both a clung-to and an unclung-to phenomenon by nutriment condition: clung-to and unclung-to edible food is a condition for this clung-to and unclung-to body by nutriment condition. (3)

Indriyapaccayādi

Faculty Condition, etc.

461. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – upādinnā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

461. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of faculty condition: clung-to faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of faculty condition. (1)

Paṭisandhikkhaṇe [M 3.0555] upādinnā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo; cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (2)

At the moment of rebirth-linking, clung-to faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of faculty condition; the eye faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body faculty is a condition for body-consciousness …pe… the material life faculty is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of faculty condition. (2)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa…pe… (upādinnamūlake tīṇi, paṭhamasseva rūpajīvitindriyaṃ, itaresu natthi). (3)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon …pe… (There are three with clung-to as root. In the first, only the material life faculty; in the others, there is none). (3)

Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – anupādinnā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of faculty condition: unclung-to faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of faculty condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo… cattāri, maggapaccayena paccayo… cattāri, sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… dve.

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of jhāna condition… four; by way of path condition… four; by way of association condition… two.

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

462. Upādinno [V 3.0683] dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe [T 4.0228] upādinnā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu upādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – upādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādinnassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

462. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: by conascence, prenascence, and postnascence. By conascence: at the moment of rebirth-linking, clung-to aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of dissociation condition; aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of dissociation condition; the physical base is a condition for the aggregates by way of dissociation condition. By prenascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe… the physical base is a condition for the clung-to aggregates by way of dissociation condition. By postnascence: clung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clung-to body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – upādinnā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu anupādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – upādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa anupādinnassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: by conascence, prenascence, and postnascence. By conascence: clung-to aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition. By prenascence: the physical base is a condition for the unclung-to aggregates by way of dissociation condition. By postnascence: clung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent unclung-to body by way of dissociation condition. (2)

Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – upādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to and an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation condition. By postnascence: clung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clung-to and unclung-to body by way of dissociation condition. (3)

463. Anupādinno [M 3.0556] dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – anupādinnā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – anupādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa anupādinnassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

463. An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: by conascence and postnascence. By conascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition. By postnascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent unclung-to body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa [T 4.0229] dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – anupādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādinnassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation condition. By postnascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clung-to body by way of dissociation condition. (2)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo[V 3.0684]. Pacchājātā – anupādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to and an unclung-to phenomenon by way of dissociation condition. By postnascence: unclung-to aggregates are a condition for this prenascent clung-to and unclung-to body by way of dissociation condition. (3)

Atthipaccayādi

Presence Condition, etc.

464. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ. Yathā nikkhittapadāni vibhajitabbāni paripuṇṇāni). (1)

464. A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. (In brief. As the terms are laid down, they should be analyzed in full.) (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ (saṃkhittaṃ, yathā nikkhittapadāni vitthāretabbāni. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by conascence, prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (In brief. The terms should be expanded as laid down.) (2)

Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ (saṃkhittaṃ, yathā nikkhittapadāni vitthāretabbāni). (3)

A clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to and an unclung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by conascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (In brief. The terms should be expanded as laid down.) (3)

Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ (saṃkhittaṃ, yathā nikkhittapadāni vibhajitabbāni). (1)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by conascence, prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (In brief. The terms should be analyzed as laid down.) (1)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ. Purejātaṃ – anupādinne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati[T 4.0230]; kusalākusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ [M 3.0557] cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Pacchājātā – anupādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādinnassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; anupādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (i) By prenascence: when non-clung-to forms … sounds … smells … tastes … tangibles are regarded as impermanent …pe… grief arises; when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased, resultant consciousness and that which has them as object arise; the non-clung-to form-base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the tangible-base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe…. (ii) By postnascence: non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent clung-to body by way of presence condition. (iii) By nutriment: non-clung-to edible nutriment is a condition for this clung-to body by way of presence condition. (2)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ. Pacchājātā – anupādinnā khandhā purejātassa imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa [V 3.0685] ca kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; anupādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a clung-to and a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by postnascence and nutriment. (i) By postnascence: non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent clung-to and non-clung-to body by way of presence condition. (ii) By nutriment: non-clung-to edible nutriment is a condition for this clung-to and non-clung-to body by way of presence condition. (3)

465. Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā upādinnassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Purejātaṃ – anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanañca cakkhāyatanañca cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… anupādinnaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca kāyāyatanañca kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo; anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanañca vatthu ca…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca vatthu ca upādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – upādinnā khandhā ca anupādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa upādinnassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – anupādinnā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

465. Clung-to and non-clung-to phenomena are a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. (i) By prenascence: the non-clung-to form-base and the clung-to eye-base are a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the non-clung-to tangible-base and the clung-to body-base are a condition for body-consciousness by way of presence condition; the non-clung-to form-base and the clung-to physical base …pe… the non-clung-to tangible-base and the clung-to physical base are a condition for the clung-to aggregates by way of presence condition. (ii) By postnascence: clung-to aggregates and non-clung-to edible nutriment are a condition for this clung-to body by way of presence condition. (iii) By postnascence: non-clung-to aggregates and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence condition. (1)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā anupādinnassa dhammassa atthipaccayena [T 4.0231] paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ. Sahajātā – upādinnā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajāto – anupādinno eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. Purejātaṃ – anupādinnaṃ rūpāyatanañca vatthu ca anupādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca vatthu ca anupādinnānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – upādinnā khandhā ca anupādinno kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa anupādinnassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

Clung-to and non-clung-to phenomena are a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition: by conascence, prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (i) By conascence: clung-to aggregates and the great elements are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of presence condition. One non-clung-to aggregate and the clung-to physical base are a condition for the other three aggregates by way of presence condition …pe… two aggregates and the clung-to physical base are a condition for the other two aggregates …pe…. (ii) By prenascence: the non-clung-to form-base and the clung-to physical base are a condition for non-clung-to aggregates by way of presence condition …pe… the non-clung-to tangible-base and the clung-to physical base are a condition for non-clung-to aggregates by way of presence condition. (iii) By postnascence: clung-to aggregates and non-clung-to edible nutriment are a condition for this non-clung-to body by way of presence condition. (2)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Āhāraṃ – upādinno ca anupādinno ca kabaḷīkāro [M 3.0558] āhāro imassa upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

Clung-to and non-clung-to phenomena are a condition for a clung-to and a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of presence condition. By nutriment: clung-to and non-clung-to edible nutriment is a condition for this clung-to and non-clung-to body by way of presence condition. (3)

Natthipaccayena paccayo… vigatapaccayena paccayo… avigatapaccayena paccayo.

By way of absence condition… by way of disappearance condition… by way of non-disappearance condition.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Positive Application

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Section on Enumeration

Suddhaṃ

Pure

466. Hetuyā [V 3.0686] cattāri, ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā dve, anantare cattāri, samanantare cattāri, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye pañca, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte cha, pacchājāte cha, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme pañca, vipāke cattāri, āhāre nava, indriye cattāri, jhāne cattāri, magge cattāri, sampayutte dve, vippayutte cha, atthiyā nava, natthiyā [T 4.0232] cattāri, vigate cattāri, avigate nava.

466. In relation to cause, four; in relation to object, four; in relation to predominance, two; in relation to contiguity, four; in relation to immediate contiguity, four; in relation to conascence, five; in relation to mutuality, two; in relation to support, five; in relation to decisive support, four; in relation to prenascence, six; in relation to postnascence, six; in relation to repetition, one; in relation to kamma, five; in relation to result, four; in relation to nutriment, nine; in relation to faculty, four; in relation to jhāna, four; in relation to path, four; in relation to association, two; in relation to dissociation, six; in relation to presence, nine; in relation to absence, four; in relation to disappearance, four; in relation to non-disappearance, nine.

Negative Summary

467. Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

467. A clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of object condition... by way of conascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of prenascence condition... by way of postnascence condition... by way of nutriment condition... by way of faculty condition. (1)

Upādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A clung-to state is a condition for a non-clung-to state by way of object condition... by way of conascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of prenascence condition... by way of postnascence condition... by way of nutriment condition. (2)

Upādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A clung-to state is a condition for both a clung-to state and a non-clung-to state by way of conascence condition... by way of postnascence condition... by way of nutriment condition. (3)

468. Anupādinno dhammo anupādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

468. A non-clung-to state is a condition for a non-clung-to state by way of object condition... by way of conascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of postnascence condition... by way of nutriment condition. (1)

Anupādinno [M 3.0559][V 3.0687] dhammo upādinnassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena [T 4.0233] paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of object condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of postnascence condition... by way of kamma condition... by way of nutriment condition. (2)

Anupādinno dhammo upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An unclung-to phenomenon is a condition for both a clung-to phenomenon and an unclung-to phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition... by way of nutriment condition. (3)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā upādinnassa dhammassa purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (1)

A clung-to phenomenon and an unclung-to phenomenon are a condition for a clung-to phenomenon by way of pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. (1)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā anupādinnassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ. (2)

A clung-to phenomenon and an unclung-to phenomenon are a condition for an unclung-to phenomenon by way of co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, and nutriment. (2)

Upādinno ca anupādinno ca dhammā upādinnassa ca anupādinnassa ca dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A clung-to phenomenon and an unclung-to phenomenon are a condition for both a clung-to phenomenon and an unclung-to phenomenon by way of nutriment condition. (3)

1. Upādānaṃ [M 3.0560][V 3.0689] dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – diṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca kāmupādānaṃ, kāmupādānaṃ paṭicca diṭṭhupādānaṃ[T 4.0234], sīlabbatupādānaṃ paṭicca kāmupādānaṃ, kāmupādānaṃ paṭicca sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ paṭicca kāmupādānaṃ, kāmupādānaṃ paṭicca attavādupādānaṃ. (1)

1. Dependent on a clinging phenomenon, a clinging phenomenon arises by way of cause condition: dependent on clinging to views, clinging to sensual pleasures arises; dependent on clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views arises; dependent on clinging to rules and observances, clinging to sensual pleasures arises; dependent on clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to rules and observances arises; dependent on clinging to a doctrine of self, clinging to sensual pleasures arises; dependent on clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to a doctrine of self arises. (1)

Upādānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – upādāne paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on a clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by way of cause condition: dependent on clinging, associated aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. (2)

Upādānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno ca noupādāno ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – diṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca kāmupādānaṃ sampayuttakā ca khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ, kāmupādānaṃ…pe… (sabbaṃ cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). (3)

Dependent on a clinging phenomenon, both a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon arise by way of cause condition: dependent on clinging to views, clinging to sensual pleasures and associated aggregates and mind-originated matter arise; dependent on clinging to sensual pleasures...pe... (the entire wheel should be constructed). (3)

2. Noupādānaṃ [V 3.0690] dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

2. Dependent on a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by way of cause condition: dependent on one non-clinging aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise...pe... two aggregates...pe... At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one non-clinging aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-produced matter arise...pe... two aggregates...pe... dependent on the aggregates, the physical base arises; dependent on the physical base, the aggregates arise; dependent on one great primary element...pe... dependent on the great primary elements, mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise. (1)

Noupādānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noupādāne khandhe paṭicca upādānā. (2)

Dependent on a non-clinging phenomenon, a clinging phenomenon arises by way of cause condition: dependent on non-clinging aggregates, clinging arises. (2)

Noupādānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno ca noupādāno ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā upādānā ca cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā upādānā ca cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (3)

Dependent on a non-clinging phenomenon, both a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon arise by way of cause condition: dependent on one non-clinging aggregate, three aggregates, clinging, and mind-originated matter arise...pe... dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates, clinging, and mind-originated matter arise. (3)

3. Dependent on a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon, a clinging phenomenon arises by way of cause condition: dependent on clinging to views and associated aggregates, clinging to sensual pleasures arises (all wheels should be constructed). (1)

Upādānañca noupādānañca dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca upādānañca paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ, dve khandhe ca…pe… upādānañca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

Upādānañca noupādānañca dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno ca noupādāno ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca diṭṭhupādānañca paṭicca tayo khandhā kāmupādānañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, dve khandhe ca…pe… (cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). (3)

Dependent on a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon, both a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon arise by way of cause condition: dependent on one non-clinging aggregate and clinging to views, three aggregates, clinging to sensual pleasures, and mind-originated matter arise; two aggregates...pe... (the wheel should be constructed). (3)

13. Upādānañca [M 3.0564] noupādānañca dhammaṃ paccayā upādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – diṭṭhupādānañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paccayā kāmupādānaṃ, kāmupādānañca sampayuttake [V 3.0694] ca khandhe paccayā diṭṭhupādānaṃ (cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). Diṭṭhupādānañca vatthuñca paccayā kāmupādānaṃ (cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). (1)

13. Dependent on a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon, a clinging phenomenon arises by way of root condition: dependent on clinging to views and associated aggregates, clinging to sensual pleasures arises; dependent on clinging to sensual pleasures and associated aggregates, clinging to views arises (a cycle is to be made). Dependent on clinging to views and the physical base, clinging to sensual pleasures arises (a cycle is to be made). (1)

Upādānañca noupādānañca dhammaṃ paccayā noupādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca upādānañca paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… (cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). Upādāne ca mahābhūte ca paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, upādānañca vatthuñca paccayā noupādānā khandhā. (2)

Dependent on a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by way of root condition: dependent on one non-clinging aggregate and clinging, three aggregates and mind-originated material form arise … two aggregates … (a cycle is to be made). Dependent on clingings and the great elements, mind-originated material form arises; dependent on clinging and the physical base, non-clinging aggregates arise. (2)

Upādānañca noupādānañca dhammaṃ paccayā upādāno ca noupādāno ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca diṭṭhupādānañca paccayā tayo khandhā kāmupādānaṃ [T 4.0239] cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… (cakkaṃ). Diṭṭhupādānañca vatthuñca paccayā kāmupādānaṃ sampayuttakā ca khandhā…pe… (cakkaṃ). (3)

Dependent on a clinging phenomenon and a non-clinging phenomenon, clinging and non-clinging phenomena arise by way of root condition: dependent on one non-clinging aggregate and clinging to views, three aggregates, clinging to sensual pleasures, and mind-originated material form arise … (a cycle). Dependent on clinging to views and the physical base, clinging to sensual pleasures and associated aggregates arise … (a cycle). (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayā… (ārammaṇe noupādānamūlake pañcāyatanañca vatthuñca kātabbā).

By way of object condition … (in the object condition section, for the triad with a non-clinging root, the five sense-bases and the physical base are to be formulated).

Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava (sabbattha nava), vipāke ekaṃ…pe… avigate nava.

In root condition, nine; in object condition, nine; in dominance condition, nine (in all cases, nine); in result condition, one … in non-disappearance condition, nine.

Anulomaṃ.

Positive

14. Noupādānaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā noupādāno dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā) cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā ahetukā noupādānā khandhā, vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho.

14. Dependent on a non-clinging phenomenon, a non-clinging phenomenon arises by way of not-root condition: dependent on one rootless non-clinging aggregate … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … (as far as non-percipient beings); dependent on the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises … dependent on the body-base, body-consciousness arises; dependent on the physical base, rootless non-clinging aggregates arise; dependent on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness and the physical base, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises.

Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava, naanantare tīṇi, nasamanantare tīṇi…pe… napurejāte nava…pe… nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava (paṭiccasadisaṃ)…pe… novigate tīṇi.

In not-root condition, one; in not-object condition, three; in not-dominance condition, nine; in not-contiguity condition, three; in not-immediate contiguity condition, three … in not-prenascence condition, nine … in not-kamma condition, three; in not-result condition, nine (similar to the Dependence Section) … in not-disappearance condition, three.

Paccanīyaṃ.

Negative

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

15. Upādānaṃ [M 3.0565] dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho upādāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – diṭṭhupādānaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ kāmupādānaṃ, kāmupādānaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhupādānaṃ (cakkaṃ. Evaṃ navapi pañhā kātabbā).

15. A clinging phenomenon arises associated with a clinging phenomenon by way of root condition: clinging to views is associated with clinging to sensual pleasures; clinging to sensual pleasures is associated with clinging to views. (A cycle. Thus, the nine questions are to be formulated.)

Hetuyā [T 4.0240] nava, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava (sabbattha nava), vipāke ekaṃ…pe… vigate nava, avigate nava.

Nine by way of root, nine by way of object, nine by way of predominance (nine in all cases), one by way of result … nine by way of disappearance, nine by way of non-disappearance.

Anulomaṃ.

Positive.

16. Noupādānaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho noupādāno dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ noupādānaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe saṃsaṭṭho vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho.

16. A non-clinging phenomenon arises associated with a non-clinging phenomenon by way of not-root condition: associated with one rootless non-clinging aggregate are three aggregates … two aggregates … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is associated with aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness.

Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naadhipatiyā nava, napurejāte nava, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, navippayutte nava.

One by not-root, nine by not-predominance, nine by not-prenascence, nine by not-postnascence, nine by not-repetition, three by not-kamma, nine by not-result, one by not-jhāna, one by not-path, nine by not-dissociation.

Paccanīyaṃ.

Negative.
